**`DeusData/codebase-memory-mcp`** = tagline *"The fastest and most efficient code intelligence engine for AI coding agents."* A **self-hosted, 100%-local MCP server** that indexes a codebase into a persistent SQLite-backed **knowledge graph** so a coding agent **queries the graph** (read-only openCypher: MATCH/WHERE/aggregates/traversal, NO writes) instead of reading files one-by-one. Headline = **token economy**: README claims **~99.2% reduction** (~412,000 → ~3,400 tokens over 5 queries) + sub-ms queries + Linux-kernel (28M LOC/75K files) full index in ~3 min. **14 MCP tools** (index_repository/list_projects/delete_project/index_status · search_graph/query_graph/get_graph_schema/trace_path/detect_changes/get_architecture/get_code_snippet/search_code · **manage_adr** [persist ADRs into the graph] · **ingest_traces** [validate HTTP_CALLS edges with runtime traces]). Architecture: multi-pass pipeline (structure→definitions→calls→HTTP-linking; IaC Dockerfiles/K8s/Kustomize = first-class nodes) → SQLite graph + **Louvain community detection** → read-only Cypher engine; **Hybrid LSP** type-resolution for 9 langs (no external LSP process) + **158 langs** via vendored tree-sitter; .gitignore/.cbmignore-aware discovery; git-polling watcher; optional 3D viz (localhost:9749). **Team-shared graph artifacts:** git-track `.codebase-memory/graph.db.zst` (zstd SQLite snapshot) → teammates skip re-indexing. **C 88.2% / C++ 10.5%; single static binary, ZERO runtime deps.** **Auto-detects + configures 11 agents** (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Zed, OpenCode, Antigravity, Aider, KiloCode, VS Code, OpenClaw, Kiro) via MCP JSON + optional instruction-injection + non-blocking pre-tool hooks. Install: `curl|bash` (mac/Linux) / PowerShell (Win); also AUR/npm/PyPI/Homebrew/Scoop/Winget/Chocolatey/go-install. **MIT; v0.8.1 (2026-06-12, adds Java+Kotlin Hybrid LSP).** Supply-chain: VirusTotal 0/72 + **SLSA L3** + keyless **Sigstore** cosign + SHA-256 + CodeQL SAST + 100%-local. ## v173 — claude-tap (liaohch3) — 2026-06-20 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 — CORPUS-FIRST wire-level API-traffic interceptor / trace-viewer (protocol-inspection proxy) for coding agents; 1 NEW §C standalone (NO count change)

**`liaohch3/claude-tap`** = *"a local proxy and trace viewer for AI coding agents"* / *"Intercept and inspect Coding Agent API traffic from Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Cursor CLI, OpenCode, Kimi/Kimi Code, Pi, and Hermes in a local trace viewer."* You run your agent CLI **through** claude-tap; it sits in the middle as a **man-in-the-middle proxy**, forwards the traffic unchanged, and **records every request/response pair** — then renders them in a browser trace-viewer for **debugging by evidence**. Captured: *"system prompts, conversation history, tool schemas, tool calls, streaming responses, token usage, and request diffs."* Viewer: **structural diff** between consecutive requests (*"new/removed messages, system prompt diffs, character-level inline highlighting"*) · full-text search across messages/tools/prompts · path filter by endpoint · token-usage breakdown (input/output/cache) · tool-schema inspector · live browser viewer (default) · export to a **self-contained HTML viewer** or a **compact JSON/JSONL bundle** ("Share one portable artifact") · dark/light · iframe embed · i18n (8 langs). Architecture: **dual reverse/forward proxy modes** (reverse = base-URL clients point at the proxy; forward = proxy/CA env vars for clients without base-URL support) → taps **14 client CLIs** (`claude/agy/codex/codexapp/gemini/kimi/kimi-code/opencode/openclaw/pi/hermes/cursor/qoder/codebuddy`); *"SSE and WebSocket streams are forwarded as chunks/messages arrive with low proxy overhead"*; **100% local** (*"Keep traces on your machine: no hosted dashboard is required, and common auth headers are redacted before recording"*). Install `uv tool install claude-tap` / `pip install claude-tap` (Python 3.11+); `claude-tap` defaults to Claude Code w/ live viewer, `--tap-client <name> -- <downstream flags>`. **Python 82.4% / JS 9.7% / HTML 4.5% / CSS 2.6% / Shell 0.8%; MIT; v0.1.120 (2026-06-18); 100+ releases; 9 contributors.** Related: **Phistory** (`WEIFENG2333/phistory`) archives versioned system-prompt snapshots using claude-tap's *"capture-only prompt export"* (a downstream dependent). Author **"liaohch3"** = a bare GitHub handle (NO disclosed individual identity / affiliation / location). **On the goal-#1 substrate core — 3rd consecutive core-substrate ship after v171 devspace + v172 codebase-memory-mcp; a distinct *protocol-inspection* shape (not the v153→v166 usage-monitoring niche).**

Read & search Twitter, Reddit, YouTube, GitHub, Bilibili, XiaoHongShu — one CLI, zero API fees."* / CN *"给你的 AI Agent 一键装上互联网能力."* Design thesis, verbatim: *"能力层（capability layer），不是又一个工具"* = **a capability layer, not just another tool.** Problem named: AI coding agents can code/edit/manage but go blind on the web (can't pull YouTube subtitles, search Twitter without a paid API, read Reddit [403], read Xiaohongshu without login, download B站 [yt-dlp blocked], do semantic search, parse raw HTML, or manage per-platform auth). Agent-Reach fixes all of it as one **capability layer**. **13 platforms, each behind an ordered primary+fallback backend list:** Web (Jina Reader) · YouTube (yt-dlp) · RSS/Atom (feedparser) · Web Search (**Exa via mcporter — free, MCP-based, no API key**) · GitHub (gh CLI) · Twitter/X (twitter-cli cookie → OpenCLI) · B站 (bili-cli → OpenCLI/search-API; *yt-dlp retired — 风控/blocked*) · Reddit (OpenCLI desktop → rdt-cli) · Xiaohongshu (OpenCLI desktop → xiaohongshu-mcp/xhs-cli; browser-login reuse) · LinkedIn (linkedin-scraper-mcp → Jina Reader) · V2EX (native API) · 雪球/Xueqiu (native API; stock data/search/rankings) · 小宇宙 Podcast (Whisper transcription). **Multi-backend routing:** a fallback = *list reordering, not code rewriting*; real-time detection of *functional* backends (not just "command exists"); damaged paths get repair instructions; **auto-switch on failure, zero user intervention** (concrete 2026-06 example: yt-dlp B站 blockade → automatic bili-cli switchover). Durability thesis: *"接入方式会换代，你不用操心"* (access methods will change; you don't manage it). **`agent-reach doctor`** = one-command health check (active channels / current backend per platform / functional-vs-broken / remediation). **Agents:** Claude Code ✓ · OpenClaw ✓ (needs `tools.profile:"coding"`) · Cursor ✓ · Windsurf ✓ · any shell-capable agent (LLM-agnostic). **Security:** local-only creds (`~/.agent-reach/config.yaml`, 600 perms) · no-upload of cookies/tokens · open source · `--safe` (preview, no system mod) · `--dry-run` · clean uninstall (removes config + skill files + MCP settings) · ⚠️ warns to use disposable accounts for cookie platforms (封号风险). **Cost:** completely free, zero mandatory API fees; optional ~$1/mo residential proxy for geo-blocked access (China-mainland → Reddit/Twitter); local machines need none. **Install:** you tell the *agent* a one-liner (*"帮我安装 Agent Reach：<install.md URL>"*) and it autonomously pip-installs + detects env + configures MCP. Integrations: mcporter (MCP Exa, no key) · BrowserAct (forms/multi-session/auto-login) · **Tencent Cloud OpenClaw** partnership (official distribution) · AtomGit mirror (China). Auto-installed deps: twitter-cli/bili-cli/rdt-cli/yt-dlp/feedparser/Node.js/gh/mcporter + the `agent-reach` Python pkg. **Python 95% / Shell 5%; MIT; v1.5.0 (2026-06-11); 7 releases; 290 commits; 35.2k★/2.8k forks (page-stated).** Author **"Panniantong"** (display "Pnant Panniantong") = a DISCLOSED indie builder — bio name **"Neo Reid"**, since 2020, *"Solo founder. ## v175 — PilotDeck (OpenBMB) — 2026-06-20 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 — CORPUS-FIRST open-source self-contained "agent OS" organized around per-project WorkSpace isolation + white-box editable/rollback memory; 1 NEW §C standalone (NO count change); stays on the goal-#1 substrate core (5th consecutive after v171/v172/v173/v174)

**`OpenBMB/PilotDeck`** = *"Task-oriented AI Agent productivity platform — redefining operational boundaries and memory evolution, one WorkSpace at a time"* (tagline, verbatim). An open-source, **self-contained "agent operating system"** — its own agent runtime (NOT a wrapper around another CLI, NOT an orchestrator that drives a fleet of other agents, NOT a pluggable memory add-on), built around three pillars. **Pillar 1 — Traceable White-box Memory:** *"Memory generation, extraction, storage and retrieval are visible end-to-end. When AI mis-remembers, you can pinpoint and fix the offending entry"* — the whole memory lifecycle is visible + editable + **one-click rollback** (vs the corpus's black-box auto-consolidating engines), paired with **Dream Mode** (idle-window consolidation). **Pillar 2 — Smart Routing & Cost Optimization:** built-in **ClawXRouter** auto-detects task difficulty → routes hard work to a flagship model, easy work to a cheap one (project-stated, single-scenario: ~70% cost savings on social-media workloads; a Sonnet-4.6+MiniMax-M2.7 routed mix scored 70.6 @ $3.15 vs Sonnet-4.6 solo 69.1 @ $18.36 — *the project's own unreplicated benchmarks*). **Pillar 3 — Always-on Background Execution:** the agent keeps working after you sign off (discovers candidate tasks, runs long-horizon monitors, lands deliverables as local files) — the "OS" framing (agents = long-lived processes, not one-shot chats). The central organizing primitive is the **per-project WorkSpace**: each project gets its own *isolated* filesystem + memory store + skill set ("WorkSpace-Level Isolation & Accretion … avoiding global context pollution"). Uses model providers underneath (OpenAI / **Anthropic** / DeepSeek / Qwen / Kimi / MiniMax / any OpenAI-compatible). MCP host; consumes ClawHub skills + lifecycle hooks (`PreToolUse`/`UserPromptSubmit`); multi-frontend (Web/CLI/IM); built on OpenBMB's own stack (ClawXRouter / ClawXMemory / **UltraRAG**) + Vite/React/Tailwind/shadcn UI. Three install paths (one-line `curl|bash` auto-installing Node 22 / source / Docker-compose). **TS 70.8% / JS 22.1% / Python 3.8%; AGPL-3.0; PilotDeck Desktop v0.1.0 (2026-06-10); 1 release; open-sourced 2026-05-28; 3.6k★/364 forks (page-stated).** Author **= OpenBMB** (*"Open Lab for Big Model Base … towards AGI"*), an institutional umbrella jointly developed here by **Tsinghua University THUNLP + ModelBest + OpenBMB + AI9Stars** — a serious Chinese academic-industrial AI lab (79 repos incl. ChatDev / MiniCPM / VoxCPM / UltraRAG / AgentVerse / XAgent). **On the goal-#1 substrate core — 5th consecutive core-substrate ship after v171/v172/v173/v174.**

## v178 — SkillOpt (microsoft / Microsoft Research) — 2026-06-22 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) STRONG · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG] — CORPUS-FIRST text-space skill optimizer (training-loop optimization of a frozen agent's natural-language skill document via validation-gated edits)

**`microsoft/SkillOpt`** = *"a text-space optimizer that trains reusable natural-language skills for frozen LLM agents through trajectory-driven edits, validation-gated updates, and deployable best_skill.md artifacts"* (repo description, verbatim); README hook *"Train agent skills like you train neural networks — with epochs, (mini-)batchsize, learning rates, and validation gates — but without touching model weights"* (verbatim). It treats **the skill document as the trainable state of a frozen agent**: a *separate optimizer model* turns scored rollouts into **bounded add / delete / replace** edits on a single skill doc, and **a candidate edit is accepted only when it strictly improves a held-out validation score**. Loop = **rollout → reflect → edit → validate**, with a **textual learning-rate budget** (edit magnitude), a **rejected-edit buffer**, and an **epoch-wise slow / meta update** for stability. Output = a deployable **`best_skill.md`** (≈300–2,000 tok) that runs against the **unchanged** target model with **zero inference-time overhead**. Backed by a paper: *"SkillOpt: Executive Strategy for Self-Evolving Agent Skills,"* Yang et al. (2026), **arXiv 2605.23904** (Microsoft Research publication page + HF papers). **Target models (7):** OpenAI / Azure / **Claude** / Qwen / MiniMax / **GPT-5.5** / Codex (GPT-5.5 = headline benchmark target; Claude = first-class backend). **Harnesses (3):** direct chat / **Codex CLI** / **Claude Code CLI** (+19.1-pt lift reported inside Claude Code). **6 built-in benchmarks**; WebUI dashboard (the HTML 12.2%). **Python 86.6% / HTML 12.2% / Shell 1.2%; MIT; v0.1.0 (Jun 2 2026); 1 release; PyPI `pip install skillopt`; 8.6k★/828 forks (page-stated).** Related MS projects: gbrain / gbrain-evals / darwin-skill. ## v183 — serve-sim (EvanBacon / Evan Bacon) — 2026-06-22 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) STRONG · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG] — CORPUS-FIRST agent-first iOS/Apple-Simulator perception+control layer ("Browser Use, but for the iOS Simulator"); 1 NEW §C standalone (corpus-first for the mobile/simulator surface, N=1); NO count change (46/11)

**Subject:** [`EvanBacon/serve-sim`](https://github.com/EvanBacon/serve-sim) — tagline (package description) **"The `npx serve` of Apple Simulators."**; GitHub About *"Host your simulator for use with Agent tools like Codex, Cursor, or Claude Desktop — locally, over your LAN, or host on a remote mac and tunnel anywhere."* Author **Evan Bacon** (creator of **Expo**, the dominant React-Native framework; `baconbrix@gmail.com` / evanbacon.dev). **Apache-2.0; TypeScript ~73% + native Swift/ObjC(++); npm `serve-sim` v0.1.34 (+ `serve-sim-client` v0.1.15); "No releases published" on GitHub; ~2k★ / 102 forks (page-stated); ~17,087 lines TS + 23 native files + 47 test files; monorepo (2 workspaces). macOS / Apple-Silicon (arm64) ONLY; needs Xcode CLT (`xcrun simctl`); Node ≥20; macOS 14+ for camera injection. NO postinstall scripts; NO telemetry.** Requested from a Vietnamese Facebook post (*"Làm sao để agent 'nhìn thấy' iPhone Simulator?"*). Cloned + source-verified at commit **`a55ce8e`** (default branch `main`, 2026-06-21) by one read-only Explore agent; all corpus claims verified by hand.

**What it is / how it works:** `npx serve-sim` solves a specific gap — *an AI coding agent cannot fix an iOS UI it cannot see.* It spawns a small **Swift helper (`serve-sim-bin`, one per device)** that captures the iOS-Simulator framebuffer via **`xcrun simctl io`** and serves it as **live 60 FPS video** to a browser — **MJPEG** (`/stream.mjpeg`) or hardware **H.264/AVCC** (`/stream.avcc`) — with a **React preview UI on port 3200** (helper on 3100). PERCEPTION surface: the browser-watchable stream (an agent "sees" it via a browser-vision tool) + an **accessibility-tree endpoint `/.sim/ax`** + a **WebKit/CDP DevTools bridge** + **forwarded simulator logs** ("for browser-use MCP tools to read from" — the README's exact phrasing). ACTION surface: a **token-authed WebSocket exec channel** (SHA-256 constant-time match, 10s auth, `{id,command}`→`{id,stdout,stderr,exitCode}`) + CLI subcommands — `gesture` (tap/swipe/drag, pinch-zoom on Option), `button` (hardware + keyboard hotkeys e.g. ⌘⇧H), `type`, `rotate`, `ca-debug`, `memory-warning`, and **`camera`** (inject a synthetic placeholder/image/video/live-webcam feed by swizzling AVFoundation via a `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES` dylib `libSimCameraInjector.dylib`). Drag-and-drop media onto the streamed device. Deploy localhost → LAN → **remote Mac + tunnel** ("use it as if it were local"). Auto-integrates with `npx expo start` (Metro middleware); mountable in any Connect-style server via `simMiddleware({ basePath: "/.sim" })`. **Agent integration = an Agent Skill** (`skills/serve-sim/`) that teaches Claude Code / Codex CLI / Cursor / Gemini CLI / any open-Agent-Skills host to drive the Simulator through the CLI + hand the stream to the host's preview pane; install `bunx add-skill EvanBacon/serve-sim` or `/plugin marketplace add EvanBacon/serve-sim`; Claude Desktop via `.claude/launch.json`. **NOTE: serve-sim is NOT a single MCP server** — it is a streaming server + CLI + Agent Skill that *pairs with* browser-use MCP tools for the vision half.

**The "double deep-dive" into the originals (per the request):** the image's load-bearing reference is **Browser Use** (corpus **v41**, `browser-use/browser-use`, *"Make websites accessible for AI agents"*; MIT; ~89.9k★; gives an agent a real browser it can see + control — the corpus reference point for "agent eyes+hands on the **web**"). ⚠️ **Corpus correction:** the CLAUDE.md shim head miscaches browser-use as "v34" in places; the **authoritative chapter (`_state/03b`) records it as v41** — this wiki uses v41. The general paradigm = **Anthropic computer use** (screenshot → reason → act → verify; not a corpus subject, the conceptual parent). The older simulator tooling serve-sim supersedes: **`xcrun simctl`** (Apple, human/CI — fire-a-command, no live stream/loop; serve-sim *uses* `simctl io` under the hood) and **`facebook/idb`** (Meta, daemon + Python client adding tap/swipe/accessibility, ~5.1k★ MIT, maintenance slowed ~2022, headless). The fast-emerging external peer crop (NOT corpus subjects, honestly flagged so the corpus-first claim stays scoped): **ios-simulator-mcp** (joshuayoes, idb-wrapping MCP, 15 tools, ~2.1k★), **mobile-mcp** (mobile-next, cross-platform iOS+Android), **agent-device** (Callstack, "give AI coding agents a real app feedback loop"), and **agent-simulator** (jasonkneen — MJPEG + accessibility + MCP, the **closest functional twin**, near-simultaneous). Honest read: serve-sim is **not a world-first**; its distinctive *combination* = agent-first design + a human-watchable live browser stream + a bundled Agent Skill (not a separate MCP wrapper) + one-command `npx` UX + camera injection + Expo/Metro middleware + the Expo author's backing. The hard primitives (`simctl io`, AVFoundation) are platform-provided; serve-sim is the agent-surface + streaming/orchestration layer (the camofox-v179 "the hard part is upstream" shape).

**Subject:** [`addyosmani/agent-skills`](https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills) — **"Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents."** A cross-harness **Claude Code plugin / skill marketplace** by **Addy Osmani** (Director at Google Cloud AI; previously led **Chrome Developer Experience 10+ yrs** — created **Lighthouse**, co-led **Core Web Vitals**, ran DevTools; author of *Learning JavaScript Design Patterns* (O'Reilly) + *Image Optimization* (Smashing); creator of Yeoman/TodoMVC/Workbox — all page-stated from `addyosmani.com/bio`). **MIT (© 2025 Addy Osmani); 24 skills (23 lifecycle + 1 meta) + 4 review personas + 8 slash commands (×3 native command-dirs `.claude`/`.gemini`/`commands`) + session hooks + 7 reference checklists; cross-harness Claude Code / Cursor / Gemini CLI / Antigravity / OpenCode / Windsurf / Copilot / Kiro; 63 .md / 16 .toml / 7 .sh / 4 .json; ~27K★ (page-stated, NOT API-verified).** Cloned + source-verified at commit **`aba7c4e`** (default `main`, 2026-06-28). Requested by the operator ("build LLM wiki + double deep dive + pilot methods"). Deep-dive performed by a 10-agent read-only workflow (8 repo readers + 2 upstream researchers; ~332K subagent-tokens); **verdict produced INLINE; all corpus-fact / collision / identity claims verified by hand** (per `feedback_wiki_verify_independently_check_collisions`).

**What it is / how it works:** the executable form of Osmani's **"70% problem"** thesis — AI produces ~70% fast, but the human **30%** (edge cases, security, a11y, integration) is judgment, not velocity → **encode the senior-engineer 30% as agent skills.** Treats the agent as *"an extremely capable junior engineer"* needing scaffolding. Four layers: **(1)** a **meta-router** (`using-agent-skills`) enforcing six non-negotiable behaviors (Surface Assumptions / Manage Confusion / Push Back / Enforce Simplicity / Scope Discipline / Verify-Don't-Assume); **(2)** **8 slash commands** mapped 1:1 to the SDLC (Define→Plan→Build→Verify→Review→Ship: `/spec /plan /build /test /review /code-simplify /ship` + `/webperf`; `/build auto` = plan+implement in one approved pass, still test-driven per task); **(3)** **4 review personas** (code-reviewer / security-auditor / test-engineer / web-performance-auditor) **fanned out in parallel by `/ship`** → one go/no-go (**hard rule: personas never invoke personas**); **(4)** hooks (SessionStart injects the router; sdd-cache; simplify-ignore) + 7 reference checklists. **Skill anatomy:** Overview → When → Process → **Common Rationalizations (excuse→rebuttal table)** → Red Flags → **Verification (evidence gates)**; progressive disclosure (<500-line SKILL.md). The anti-rationalization table is the distinctive mechanic — the immune system against an agent talking itself out of the work. **Bakes in Google SWE canon:** Hyrum's Law (api-design), Beyoncé Rule + test pyramid 80/15/5 (TDD), Chesterton's Fence + Rule-of-500 (simplification), trunk-based dev (git), Shift Left + feature flags (CI/CD), code-as-liability (deprecation), ADRs (docs), RED/USE + symptom-based alerts (observability).

**The "double deep-dive" into the originals (per the request):** the 24 skills each distill real heuristics with exact thresholds (~100-line change cap; CWV LCP≤2.5s/INP≤200ms/CLS≤0.1; perf budget JS<200KB gz; context flooding >5000 lines; review sizing 100/300/1000; rollout error<10%/p95<20% advance, >2×/>50% rollback; bcrypt≥12; OWASP Top 10 **+ OWASP LLM Top 10**). Two distinctive home-grown methodologies: **`source-driven-development`** (DETECT→FETCH→IMPLEMENT→CITE — ground every framework decision in official docs, deep-linked, flag UNVERIFIED; "training data goes stale, confidence is not evidence") and **`doubt-driven-development`** (CLAIM→EXTRACT→DOUBT→RECONCILE→STOP — adversarial fresh-context review that gets ARTIFACT+CONTRACT but **never the CLAIM**, with optional cross-model escalation; 3-cycle bound; "doubt theater" red flag) — the latter is the productized form of the vault's own `feedback_wiki_verify_independently_check_collisions` discipline. **Upstream canon traced** (confidence high/stated): TDD=Kent Beck/XP (1990s); Hyrum's Law=Hyrum Wright, coined in *SWE at Google*; Beyoncé Rule=*SWE at Google*; context-engineering=**Karpathy, 2025** (= the literal substrate of this vault); Core Web Vitals/Lighthouse=Google, **co-created by Osmani himself**. Osmani's **"Loop Engineering"** (*designing the system that prompts the agent instead of you*) = the same philosophy as the vault's Karpathy LLM-Wiki / autopilot pattern.

**THE NOVEL METHOD (DSpark, the "double deep dive"):** paper *"DSpark: Confidence-Scheduled Speculative Decoding with Semi-Autoregressive Generation"* — Xin Cheng + Xingkai Yu + Chenze Shao + Jiashi Li + Yunfan Xiong (equal) + DeepSeek-AI incl. Damai Dai + **Wenfeng Liang**; ¹Peking University ²DeepSeek-AI. **(1) Semi-autoregressive generation** = heavy **parallel backbone** (DFlash — KV-injection of the target model's hidden states, γ base logits in one pass; *code-verified:* `Qwen3DSparkAttention` concatenates `[target_hidden ‖ draft_hidden]` for K/V) + a **lightweight sequential head** adding a prefix-dependent transition bias so each draft position conditions on tokens actually sampled before it — kills the "suffix decay" pure parallel drafters suffer. **Markov head (default):** `B(x_{k-1}) = W1[x_{k-1}]·W2`, low-rank **r=256** (*code-verified:* `VanillaMarkov` = `nn.Embedding(vocab,r)` then `nn.Linear(r,vocab)`); also `GatedMarkovHead` + `RNNHead`. **(2) Confidence-scheduled verification** = a **confidence head** `c_k=σ(wᵀ[h_k;W1[x_{k-1}]])` predicts per-position prefix-survival (supervised on `c*_k = 1 − ½‖p^d−p^t‖₁`), calibrated by **Sequential Temperature Scaling**, feeding a **Hardware-Aware Prefix Scheduler (Algorithm 1)** that greedily spends the target model's verification budget to maximize throughput **Θ = τ·SPS(B)**. **Training:** target FROZEN; draft shares (copies+freezes) target embed+LM-head; 3 position-weighted losses (CE + total-variation distribution-matching + confidence-BCE) at default **α_ce=0.1 / α_tv=0.9 / α_conf=1.0** (in configs). **Offline:** +30.9%/26.7%/30.0% accepted-length over Eagle3 and +16.3%/18.4%/18.3% over DFlash (Qwen3 4B/8B/14B). **Online:** deployed in **DeepSeek-V4** (Flash+Pro previews) — **+60–85%** (V4-Flash) / **+57–78%** (V4-Pro) per-user gen speed vs the prior **MTP-1** baseline *(all DeepSeek's own, unreplicated benchmarks)*.

**Operator-requested** ("build LLM wiki from `palmier-io/palmier-pro` + double deep dive into the original resource for knowledge + pilot to apply knowledge into my working flow, show me many methods"). `palmier-io/palmier-pro` — tagline **"The video editor built for AI."** GPLv3 core + closed generative-AI backend; Swift 98.7%; 9.8k★/708 forks/62 releases (page-stated §37.4); created 2026-04-07; cloned + source-verified at commit **`9a3ae5028...cf043b8d2`** (last commit 2026-07-01, "Add v0.5.2 to appcast"); v0.5.2.

**⚠️ Corrects a wrong first guess this vault's own history primed:** given the MCP angle + the code-context/code-graph precedent (graphify v16 / GitNexus v33 / codegraph v70 / codebase-memory-mcp v172, CONFIRMED Library-vocab #23), the first hypothesis was another coding-agent tool. It is instead a **native macOS video editor** with generative AI (Seedance 2, Kling 3, Nano Banana Pro, GPT-image-2, Veo, Suno) wired directly into the timeline AND its own **MCP server** (`127.0.0.1:19789/mcp`, 51 tools via one `ToolExecutor` dispatcher) so Claude Code, Claude Desktop, Codex, or Cursor can drive real editing directly — read timeline state, add/trim/reorder clips, generate media, apply color, export. A DIFFERENT, older "Palmier" (a GitHub code-review tool, same two-person team, YC S24 2024) is a separate repo, not this subject.

**Author Palmier, Inc.** — San Francisco, incorporated 2024, Y Combinator S24, 2 employees. **2 disclosed founders:** Marcos Rico Peng (CEO, UC Berkeley EECS, ex-LinkedIn infrastructure) + Harrison Tin (CTO, UC Berkeley EECS, ex-Microsoft). ~$500K pre-seed/seed (YC + Immeasurable + Interlace Ventures + Scale Asia Ventures + angels). **Not Anthropic** — verified explicitly; Claude is one of three equally-billed agent integrations (Codex + Cursor get identical MCP-config treatment in the README). Company-self-reported revenue ($440K/2025, per Latka) is **not independently corroborated** — flagged, used for nothing.

**ARCHITECTURE (hand-read, ~325 Swift files, three real subsystems):** **Editor** (`EditorViewModel` + ~40 extension files: ripple/overwrite engines, snapping, keyframes, color grading, captions; frame-accurate AVFoundation compositing + Metal-shader color). **Agent/MCP** (wraps the official `modelcontextprotocol/swift-sdk`; an HTTP MCP server, not stdio, on `127.0.0.1:19789/mcp`; the `ToolExecutor` dispatcher spans 21 extension files implementing the 51 tools; a separate in-app `AgentService` chat panel routes to the Anthropic API or Palmier's own cloud backend and reads a `.agents/skills` folder for skill context). **Generation** (a `GenerationService` abstracting multiple video/image/audio providers with per-generation cost estimation and an async submit→poll→auto-import pattern, no webhooks). **Visual semantic search** via SigLIP 2 (Google, Apache-2.0) converted to Core ML — a genuine, credited upstream ML dependency. Other deps: Sparkle (auto-update), Sentry (error reporting), Clerk (auth), Convex (real-time backend), `swift-transformers`, Lottie. **13.9K test lines / 90+ files**, with the MCP tool layer itself the single best-tested subsystem (`ToolExecutorTests.swift` = 1,885 lines). CI = GitHub Actions on a `macos-26` runner (`swift build`+`swift test`). Distribution = signed + notarized DMG + Sparkle appcast auto-update; **no `curl|bash`, no postinstall, no binary downloads at install** — but **no checksum/signature published for the DMG itself**. Non-sandboxed app (full file/network/camera entitlements) by deliberate design, to support the MCP tool surface.

**License, cleanly disclosed:** GPLv3 covers the editor + MCP server + in-app agent chat; only the generative-AI cloud backend is closed source (the repo's own words: *"The only thing that is closed source is the generative AI processing"*). Single repo, no separate free-tier sibling — the open/closed split is a feature split inside one codebase. Pricing: editor free forever, no login; generation requires a subscription (Pro $29/mo launch / $49 list, Max $69/mo launch / $99 list, credit-metered across video/image/audio/upscale/chat); Enterprise "contact us" with an admittedly-incomplete team/security feature set.

**Honest gaps flagged:** an acknowledged-early product (~3 months old, missing transitions/masking/some graphics per the team + early HN commenters); zero published benchmarks (generation speed, export stability, agent-edit accuracy — the FAQ is candid about this); **Sentry is a shipped runtime dependency with an undocumented telemetry-consent flow** (`UserDefaults` key `io.palmier.pro.telemetry.enabled` defaults `true`, not disclosed in the README — a real doc-vs-code gap); macOS-26-Apple-Silicon-only platform footprint by design; stars/forks page-stated not API-verified (§37.4).

## v193 — TimesFM (google-research / Abhimanyu Das + Weihao Kong + Rajat Sen + Yichen Zhou, Google Research) — 2026-07-04 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 **per operator direction** [(a) FAIL · (b) MODERATE · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG] — Google Research's pretrained decoder-only foundation model for time-series **forecasting** (the corpus's FIRST forecasting-domain FM; the GLM-5 v176 / DeepSpec v186 "off-domain-but-goal-adjacent model" situation, OFF-GOAL CAPTURE equally defensible); **NO MINT** (corpus-knowledge data-point in a new domain; the tempting "corpus-first forecasting FM" mint DECLINED per §28; counts **46/11 UNCHANGED**, §C surface unchanged)

`google-research/timesfm` = *"TimesFM (Time Series Foundation Model) is a pretrained time-series foundation model developed by Google Research for time-series forecasting."* Apply LLM-style pretraining to numbers-over-time: a decoder-only transformer pretrained on ~100B time-points that forecasts an **unseen** univariate series **zero-shot**, competitively with models trained specifically on that series, returning a point forecast + calibrated quantile prediction intervals. The mechanism is **patching** — a window is chopped into fixed 32-point chunks ("tokens") and the model predicts the next chunk. **Apache-2.0 (code + checkpoints); README caveat "This open version is not an officially supported Google product."** Latest **TimesFM 2.5** (200M params, 16k context, calibrated deciles + XReg covariates); PyPI `timesfm 2.0.2` (Jul 2 2026, loads the 2.5 model); Python ≥3.10; torch + flax backends. Repo **~26.5k★/2.6k forks, Python 70.8%** (page-stated §37.4). Paper *"A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting"* arXiv **2310.10688**, ICML 2024. Authors **Das/Kong/Sen/Zhou** (+ Petros Mol, Michael Chertushkin in `pyproject`) — Google Research. **Cloned + source-verified at commit `4a6c5cd`** (default branch `master`, 2026-07-02). **Operator-requested** ("build LLM wiki from this + double deep dive into the original resource for knowledge + pilot to apply into my working flow, show me many methods").

**⚠️ HONEST FRAMING:** TimesFM's *domain* — time-series forecasting — is **OFF Goal #1** ("master Claude + autonomous agents for software development"). It is not Claude, not an agent, not agent infra, not a coding tool. It is the **GLM-5 v176 / DeepSpec v186 situation** (a Google model, goal-*adjacent*, built at operator request). Two genuine on-goal bridges keep it above FAIL: **(1)** the repo deliberately ships a **first-party Claude Code Agent Skill** — `AGENTS.md` "Agent Entry Point" + `timesfm-forecasting/SKILL.md` (author community-contributor **Clayton Young @borealBytes**; a well-built skill with a mandatory preflight system-checker, dataset-fit memory estimation, quantile-based anomaly detection, a backtest recipe; installable via `cp -r timesfm-forecasting/ ~/.claude/skills/`; agentskills.io standard) + a Vertex "**Dockerized endpoint for agentic calling**" → packaged to be **agent-native**, on the exact agent-skills substrate the vault studies. **(2)** the realistic *use* is **Claude Code orchestrating a forecast pipeline** (schema → query → forecast → backtest → gate → PR) = a genuine autonomous-agent-for-software task. **ARCHITECTURE (2.5, source-verified from `src/timesfm/`):** decoder-only transformer, **200M params** (down from 2.0's 500M); **20 layers · model_dims 1280 · 16 heads (head-dim 80)**; **RoPE** + **RMSNorm** (pre-LN, QK-norm, **fused QKV**, per-dim scale); **SiLU/swish** FF; **input patch 32 / output patch 128** (larger output patch → fewer autoregressive steps); output_quantile_len 1024; **context_limit 16,384**; **10 output slices** (deciles q10–q90 + mean; idx 0 = mean, 1 = q10 … 9 = q90); **ReVIN** reversible instance-norm + Welford online running-stats; KV-cache autoregressive decode; scale/shift-equivariance `TimesFM(aX+b)=a·TimesFM(X)+b`. Covariates via `forecast_with_covariates()` → `BatchedInContextXRegLinear` (sklearn LinearRegression + one-hot), modes `"xreg + timesfm"` / `"timesfm + xreg"`; needs `pip install timesfm[xreg]`. **API (source-verified):** `timesfm.TimesFM_2p5_200M_torch.from_pretrained("google/timesfm-2.5-200m-pytorch")` → `.compile(timesfm.ForecastConfig(max_context, max_horizon, normalize_inputs, use_continuous_quantile_head, force_flip_invariance, infer_is_positive, fix_quantile_crossing, per_core_batch_size, return_backcast))` → `.forecast(horizon, inputs=[np arrays])` → `(point (N,H), quantiles (N,H,10))`. **PRETRAINING (paper-stated):** ~100B time-points (predominantly Wikipedia pageviews + Google Trends + synthetic ARMA/seasonal/trend/step), ~80% real / 20% synthetic; 16 TPUv5e ~2 days ~1.5M iters; MSE loss + random patch masking + RIN. **BENCHMARKS (paper-stated):** Monash 18-dataset geomean scaled-MAE **0.6846** vs supervised N-BEATS 0.7005; ETT **~0.36** MAE ≈ supervised PatchTST 0.37 (zero-shot ≈ supervised, 200M vs 175B GPT-3.5-based). **Landscape (leaderboard-stated, churns):** TimesFM 2.5 led GIFT-Eval zero-shot on release (Sept 2025) but is now a strong **#2** — **Chronos-2 (Amazon, Oct 2025) leads** (~79.8% vs ~70.0% win-rate, competitor-paper-stated); Moirai-2.0 (Salesforce) native-multivariate #3; IBM TTM tiny/CPU; Toto (Datadog) observability; TimeGPT (Nixtla) closed/API; Moment (CMU, MIT) multi-task. TimesFM wins long context (16k, longest), param-efficiency (200M), Google Cloud integration; loses multivariate (→Moirai-2.0), pure accuracy (→Chronos-2), edge/CPU (→IBM TTM). **DEPLOYMENT:** PyPI `pip install timesfm[torch|flax|xreg]`; HF checkpoints (custom loader, not plain `AutoModel`; a `-transformers` checkpoint exists); **BigQuery ML `AI.FORECAST` — built-in TimesFM, NO `CREATE MODEL`/no training, all regions** (verified via the redirected Cloud doc — exact arg names not fetchable from the SPA, confirm against the live doc); Google Sheets Connected Sheets + Vertex Model Garden agentic endpoint (README-advertised, not independently verified here); fine-tune via HF Transformers + PEFT **LoRA** (`timesfm-forecasting/examples/finetuning/`). **VERSIONS (README update-log authoritative — two research agents' dates were garbled/conflicting, discarded):** 1.0 (200M/512/uncalibrated/freq-indicator, paper Oct 2023/ICML 2024) → 2.0 (500M/2048/+LOTSA/median-head) → **2.5 launched Sept 15 2025** (200M/16k/calibrated deciles/no-freq/QKV-fused), XReg restored Oct 29 2025, AGENTS.md+SKILL.md Mar 19 2026, LoRA+tests Apr 9 2026, PyPI 2.0.2 Jul 2 2026. ## v194 — fff (dmtrKovalenko / Dmitriy Kovalenko) — 2026-07-04 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) STRONG · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG] — a resident, in-process **fuzzy file+content search LIBRARY** (explicitly NOT a CLI) for humans and AI coding agents, delivered via an **MCP server** + Pi extension + Neovim plugin + C/Node/Bun/Python SDKs; **1 NEW §C standalone at N=1 (CORPUS-FIRST for the local-file-search-SDK-for-agents surface, NOT world-first); counts 46/11 UNCHANGED**

**Operator-requested** ("build LLM wiki from `https://github.com/dmtrKovalenko/fff` + double deep dive into the original resource for knowledge + pilot to apply into my working flow, show me many methods"). `dmtrKovalenko/fff` — tagline **"A file search toolkit for humans and AI agents. Really fast."** README lede: *"Typo-resistant path and content search, frecency-ranked file access, a background watcher, and a lightweight in-memory content index. Way faster than CLIs like ripgrep and fzf in any long-running process that searches more than once."* **MIT ("& open source forever"), © 2025 Dmitriy Kovalenko; Rust 62.5%; ~9.5k★/366 forks (page-stated §37.4); stable `v0.9.6` (2026-06-21), HEAD `0.9.7-nightly.1cd8d31`; cloned + source-verified at commit `1cd8d31` (2026-07-02).** Began as the Neovim plugin `fff.nvim` (a drop-in for telescope/fzf-lua/snacks.picker) → generalized to a library because "plenty of AI harnesses and code editors need the same thing: accurate, fast file search as a library."

**THE THESIS (source-read):** ripgrep/fzf are CLIs — every call forks a process, re-reads `.gitignore`, re-stats dirs, rebuilds state. Fine once from a shell; wasteful when an AI agent runs hundreds of searches/session. fff keeps the index + file cache **resident in one long-lived process** and exposes the same Rust core through thin layers, so every search after the first hits warm memory. Two-sided agent payoff: **latency** (README: 500k-file Chromium → ripgrep spawn 3–9 SECONDS vs fff sub-10 ms; ⚠ author-stated, warm-vs-cold, unpublished methodology) + **tokens** ("fewer grep roundtrips, less wasted context") → lands on the `claude-api-cost-optimization` thread.

**ARCHITECTURE (7-crate Cargo workspace + language packages, source-verified):** `fff-core` (published `fff-search`, the engine) · `fff-grep` (3 content-search modes) · `fff-query-parser` (constraint grammar) · `fff-c` → `libfff_c` stable C ABI (versioned `FffCreateOptions` v2, frozen top-level API) · `fff-mcp` → the `fff-mcp` stdio binary · `fff-nvim` (mlua/luajit) · `fff-python` (PyO3, abi3-py310) · `packages/fff-node`+`fff-bun` (`@ff-labs/fff-node`, `Result<T>`) · `packages/pi-fff` (`@ff-labs/pi-fff`) · 8 prebuilt `fff-bin-*` platform packages. Release profile tuned hard (opt-level 3, lto=fat, codegen-units=1). Two LMDB (heed) DBs: frecency + query-history.

**MCP SURFACE (the load-bearing agent-facing part, hand-read `crates/fff-mcp/src/`):** one resident `FilePicker` for the process lifetime; discovers the git root (`git2::Repository::discover`); background scan + watcher; `FFFMode::Ai`; 900s idle-exit; **startup update-check network call** (`--no-update-check`). **Three tools (code-accurate names): `grep`** (DEFAULT — file contents; auto regex-detect else plain SIMD; 3-stage fallback on 0 hits: drop-first-word → fuzzy → file-path), **`find_files`** (fuzzy file NAMES, frecency-aware, auto-retry shorter query, `→ Read <file>` hints), **`multi_grep`** (OR across literal patterns, SIMD Aho-Corasick). Default `max_results` 20, cursor pagination, output modes content/files_with_matches/count/usage, stdio, no auth. ⚠ **Doc-vs-code nuance (documented faithfully):** the README's MCP section loosely uses the Pi extension's names `ffgrep`/`fffind`/`fff-multi-grep`; the MCP server registers `find_files`/`grep`/`multi_grep` (`#[tool(name=…)]` server.rs:422/538/575). **`MCP_INSTRUCTIONS` system prompt** (main.rs:19–93) = a portable search discipline (bare-identifiers / never gratuitous regex / **stop after 2 greps → READ** / multi_grep for variants / structured constraints) — borrowable verbatim, zero install. **Output shaped for tokens** (output.rs): frecency labels `hot`≥100/`warm`≥50/`frequent`≥10 + `git:<status>`, "(NNKB - use offset to read relevant section)" coaching tag on files ≥20KB, def-body auto-expansion to skip follow-up Reads, bounded caps.

**CORE ALGORITHMS (the "double deep dive" knowledge):** fuzzy path = **neo_frizbee 0.10.3** (SIMD Smith-Waterman, the frizbee/blink.cmp matcher, ~6× fzf) over a 16-byte SIMD-chunk arena w/ cross-corpus chunk dedup + an ~11-component saturating score (base + frecency + git + distance + filename + combo + alignment). Content grep 3 modes: plain (SIMD `memmem`), regex (Rust `regex`, ripgrep's engine, fallback to plain on invalid), fuzzy (Smith-Waterman per line → typo-resistant, `shcema`→`schema`). Multi-pattern OR = SIMD Aho-Corasick. Frecency (Firefox-2008 idea): LMDB, 128 timestamps/file, 30-day purge, exponential decay `ln(2)/10` = 10-day half-life (human) vs **`ln(2)/3` = 3-day half-life in AI mode** + git-touch warm-up. Perf: mimalloc, contiguous arena string storage, mmap content cache (~360 B/file → ~36 MB per 100k files; default budget 30k files), rayon parallel pipeline, platform FS syscalls (getdents64/NTFS API), debounced watcher (notify, 50ms; FSEvents/inotify/ReadDirectoryChangesW) via libgit2-direct. Launched **~2026-07-01/02** ([LangChain blog "Introducing OpenWiki"](https://www.langchain.com/blog/introducing-openwiki-an-open-source-agent-for-repo-documentation) + [official X post](https://x.com/LangChain/status/2072376975545798792) — hand-verified via my own WebSearch).

**THESIS (source-read):** agents write better code when they understand the repo — but you don't want the whole repo in one giant instruction file. OpenWiki runs an autonomous **documentation agent** that inspects the code + git history, writes a navigable Markdown wiki into an `openwiki/` directory, **appends a standardized "OpenWiki" reference section to your top-level `AGENTS.md` and/or `CLAUDE.md`** so your *other* coding agents discover it, and keeps it current via a **daily human-review PR**. It is a **productized, code-scoped version of THIS VAULT'S OWN founding pattern** (Karpathy's LLM-Wiki — an LLM that incrementally maintains a wiki so future queries don't re-derive knowledge), pointed at source code instead of curated knowledge — the closest commercial mirror of what Storm Bear does by hand.

**ARCHITECTURE (hand-read; ~30 files — the intelligence is a system prompt + a dependency, not a big codebase):** built on **LangChain's `deepagents` harness (v1.10.5) + LangGraph** (`package.json` desc: *"A CLI that uses a DeepAgents documentation agent…"*). `createDeepAgent({ model, tools: [], checkpointer: SqliteSaver, backend: LocalShellBackend({virtualMode:true, rootDir:cwd, timeout:120, maxOutputBytes:100_000}), systemPrompt })` — ships **no custom tools**; every capability (filesystem `ls`/`glob`/`grep`/`read_file`/`write_file`/`edit_file`, shell `execute`, `write_todos` planning, `task` read-only subagents) comes from the harness (the corpus's **FIRST DeepAgents-built subject**; DeepAgents = LangChain's "batteries-included agent harness," an "open-source Claude Code alternative that works with any model"). **LangGraph `SqliteSaver` checkpointer** at `~/.openwiki/openwiki.sqlite` (resumable threads keyed by a SHA-256 of the repo path; dir `chmod 0700`, checkpoint `0600`). **5 providers** (`src/constants.ts`): OpenRouter (**default, model = GLM 5.2 via `z-ai/glm-5.2`**, `route:"fallback"` → gpt-5.4-mini → claude-sonnet-5), Anthropic native, OpenAI, Fireworks, Baseten (Claude is one of several; the out-of-box default is NOT Claude — a deliberate cost decision for a high-volume doc-writing task). Git-evidence collection (`status`/`HEAD`/`log <lastHead>..HEAD`/`diff`). Ink terminal UI. Optional LangSmith tracing.

**THE SYSTEM PROMPT IS THE PRODUCT (the "double deep dive" gold):** `createSystemPrompt()` in `src/agent/prompt.ts` = a ~130-line doc-authoring doctrine — grounding (*"Do not invent… Ground every important claim in source, docs, or git evidence you have inspected"* — the vault's own anti-fabrication rule), discovery discipline (targeted grep/glob, never `glob **/*` from root), **read-only subagent discipline** (default 1–2, inspect+summarize only, main agent owns all writes), a temporary `_plan.md`, git-heavy discovery (explain WHY not just WHAT), existing-docs-as-primary-source, security (**never read `.env`/secrets**), section-quality (**no thin pages**, merge stubs), required-structure (`quickstart.md` entrypoint, ≤8 pages on init), and mode-specific behavior (`init`/`update`/`chat`). **`--update` is surgical:** a "source change → docs affected → edit needed → why" impact plan + a **soft diff budget** (fewer than ~5 files changed → update at most 1–2 pages; **no formatting-only edits; may be a no-op**). Borrowable verbatim into a vault `05 Skills/` doc-authoring skill (zero install).

**THE UPDATE LOOP + ANTI-CHURN GUARD (the loop-engineering v189 angle):** `examples/openwiki-update.yml` = a GitHub Action, daily cron (`0 8 * * *`), `permissions: contents: write`, `npm i -g openwiki` → `openwiki --update --print` (secrets `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` + `LANGSMITH_API_KEY`) → opens a **human-review PR** via `peter-evans/create-pull-request` on branch `openwiki/update` (never auto-commits to default — the L1/L2 "propose-don't-act" discipline). **The content-snapshot no-op guard** (`src/agent/utils.ts`): SHA-256 of the whole `openwiki/` tree (excluding `.last-update.json`) before + after; metadata (+ the PR) written **only if the hash changed** → the concrete answer to "how do I run an agent on a daily cron without daily noise" — a reusable pattern for any scheduled agent loop.

**THE LOAD-BEARING IDEA — "read the video, don't watch it" (the perception layer):** README frames it — *"Naive: 30,000 frames × 1,500 tokens = 45M tokens of noise. Video Use: 12KB text + a handful of PNGs. Same idea as browser-use giving an LLM a structured DOM instead of a screenshot — but for video."* Two layers give word-boundary precision from *text*: **Layer 1 (always loaded)** = one ElevenLabs **Scribe** call per source → word-level timestamps + speaker diarization + audio-event tags, packed into a ~12KB `takes_packed.md` (`transcribe.py:65-68` uses model **`scribe_v1`**, `timestamps_granularity=word`, `diarize=true`, `tag_audio_events=true`); **Layer 2 (on demand)** = `timeline_view.py` renders a filmstrip+waveform+word-labels PNG *only at decision points*. **PIPELINE:** Transcribe → Pack → LLM reasons → **EDL** (`edl.json` cut list) → Render (ffmpeg) → **Self-Eval** (runs the visual composite on the RENDERED output at every cut boundary — visual jumps / audio pops / hidden captions — fix + re-render, **max 3 passes**, before you see a preview = a maker/checker loop baked into a skill). **SKILL.md structure** = "12 Hard Rules (correctness, non-negotiable) + everything-else-is-a-worked-example (artistic freedom)" — a clean skill-authoring template. Ships a vendored **`manim-video/` sub-skill** (14 progressive-disclosure reference files; a skill that vendors a second skill).

**PRODUCTION CORRECTNESS IS REAL CODE** (`render.py` 659 LOC, hand-read + workflow-verified): per-segment extract → lossless `-c copy` concat (`:214-283`) · 30ms `afade` at every cut (`:188-189`) · overlays `setpts=PTS-STARTPTS+T/TB` (`:524`) · **subtitles applied LAST** (`:538-543`) · master SRT = output-timeline offsets `word.start − seg_start + seg_offset` (`:360-363`) · grade presets (`warm_cinematic`/`neutral_punch`/`none`) + `--filter` raw, per-segment (`grade.py:38-62`) · **UNDOCUMENTED (does more than the docs say):** default two-pass `loudnorm` to −14 LUFS/−1 dBTP/LRA 11 (`:387-490,643-652`) + HDR→SDR tonemap (PQ/HLG auto-detect, `:95-132`) + portrait auto-detect (`:134-146`). **Doc-vs-code notes (faithfully flagged, none are bugs):** `--preview` is **1080p `medium` CRF 22**, NOT "720p fast" (that's the separate `--draft` flag); subtitle **`MarginV=90`**, not the README's 35 (a 9-line code comment explains it's a mobile-UI safe-zone rule); transcript cache is **filename-stem-keyed only** (re-shoot with the same name → stale transcript silently reused); "1/10 the tokens" is plausible-but-unmeasured-in-code. SKILL.md's own frame — "the values are worked examples, the Hard Rules are law" — holds: all Hard Rules verified.

**COST + PRIVACY (the one real fence):** ElevenLabs Scribe v2 batch ≈ $0.22/hr → **~$0.11 per 30-min take** (free tier has no commercial rights; needs a paid plan ≥ Starter $6/mo; the repo pins `scribe_v1` though the current product is Scribe v2 — a version lag). **PRIVACY — load-bearing:** every source file's audio is uploaded to ElevenLabs, which **retains it ~3 years and trains on it BY DEFAULT** (opt-out is future-only; Zero-Retention is enterprise-only). Fine for your own footage; **a GDPR + consent problem for candidate-interview / third-party-PII footage.** The repo itself is **clean of telemetry** (no PostHog/Sentry; only a `utm_` marketing link to Browser Use Cloud); install is **benign** (no `curl|bash`, no postinstall, no `npx --yes` at install time — animation engines install lazily; `.env` `chmod 600` + `.gitignore`'d, never echoed).

## v199 — page-agent (alibaba/page-agent · Simon `gaomeng1900` / SimonLuvRamen + Alibaba Group Holding) — 2026-07-08 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) STRONG · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG] — an in-page, client-side-JavaScript GUI agent a web-app owner embeds so their END USERS drive the app by natural language; the FIRST corpus subject that lives INSIDE the page (vs external browser-automation drivers); 1 NEW §C standalone at N=1 (CORPUS-FIRST for the surface, NOT world-first); counts 46/11 UNCHANGED.

**Operator-requested** ("build LLM wiki v199 from `github.com/alibaba/page-agent` and double deep dive into the original resource for knowledge. Then i want to pilot to apply knowledge into my working flow, show me many method for my apply"). **MIT © 2026 SimonLuvRamen + Alibaba Group Holding Limited; TypeScript 82.6% / JS 11.8% / CSS 4.4%; v1.11.0 (2026-07-03); 34 releases; first commit 2025-09-23; ~25k★/2.1k forks page-stated §37.4; Trendshift badge + HN (item 47264138) + MarkTechPost/Medium coverage; homepage alibaba.github.io/page-agent; source-verified at commit `35ff6d4`.** Author **Simon** (GitHub `gaomeng1900`, X `@simonluvramen`, © "SimonLuvRamen") — an Alibaba engineer; official `alibaba/` org open-source project. *(Fuller identity unverified — the identity research agent returned empty; not relied upon.)*

**THE ONE-SENTENCE THESIS:** every other corpus web-agent drives a browser FROM THE OUTSIDE for a developer/coding-agent (browser-use v41 / Skyvern v24 / crawl4ai v29 — external Python/Playwright→CDP). page-agent inverts it: a **~50–100KB client-side JS library a web-app owner drops into their OWN site** (`<script>` or `npm install`) that gives **that site's END USERS** a natural-language agent driving the app's **OWN real DOM** — no extension, no Python, no headless browser, no backend, no screenshots. README: *"`PageAgent` is designed for **client-side web enhancement**, not server-side automation."* "browser-use, but living inside the page."

**CORPUS-RECURSIVE PROVENANCE (load-bearing, source-verified):** README NOTICE — *"This project builds upon the excellent work of `browser-use`. … DOM processing components and prompt are derived from browser-use. Copyright (c) 2024 Gregor Zunic."* + `packages/core/src/tools/index.ts` header `@note Adapted from browser-use` + the `scroll` tool `@note Reference from browser-use`. **browser-use = corpus subject v41** (and the org that built v198 video-use).

**ARCHITECTURE (8-package source-first monorepo, hand-read + workflow-verified):** `@page-agent/core` (headless `PageAgentCore` ReAct loop, ~1.9K LOC) · `page-agent` (thin entry + UI Panel + demo IIFE) · `@page-agent/llms` (OpenAI-compatible client, ~1.5K) · `@page-agent/page-controller` (DOM extraction+dehydration+actions+SimulatorMask, NO LLM dep, ~2.2K) · `@page-agent/ui` (Panel+i18n) · `@page-agent/mcp` (MCP server, Beta) · extension (WXT+React multi-tab, ~5K) · website (private). Load-bearing decoupling: page-controller has no LLM dependency; llms has no page dependency; the same core runs in-page AND in the extension's `MultiPageAgent`.

**THE ReAct LOOP (`PageAgentCore.execute`):** observe (`getBrowserState()` refreshes DOM) → think (LLM: reflection {evaluation_previous_goal/memory/next_goal} + one action) → act (execute tool by element index) → loop; maxSteps 40, stepDelay 0.4s. **ONE "MacroTool" call per step** — all tools merged into a single forced `AgentOutput` tool (`toolChoiceName:'AgentOutput'`) carrying reflection + a union-of-all-tool-schemas `action`. **Two deliberately separated streams:** persistent History events (fed into LLM context as `<agent_history>`) vs transient Activity events (UI-only, NOT in context — errors kept out of the model's reasoning). System observations injected pre-step (URL-change / accumulated-wait / 5-and-2-steps-remaining). Human-in-loop first-class: `ask_user` tool + `user_takeover` history event. Lifecycle hooks (all `@experimental`); one AbortController threaded to LLM fetch + every tool + callbacks. **System prompt** (browser-use-derived) teaches `[index]<type>text</type>` / `\t`=child / `*[index]`=new, and is honest: *"It is ok to fail the task… Trying too hard can be harmful… User would rather you complete the task with a fail"*; *"Never assume an action succeeded"*; single-page-app constraint (*"Do not jump out of current page"*).

**THE DOM ENGINE — "dehydration" (the double-deep-dive core, source-verified `page-controller/src/`):** `updateTree()`→`getFlatTree()`→`processElementsV2()` walks the live DOM, running a multi-signal `isInteractiveElement()` (blacklist/whitelist → CSS cursor → tag whitelist a/button/input/select/textarea/details/summary/label/option/li → ARIA role → `getEventListeners()` w/ on*-fallback → contenteditable → scrollable `scrollHeight−clientHeight≥4px`). A global counter assigns each interactive element a **stable numeric index** (the `selectorMap` index→HTMLElement; NO CSS selectors/XPath reach the LLM). `flatTreeToString()` dehydrates to `[index]<tag>text</tag>` + `\t` parentage + `*[index]` new-since-last-step (WeakMap-tracked) + `data-scrollable='left=…,top=…'`. Actions by index: **click** = full W3C pointer sequence (pointerover→…→click) w/ pass-through hit-testing; **input_text** = synthetic events (input/textarea) or execCommand (contenteditable); scroll/select. **SimulatorMask** = full-screen overlay + animated AI cursor (20%/frame easing, rAF), coordinated by `window` events. Caveats: no cross-origin iframes; `getEventListeners()` context-dependent; 4px threshold arbitrary; caches can stale. **⚠️ text-DOM-not-screenshots is NOT a page-agent innovation** — browser-use/Stagehand/Playwright-MCP have all converged on it; page-agent inherits it from browser-use, its OWN novelty is the in-page delivery.

**THE LLM CLIENT (`@page-agent/llms`, provider-quirk-hardened):** BYOK OpenAI-compatible (`LLMConfig{baseURL,model,apiKey,maxRetries,transformRequestBody,disableNamedToolChoice,customFetch}`); works with OpenAI/**Claude**/Qwen(dashscope)/DeepSeek/Gemini/GLM/MiniMax/OpenRouter/**Ollama**. tool_choice `'required'` or forced-by-name; `disableNamedToolChoice` for models that reject it (DeepSeek). `modelPatch()`+`normalizeModelName()` per-provider tweaks. Retries: default 2 (3 attempts), **fixed 100ms backoff** (not exponential — caveat); typed InvokeError retryable/non-retryable taxonomy; AbortError never retried. Usage tracks promptTokens/completionTokens/cachedTokens/reasoningTokens. **`autoFixer`/`normalizeResponse`** repairs ≥5 malformed-response classes (JSON-in-content, action-name-as-tool, double-stringified args, nested-function, missing-action→wait) + `validateAction()` coerces `{click:2}→{click:{index:2}}` — the glue that makes weak/local models usable. **Claude is first-class + tested** (hand-read CHANGELOG, overriding the docs-SPA 404): v1.9.0 "Claude Opus 4.8 support"; v1.11.0 per-model patching "for GPT, **Claude**, Qwen, Gemini, DeepSeek."

**MULTI-PAGE (extension) + MCP:** WXT+React extension = `MultiPageAgent`+`TabsController`+`RemotePageController`; stateless service worker + `chrome.storage.local` + 1s heartbeat; `syncTabs()` in onBeforeStep; 3 tab tools (open_new_tab/switch_to_tab/close_tab); token-auth bridge (page localStorage token must match extension) → `window.PAGE_AGENT_EXT.execute/stop`. **MCP server (`@page-agent/mcp`, Beta)** = a SEPARATE Node binary (not in the extension) running an HTTP+WebSocket `HubBridge`; 3 MCP tools **execute_task/get_status/stop_task**; a `window.confirm()` user-approval gate; single-task-at-a-time. ⚠️ **DIRECTION-INVERTED:** this MCP server EXPOSES control of the in-page agent TO external clients (opposite of the canonical B1-MCP one-server-augments-many-agents) → adjacency, NOT a clean B1-MCP instance; audit flag.

**CONFIG surface (source-verified `AgentConfig`):** language(en-US/zh-CN) · maxSteps 40 · stepDelay 0.4 · customTools(add/delete) · instructions.system + **getPageInstructions(url)** per-route · **experimentalLlmsTxt** (fetch site llms.txt) · **experimentalScriptExecutionTool** (execute_javascript, OFF by default) · **transformPageContent** (redaction hook) · customSystemPrompt(@experimental) · onAskUser · lifecycle hooks · enableMask. The three "safe-to-embed" levers = execute_javascript-off-by-default + transformPageContent redaction + getPageInstructions per-route.

**SECURITY/PRIVACY (source-verified — the fence):** core posture BENIGN — *"client-side only, BYOK, no backend… does not collect/transmit data on its own"* (no telemetry, MIT, auditable, execute_javascript off-by-default, extension config chrome.storage.local no-sync-no-analytics, proper SECURITY.md). **Four fence points:** (1) **the free demo/testing LLM proxy egresses page HTML to Alibaba Cloud CHINA** (Function Compute+BaiLian Qwen; "tech-eval only, no PII, EU/EEA do-not-use") → use BYOK for anything real; (2) **HTML dehydration does NOT guarantee PII removal** (candidate data → use transformPageContent + no-training provider); (3) the **`.env` AK-inlined-in-IIFE footgun** (never ship a real key in a built bundle); (4) execute_javascript runs arbitrary in-page JS if enabled. **Anti-AI-slop stance** (nuanced, CONTRIBUTING.md): *"Vibe coding NOT allowed for the core lib or the extension; RECOMMENDED for demo/website/UI/tests"* + no unmotivated bot PRs.

## v200 career-ops — COMPLETE 2026-07-09 — THE 200th LLM-WIKI SHIP

**`santifer/career-ops`** = *"Open-source AI job search: scan job portals, score listings A-F, tailor your CV, track applications — runs locally in your AI coding CLI."* **GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) STRONG · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG]; 1 NEW §C standalone at N=1 (CORPUS-FIRST for the surface, NOT world-first); counts 46/11 UNCHANGED; operator-requested ("build LLM wiki v200 from github.com/santifer/career-ops + double deep dive + pilot to apply into my working flow, show me many method for my apply").** MIT © 2026 Santiago Fernández de Valderrama (+ a `TRADEMARK.md`); JS 70.4% / TS 20.5% / Go 6.6%; v1.18.0; 21 releases; ~635 commits; 15 README translations; ~59.2k★/11.6k forks page-stated §37.4; author **Santiago Fernández de Valderrama** (`@santifer`, hi@santifer.io, santifer.io) — **Head of Applied AI at Zinkee** (Spain), ex-founder Santifer iRepair (2009–2025, exited), Seville; **NOT Anthropic**; source-verified at commit `e9bacc48` (2026-07-08).

**THESIS (README, verbatim):** *"Companies use AI to filter candidates. I just gave candidates AI to choose companies."* = **the domain-exact INVERSE of hireui** (the operator's Goal-#2 recruitment SaaS scores candidates FOR employers; career-ops scores employers + beats their ATS filters FOR candidates — same domain, opposite actor). It turns any AI coding CLI (Claude-Code-first) into a candidate-side job-search command center: paste a URL/JD → the agent classifies the role, scores it 1–5 vs your `cv.md`, generates an ATS-safe tailored PDF, checks the posting isn't a ghost job, files it into a tracked pipeline — **local-only, and it never submits anything for you.**

**ARCHITECTURE (documented from the CODE, not the marketing):** the evaluation "brain" is **Markdown prompt files** (`modes/_shared.md` scoring core + `modes/oferta.md` A–G flow) executed by whichever AI coding CLI you point at the repo — **the coding agent IS the runtime, no orchestrator** (`ARCHITECTURE.md`: *"The logic lives in Markdown prompt files under modes/ … No single model is hardcoded"*). The mechanics = ~50 single-job, mostly zero-LLM Node scripts. **Five layers:** (1) **DISCOVER** — `scan.mjs` + **~53 provider modules** (hand-counted; README's "21" is an undercount), *"Zero Claude API tokens — pure HTTP + JSON"* to public no-auth ATS APIs (Greenhouse/Ashby/Lever/BambooHR/Breezy/Personio/Phenom + board aggregators); `--verify` runs a Playwright liveness pass to drop expired postings; a `_trust-validator` + `fingerprint-core` catch bad feeds + reposts; auth-gated sources deliberately out of core. (2) **SCORE** — `_shared.md` (hand-read): a **1–5 global** score = by default the **average of the block scores** (`oferta.md:404`, user-overridable via `_custom.md`), over **5 weighted dimensions** (CV-match/North-Star/Comp/Cultural/Red-flags); **7 report blocks A–G**; **6 archetypes** (LLMOps/Agentic/Tech-PM/Solutions-Architect/Forward-Deployed/Transformation, customizable); **Block G posting-legitimacy** (3-tier scam/ghost-job detection, 8 signals, MANDATORY ethical framing "present signals never accusations," **does NOT affect the 1–5 score**); a 10-type comp-reliability taxonomy. Score interpretation: 4.5+ apply-now / 4.0–4.4 worth / 3.5–3.9 only-with-reason / **<3.5 recommend-against** (⚠️ README markets "<4.0"). (3) **GENERATE** — two PDF pipelines (Playwright HTML→PDF default + a LaTeX path), **defensive-not-injective ATS optimization** (ligature-disable + Unicode→ASCII normalize + a system-sans stack instead of the bundled variable woff2 that inject "SUM M ARY" spaces; **keyword injection is NOT in the render layer**), a two-tier **Voice-DNA** anti-slop guardrail (HARD banned-vocab + the negative-parallelism "FATAL" rule), a 4-prompt cover-letter draft→approve→A4 flow. **Subject.** `StarTrail-org/PixelRAG` — *"Official codebase for **PIXELRAG: Web Screenshots Beat Text for Retrieval-Augmented Generation**"* (arXiv **2606.28344**, cs.IR, Jun 2026). Tagline (verbatim): *"Search any document by how it looks, not just the text it contains."* / *"The end of web parsing. The beginning of scalable pixel-native search."* Landing page `pixelrag.ai`. Traditional RAG parses documents into text chunks, discarding visual structure (tables/charts/layout/diagrams); PixelRAG renders documents to **screenshot tiles**, retrieves over the **images**, and feeds retrieved screenshots **directly as pixels to a reader VLM — no text conversion**. **Operator-requested** ("build LLM wiki for `https://github.com/StarTrail-org/PixelRAG`").

**Meta (all page-stated §37.4 — GitHub API mocked → NOT #52).** Apache-2.0; Python 80.8% / Markdown 8.7% / TypeScript 7.2% / Shell 1.8% / JS 0.7% / CSS 0.5%; ~6.7k★/560 forks; 4 releases (latest **v0.4.0**, Jul 2026). ⚠️ **Typosquat/fork forks exist** — `Puneetb/pixelrag`, `sp00ler/pixelrag`, `seco/pixelrag` all carry the same "The end of web parsing" tagline → **install from `StarTrail-org` only**.

**Identity (hand-verified).** Authors (equal contribution): **Yichuan Wang · Zhifei Li · Zirui Wang · Paul Teiletche · Lesheng Jin**; advisors (equal): **Matei Zaharia** (Databricks co-founder / Apache Spark creator) · **Joseph E. Gonzalez** · **Sewon Min**. Affiliations: **UC Berkeley (SkyLab / BAIR / Berkeley NLP) + Princeton + EPFL + Databricks. NOT Anthropic.** §41: no notability (Zaharia) / heritage / locale rescue → clean (a) FAIL. First `StarTrail-org` / Berkeley-SkyLab / Zaharia-Databricks author cluster in the corpus (#19 19a).

**Architecture — two stages, entirely in pixel space.** ① **Render (`pixelshot`)** — web pages / PDFs / images → screenshot tiles via headless Chromium (Playwright / CDP; poppler for PDFs). ② **Retrieve** — a VLM embedding model (`Qwen/Qwen3-VL-Embedding-2B`, **LoRA-fine-tuned on screenshot data**; adapter `Chrisyichuan/wiki-screenshot-embedding-lora`) embeds tiles; search over the images themselves; retrieved screenshots fed **directly as pixels** to a reader VLM. **Backends:** FAISS (default, local) / Qdrant (scalable — quantization, disk-backed, payload filtering, shared collection). **Serving:** FastAPI (`pixelrag serve`). **CLI:** `pixelshot` (render) → `pixelrag chunk/embed/build-index` → `pixelrag index build` (full, config-driven `pixelrag.yaml`) → `pixelrag serve`. **Staged install:** `pip install pixelrag[embed|index|serve|qdrant]`. **Hosted API** `https://api.pixelrag.ai` over **8.28M Wikipedia pages / ~30M screenshot tiles** (README/paper), no key, text + image queries. **Training:** separate `uv` project (`train/`), pinned `torch==2.9.1+cu129` / `transformers==4.57.1`, contrastive with LLM-augmented query gen + hard-negative mining (dataset `Chrisyichuan/screenshot-training-natural-filtered-v2`).

**THE ON-GOAL BRIDGE — the `pixelbrowse` Claude Code plugin.** Instead of raw HTML, Claude **screenshots a page and reads the image** ("charts, diagrams, tables, and layout the way a person does"). `uv tool install pixelrag` → `claude plugin marketplace add StarTrail-org/PixelRAG` → `claude plugin install pixelbrowse@pixelrag-plugins`; `/screenshot https://…`. **No backend** — calls `pixelshot` locally. Free, install-today; the one immediately-actionable piece.

**Benchmarks (paper-stated — authors' own, NOT reproduced).** Outperforms both no-retrieval and text-based RAG; wins on **text-centric** tasks (NQ, SimpleQA) too; gains on multimodal open-domain QA, noisy news corpora, agentic benchmarks; **up to +18.1%** over text baselines. It bridges OpenAI-compatible clients with web AIs (Grok, Gemini, ChatGPT) via session multiplexing."* Operator-requested (link arrived via Facebook; `fbclid` stripped). **THE MECHANISM, plainly:** you log into your OWN free Grok/Gemini/ChatGPT accounts inside an anti-detect browser; CoreOfPotato keeps those tabs alive, drives them by **scraping the chat UI's DOM**, and re-exposes them to local tools as an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/chat/completions` endpoint — **a free-tier harvester with an API face** (there is no API key to any model anywhere in the system). MIT; Python; **~16★/3 forks/7 commits total** page-stated §37.4 → **NOT #52**; v1.0.1; first commit **2026-06-06**, last **2026-06-09** → **stale ~2 months**. **ARCHITECTURE (source-verified):** three tiers client → aiohttp → Playwright/Chromium; `core/server.py` registers `app.router.add_post("/v1/chat/completions", self.api_chat_completions)` with **genuine SSE streaming** (`submit_job_streaming()` → `text/event-stream`); ⚠️ `core/routes.py` holds only the `/api/*` admin surface — I checked `server.py` before calling that a discrepancy, and it is NOT one (the v193 false-drift lesson). **"NaModu" key** = 6 chars (2-char registered caller prefix + 4-char module tag, e.g. `OCtest`), read from body `user` / `Bearer` / `x-user`, validated by `validate_user()`, then reused as the routing key `nav_key = f"{caller}{modu}_{platform}"` → the same caller always lands in the same browser tab = **conversation continuity without server-side conversation state** (the one genuinely clever idea). Three URL-cache strategies (fixed / time-based 30 min / usage-based 10 uses, the shipped default). `core/drivers/` = `base.py` + `chatgpt.py` + `gemini.py` + `grok.py` — **NO `claude.py`**; `GrokDriver(BaseDriver)` uses a union of fallback selectors, `type_human_like()`, `asyncio.sleep(random.uniform(0.5, 1.2))` before submit, `dismiss_cookie_consent()`, and detects completion by polling every 0.25s until `stable_count >= 8` (**"the answer is done when the text stops changing for ~2s"** — brittle by construction, and the cheapest possible argument for paying for a real API contract). Stealth = point Playwright at CloakBrowser's patched Chromium (`setup_cloak.py` → `ensure_binary()` → writes `browser.executable_path`; this also resolves the apparent absence of a stealth key in `config.example.json` — `executable_path` IS the cloak hook, resolved by hand, NOT reported as drift). Headless is a toggle the docs advise against (*"headless mode triggers bot protections on Grok and ChatGPT"*); headed is the default. Ops: a `/hub` dashboard (slots/keys/logs), `/api/*` admin, log export/retention, a load-test harness, real CI (`ci.yml`: Python **3.9** only, `ruff check .`, `playwright install --with-deps chromium`, `pytest`). ⚠️ **NOT source-cloned** (hand-fetched: repo page + raw README/CHANGELOG×2/DISCLAIMER/EASY_START/requirements.txt/setup_cloak.py/config.example.json + `core/` + `core/drivers/` trees + `server.py`/`routes.py`/`grok.py`/`ci.yml` + the commit list + the author profile). **(a) FAIL** — `hwahao` is a disclosed individual (bio + **Ha Noi, Viet Nam**), not Anthropic (§41 — no name/heritage/locale/notability inference); **v232 gemini-web2api** (2026-08-17): **T2 Service / Self-Hosted LLM-Access Gateway — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) MODERATE keys the tier ⚠️ STRONG + OFF-GOAL both reviewable · (c) MODERATE ⚠️ STRONG-reviewable · (d) STRONG]; 1 NEW §C standalone at N=2 (NOT corpus-first, NOT world-first); counts 46/11 UNCHANGED; §C live standalones 47 → 48; surface ≈54 → ≈55.** `Sophomoresty/gemini-web2api` — repo About verbatim: *"Convert Google Gemini web into OpenAI-compatible API. **Zero auth**, cross-platform, single file."* (The README Features subtitle reads *"**Zero cost**"* — both strings are real, in different places, and both accurate to different facets; checked against the v231 drift tell and **resolved CLEAN**.) Operator-requested (link arrived via Facebook; `fbclid` stripped).

**WHAT IT IS, PLAINLY:** it takes the **private RPC endpoint that Google's own Gemini website calls** and re-exposes it on your machine as an OpenAI-compatible API. Point any OpenAI client — including a coding agent — at `http://localhost:8081/v1` and it answers from the consumer Gemini web product. **No API key to Google exists anywhere in it.** MIT; Python; `requires-python >=3.8`; **ZERO required dependencies** (optional `streaming` extra = `httpx>=0.25`) → the core runs on the standard library; **v1.1.0** in `pyproject.toml` but **0 releases published**; ~2.7k★ / ~607–627 forks / 59 commits / 6 contributors page-stated §37.4 → **NOT #52**; Trendshift **#42981** ("#12 Python Repo of the Day" 2026-05-31; ⚠️ "#7 **JavaScript** Repo of the Day" 2026-08-01 despite Python primary — a categorisation oddity, recorded, velocity unestablishable). ⚠️ **NOT source-cloned** (hand-fetched file-by-file: repo page + `README.md` + `README_CN.md` + `pyproject.toml` + `config.example.json` + `gemini_web2api/gemini.py` + `gemini_web2api/server.py` + `gemini_web2api.py` + package/extension/cloudflare/workflow trees + releases + Trendshift + author profile; the v200→v231 self-throttle).

**AUTHOR: Sophomoresty (靝悠Sol)** — a disclosed individual, **NOT Anthropic** (§41; #19 19a first `Sophomoresty` author). Verbatim bio: *"SCU undergrad, based in Shanghai FDU. Started in Mechanical Engineering 🔧, detoured into graphic design & video editing 🎨, had an existential crisis 💀, pivoted to CS, and somehow ended up doing AI-powered reverse engineering 🤷. Jack of all trades, master of none."* ⚠️ **Two confabulations caught + discarded:** (i) an earlier search characterised the author as a *"reverse engineer and penetration tester… offensive security tool developer"* — **unsupported by the verbatim bio**; (ii) a profile summariser read "SCU" as **Santa Clara University** — in context (Shanghai, **FDU = Fudan**, Chinese-language repos + README_CN, linux.do community credits) it is **Sichuan University (四川大学)**. Only the verbatim bio is relied on. **Portfolio archetype (a genuine #19 19a data-point):** 59 public repos / 157 followers, and the notable ones form one coherent theme — *circumventing an access gate to reach otherwise paid or restricted content*: `gemini-web2api` (2.7k★, this), `mediago` (233★, downloads video from 90+ Chinese educational platforms), `bpc-fetch` (196★, paywall bypass across **936 sites**), **`gemini-search-mcp` (172★, *"Free MCP server for web search via Google AI Mode"* — the same move applied to search, delivered as MCP; an adjacency only, **v232 itself ships no MCP server**)**, `qmdec` (75★, QQ Music DRM decryptor), `typora-theme-Jinxiu` (58★).

**MECHANISM (source-verified — the decisive contrast with v231):** **pure HTTP protocol reverse-engineering; there is no browser anywhere in it.** From `gemini_web2api/gemini.py` (~350 lines, utility-module design, no classes): (1) it calls Gemini's own internal `batchexecute`-family RPC — `https://gemini.google.com{account_prefix}/_/BardChatUi/data/assistant.lamda.BardFrontendService/StreamGenerate` with `bl`/`hl`/`_reqid`/`rt=c`, `account_prefix` = `/u/{auth_user}` for non-default accounts — the *same* endpoint the web page hits when you type into it; (2) it **reimplements Google's own web-client auth**: sends the raw `Cookie` header (mtime-cached from file), parses `SAPISID` out of it, computes + sends `Authorization: SAPISIDHASH {ts}_{h}`, optional `at` XSRF param (key functions `load_cookie()` / `make_sapisidhash()` / `_build_payload()` / `_extract_texts_from_line()` / `extract_response_text()` / `generate()` / `generate_stream()`); (3) it parses the wrapped RPC stream — scan for the `"wrb.fr"` marker, deserialise nested JSON at `arr[0][2]`, extract text from `inner[4]`, regex-detect `BardErrorInfo`; (4) mimicry is **header-level only** (spoofed `User-Agent`, `X-Same-Domain: 1`, matching Referer/Origin) — **no patched browser, no TLS/JS fingerprinting**. ⚠️ **What it does NOT do:** there is **no `__Secure-1PSIDTS` rotation** (cookies static from file) — materially behind the mature upstream `HanaokaYuzu/Gemini-API`, which rotates against `accounts.google.com/RotateCookies` roughly every 9 minutes because Google expires it fast.

**FRAGILE BY CONSTRUCTION:** `config.example.json` pins `"gemini_build": "boq_assistant-bard-web-server_20260716.08_p0"` — a **hardcoded Google internal web-server build ID** (the `bl` param) that Google rotates. Keeping it alive requires a live session cookie (no auto-rotation) **+** a current `SNlM0e` XSRF token **+** a current `bl` build ID, all harvested from a real logged-in Gemini page — which is exactly why the repo ships a browser extension (`gemini-cookie-sync-extension`: `manifest.json`/`popup.html`/`popup.js`/`README.txt`/`SETUP.md`) whose entire job is that refresh, writing them to a local `gemini-auth.json`. That extension's own README carries a good warning: the auth file *"represents the real Google session and must be treated as secret. Do not send it, print it, or commit it to Git."*

**WHAT IT EXPOSES** (`gemini_web2api/server.py`, ~650 lines, stdlib `http.server` — not FastAPI/uvicorn): `POST /v1/chat/completions` · `GET /v1/models` · **`POST /v1/responses` (OpenAI Responses API — Codex CLI)** · **`GET /v1beta/models` + `POST /v1beta/models/{model}:generateContent` + `:streamGenerateContent` (Google native — Gemini CLI)** · `GET /` status. No admin endpoints. ⚠️ **The on-goal tell: the intended clients include coding agents** (Codex CLI + Gemini CLI endpoint shapes — the v231 `caller_map` OpenClaw/OpenCode shape). **Claude appears nowhere in the repo.** Models (README-stated, with the web product's output ceilings): `gemini-3.6-flash` ~12k chars · `gemini-3.5-flash-thinking` ~20k · `gemini-3.5-flash-thinking-lite` ~15k · `gemini-3.1-pro` ~12k · `gemini-auto` · `gemini-flash-lite` ~10k. Features: SSE streaming (optional `httpx`), OpenAI-format **tool/function calling**, image input (URL or base64), Gemini's native web search. ⚠️ README caveat, verbatim: *"Without a paid subscription cookie, `gemini-3.1-pro` routes to the same Flash model"* — you don't get Pro free, you get Flash relabelled.

**"ZERO AUTH" — the genuinely notable claim.** README verbatim: *"Optional API keys: `api_keys` empty = no authentication required; with keys configured, validates as OpenAI Bearer Key"* and *"Anonymous access works for all models, but `gemini-3.1-pro` without authentication routes to Flash instead."* So it can serve Gemini Flash with **no Google account at all** — a purer free-tier harvest than v231 (which required your *own* logged-in accounts) — and it **inverts the risk profile**: anonymous mode exposes no account of yours (nothing to ban; pressure lands on Google's IP throttling, which the bundled **Cloudflare Worker** path — `cloudflare/worker.js`, credentials as dashboard env vars, ~300 edge locations, stated browser-fingerprint rotation — exists to spread), whereas cookie mode exposes a **real Google account with no rotation**. The Cloudflare README also warns *"Cookie 等同于你的 Google 账号凭证"* (*"cookies are equivalent to your Google account credentials"*).

**ARCHITECTURE:** the repo ships **two implementations of the same protocol** — a root `gemini_web2api.py` (**1,108 lines / 45.9 KB**, self-contained; the "single file" claim is substantiated) **and** an 8-module `gemini_web2api/` package (`__init__`/`__main__`/`config`/`gemini`/`models`/`multimodal`/`server`/`tools`). ⚠️ Its header does not state whether the single file is generated from the package or hand-maintained alongside it — **two copies of a protocol implementation in one repo is a drift risk**, recorded as an observation, not asserted as a defect. Also present: `tests/`, `.github/workflows/` (**only `docker.yml`** — CI builds a Docker image; **the tests are not gated in CI**, the geti v213 "CI build-only" shape), `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.local.yml`, `config.example.json`, `README.md` + `README_CN.md`.
