## v233 — ClawWork (HKUDS / Data Intelligence Lab @ The University of Hong Kong, PI Chao Huang) — 2026-08-17 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) MODERATE keys the tier ⚠️STRONG-reviewable · (c) STRONG ⚠️MODERATE-reviewable · (d) STRONG] — a **live economic-survival benchmark** in which LLM agents start with $10, are assigned real professional tasks from OpenAI's **GDPval** gold subset, **pay for their own tokens out of the same balance**, are graded by an LLM judge against occupation-specific rubrics, are paid `quality × estimated_hours × BLS_wage`, and **go bankrupt at $0**; plus **ClawMode**, a wrapper applying the same accounting to a live nanobot chat gateway across 9 channels; **1 NEW §C standalone at N=1 (CORPUS-FIRST for the surface, explicitly NOT world-first); counts 46/11 UNCHANGED; §C live standalones 48 → 49; surface ≈55 → ≈56**

**Operator-requested** ("build LLM wiki for `https://github.com/HKUDS/ClawWork`"; link arrived via Facebook, `fbclid` stripped).

**IDENTITY.** Repo description verbatim: *"ClawWork: OpenClaw as Your AI Coworker - 💰 $15K earned in 11 Hours"*. MIT; Python; ~8.3k★/~1.1k forks/82 watchers page-stated §37.4 → **NOT #52**. **~37–40 commits, ALL between 2026-02-16 and 2026-03-03 — a two-week burst, then silent ~5.5 months** as of the ship date. Contributors visible: `yuh-yang`, `chaohuang-ai`, `DorianZheng`, `gnai-creator`, **`claude`**, `thakoreh`, `Re-bin`. Author **HKUDS = Data Intelligence Lab @ HKU** (PI **Chao Huang**), **NOT Anthropic** (§41). ⚠️ **NOT source-cloned** (rendered page + raw README + tree + `requirements.txt` + `configs/` listing + `clawmode_integration/README.md` + `skill/SKILL.md` + `economic_tracker.py` + `evaluator.py` + `llm_evaluator.py` + commit history; the v200→v232 self-throttle — the ~972 KB shim overflows every subagent >200K).

**THE MECHANISM (source-verified).** Start **$10.00**; one GDPval task per simulated day; daily choice **work** (earn) vs **learn** (invest, no income); token cost deducted after every LLM call; `Payment = quality_score × (estimated_hours × BLS_hourly_wage)`; task value **$82.78–$5,004.00**, avg **$259.45**; payment only above `min_evaluation_threshold` **0.6**; `is_bankrupt()` at `current_balance <= 0`. Survival states (verbatim logic): `bankrupt <=0 / struggling <100 / stable <500 / thriving otherwise`, which the shipped `SKILL.md` ("Economic Survival Protocol") turns into agent policy on a **15-iteration budget** (submit by iteration 10–12). **The one sharp idea: token cost is ENDOGENOUS to the objective** — an agent that reasons beautifully but expensively goes broke. That inversion is the reason the repo is worth reading.

**THE DATA (independently verified).** **GDPval is OpenAI's** (arXiv **2510.04374**, Oct 2025): 1,320 tasks / **44 occupations** / top **9** US-GDP industries, real professional deliverables authored by ~14-yr-experience professionals; **220 open-sourced as the "gold subset."** ClawWork consumes **exactly that 220-task gold subset**, re-bucketed into 4 domains. ⚠️ **Terminology slip in ClawWork's own README** — it says *"44 economic sectors"*; GDPval is 44 **occupations** across 9 **sectors**.

**ARCHITECTURE.** `livebench/` (agent/ · work/ · tools/ · configs/ · prompts/ · scheduler/ · api/ · data/ · utils/ · langchain_mcp_adapters/ · **trading/ = only `__init__.py`, vestigial**) + `clawmode_integration/` + `eval/meta_prompts/` + `frontend/` (React dashboard) + FastAPI/WebSocket backend. Stack: `fastmcp` (*"MCP support (required for tools)"*) · LangChain + **`langchain-openai`** + `langchain-mcp-adapters` + **LangGraph** · **`boxlite` (default) + `e2b-code-interpreter` (fallback)** sandboxes · `tavily-python` · and a full document-production stack (**python-docx / python-pptx / reportlab / openpyxl / xlsxwriter / pdf2image / Pillow**) — because **GDPval deliverables ARE Office documents** (→ direct **OfficeCLI v206** cross-ref). **8 agent tools** (`decide_activity`, `submit_work`, `learn`, `get_status`, `search_web`, `create_file`, `execute_code_sandbox`, `create_video`) exposed over an **MCP server** (`tools/start_live_services.py`) used as an **internal tool bus for its own benchmark agents**.

**`EconomicTracker` = 876 lines** (per-task + per-channel cost records [LLM/search/OCR/other], `track_flat_api_call()`, three JSONL ledgers `balance.jsonl` / `token_costs.jsonl` / `task_completions.jsonl`). 🔴 **THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING — the cost axis does not hold:** pricing is **hardcoded and universal** — `input_token_price: float = 2.5` / `output_token_price: float = 10.0` per 1M — with **NO model-specific price table**. Unless an OpenRouter response supplies a pre-computed `cost`, **every model is billed at the same rate**, so the leaderboard's **"Cost" column substantially measures token VOLUME, not vendor pricing** — and the runs mix "thirdparty" and "openrouter" configs, so it is not even internally consistent. **The project's headline claim is cost efficiency and the cost axis is its weakest link.**

**EVALUATOR = 237-line `WorkEvaluator` → 829-line `LLMEvaluator`** — genuinely careful: per-occupation rubrics from `eval/meta_prompts/{normalized}.json`, **missing rubric → `FileNotFoundError`, no fallback**; *"use_llm_evaluation must be True. Heuristic evaluation is no longer supported."*; anti-gaming (artifact must exist + be non-empty, **>2MB rejected**, extraction errors raise); `payment = normalized_score * max_payment`. ⚠️ **Doc-vs-code drift:** README advertises **GPT-5.2** as judge; **code default is `"gpt-4o"`**, overridable via `EVALUATION_MODEL` (env `EVALUATION_API_KEY`/`_API_BASE`, falling back to `OPENAI_*`).

**CLAWMODE (the product half).** Wraps a **nanobot** gateway: `TrackedProvider` intercepts every `chat()` and feeds litellm's real token counts into `EconomicTracker`, responses carry a **balance footer**; `/clawwork <instruction>` assigns a *paid* task (classify into one of **40 occupations** → estimate hours → wage value → evaluate → pay); config at `~/.nanobot/config.json` under `agents.clawwork` (`initialBalance` **default $1000** — note the contrast with the benchmark's $10); channels **Telegram/Discord/Slack/WhatsApp/Email/Feishu/DingTalk/MoChat/QQ**. ⚠️ `cli.py::_inject_evaluation_credentials()` **reads API keys out of `~/.nanobot/config.json`** and exports them as `EVALUATION_*` env vars — a credential-handling surface.

**⚠️ THREE IDENTITY FACTS A CARELESS READ GETS WRONG.** **(1) `nanobot` is NOT Anthropic's** — a summariser asserted verbatim that ClawMode wraps *"nanobot (Anthropic's agent framework)"*; **FALSE, discarded**. It is **`HKUDS/nanobot`**, *the same lab's own* framework, openly **inspired by OpenClaw**, reimplementing ~90% of it in ~**4,000 lines vs OpenClaw's ~430,000**. Left standing it would have **flipped criterion (a)**. **(2) OpenClaw is Peter Steinberger's** — and **Steinberger authored corpus subject CodexBar v159** → an author cross-ref two hops out, **NOT #57**. **(3) HKUDS is a RETURNING corpus author, NOT a new one** — `HKUDS/DeepTutor` is corpus subject **v38**; `HKUDS/OpenSpace` was credited by **cortex-hub v181**. ClawWork is the **2nd HKUDS *subject***.

**⭐ CORPUS-RECURSIVE PREDICTION-CONFIRMATION (a genuine one).** The **DeepTutor v38** wiki posited an **HKUDS vertical-stack hypothesis** — *engine (**nanobot**) → methodology (CLI-Anything) → infra (LightRAG + RAG-Anything) → runtime (OpenHarness) → **apps** (DeepTutor + DeepCode…)* — and flagged *"50% HKUDS self-dependency"*. **ClawWork lands exactly on the predicted app layer**: a same-lab application/benchmark built on the same-lab engine. **The vault's own earlier analysis confirmed by a later independent ship. NOT #57** (ClawWork cites no corpus subject).

Calibrates level with **v232** (MODERATE, Claude-absent), above **v180**, below **llm-space v221 / PixelRAG v211**. **(c) STRONG ⚠️MODERATE-reviewable** (876-line ledger + 829-line evaluator + MCP tool server + React dashboard + 18 run configs + a second product surface + a real published dataset; against: two-week burst then silent, **self-run leaderboard**, **the universal-price flaw**, doc-vs-code drift ×2, vestigial `trading/`, NOT source-cloned). **(d) STRONG** (llm-space v221 closest neighbour · **DeepTutor v38** same-lab + prediction-confirmation · cortex-hub v181 · **CodexBar v159** · **GLM-5 v176** [already cites Vending Bench 2] · **OfficeCLI v206** · agent-skills · #18 MCP · #84 84c · cost + prompt-eval + orchestration threads · hireui candidate-LLM legibility ADR).

`deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness` — repo tagline verbatim *"DeepSeek Harness: Everything is a Plugin."*; README *"an open-source agent harness developed by DeepSeek AI … It uses an architecture where **everything is a plugin**, and is powered by Cordis."* Site deepseek.com/harness. **MIT; TypeScript monorepo; `@deepseek-ai/dsh-root` `0.1.0-rc.5`; released 2026-08-13; Node ^22.19.0 || >=24; pnpm 11.7.0; topics ai-agents/cordis/dsh/dsh-plugin.** Install `npx @deepseek-ai/dsh web` → Web UI on `http://127.0.0.1:3080`. **Scale (page/press/code-read-stated): ~453,000 lines of TypeScript across ~219 workspace packages, ~170,000 lines of docs, 1,386 decision records, 12,293 commits.** README warns in bold: *"currently in **developer preview** and is iterating rapidly. **THERE WILL BE COMPATIBILITY-BREAKING CHANGES.**"* Operator-requested. ⚠️ **NOT source-cloned** (hand-fetched: rendered repo page · raw README · raw `package.json` · `docs/` tree · `packages/` tree · `packages/llm` tree · `packages/subagent` tree · raw `packages/llm/llm-pi-ai/README.md` · deepseek.com/harness · landscape/press by WebSearch).

**THE KERNEL — Cordis, and it is NOT DeepSeek's.** An independent **meta-framework** (a framework for building frameworks) by the developer **shigma**, the plugin foundation of the **Koishi** chatbot framework for four years. Its single defining capability is **disposability** — load/unload/reload plugins with *complete cleanup of side effects* — via three mechanisms: `ctx.effect` (reversible side effects), lifecycle events (`ready`/`dispose`/`fork`), and a service system for dependency ordering. That is what makes "everything is a plugin" operational rather than decorative. DeepSeek **vendors + rescopes** it (`@deepseek-ai/cordis` on npm, npm-listing-stated) **with attribution machinery in CI** — `verify-cordis-config`, `gen-cordis-catalog`, `gen-cordis-api`, `verify-vendored-links`, `gen-third-party-notices`, `verify-dsh-package-licenses`, `rescope-vendor` → **attributed vendoring, the deliberate contrast to cortex-hub v181's silent GitNexus bundling**. **`omdsh-dev/DSH-better-sidebar`** (npm `dsh-better-sidebar` **v0.13.0**, MIT, TypeScript, ~2,038★/129 forks/216 commits page-stated §37.4) — a **VS Code-style right sidebar + bottom panel mounted as a Cordis plugin inside DeepSeek Harness** (file explorer, CodeMirror editor, real terminal via xterm.js + **node-pty**, Git panel, embedded sandboxed browser, **sub-agent topology view**), isolated per conversation session — **which also re-exposes its own public extension API (`ctx.betterSidebar`) so further third-party plugins register new tabs and file viewers into it.** Repo description (verbatim): 「开放的侧边栏底座，支持三方拓展注册新侧边栏页面。内置文件渲染编辑/终端/Git/子代理页面」. **⭐⭐ SECOND FINDING — v235's plugin thesis is RE-ENTRANT, not just swappable.** v236 proved a stranger could replace the UI seam. v237 proves a plugin can **publish its own service on the host context** and become a platform: `BetterSidebarService` exposes `registerTab` / `registerFileViewer` / `matchFileViewer` / `openTab` / `subscribe` / `subscribeState` / `getSnapshot` / `version` / `features[]`, and — source-verified from `docs/external-plugin-guide.md` — **the built-in tabs and viewers use that same public API** (吃自己的狗粮, "eating our own dog food"), with built-in IDs merely **non-overridable** (duplicate registration throws). Seven design decisions worth stealing: dogfooded API (no privileged internal path) · **optional peer dependency** so `ctx.betterSidebar === undefined` makes consumer registration silently skip · **capability gates** (`features` = `badge`/`tabLifecycle`/`updateTab`/`openFile`/`targetedOpen`/`stateSubscription`/`tabMeta`/`pluginSettings`/`urlTarget`/`settingSelect`) rather than version-sniffing alone · **mandatory disposers** via `ctx.effect()` (Cordis fiber unregisters on HMR/unload) · **type-only imports across bundle boundaries** (`import type {}` erased; a **build-purity gate** blocks value-imports from `@dsh-external/*` / unlisted `@deepseek-ai/*`; cross-plugin `require()` blocked by the loader) · **orphan degradation** (a persisted tab whose plugin is gone renders as a labelled placeholder and auto-restores) · **declarative settings as part of the contract** (`toggles` / `pluginToggles` persisted under `pluginSettings[id]` / custom `render`).

**⭐ THIRD FINDING — the CI gate is stronger than v236's.** v236 mechanised non-invasiveness with *static* checks. v237's `plugin-mount` job is an **integration contract test**: `pnpm build && pnpm pack && pnpm test:mount` packs the tarball, **mounts it into a real DSH instance on a scratch profile**, and renders it headlessly under **Playwright Chromium**, asserting the `[data-dsh-better-sidebar]` root mounts, no error bars, no page/plugin console errors, panel expansion, and that the terminal/editor **lazy chunks load**. Plus unit suites (`service`/`builtins`/`plugin-list`/`theme`). → the **FOURTH CONSECUTIVE ship handing the vault machinery for its own invariants** (v234 staleness-tracking → v235 doc-verification gates → v236 CI boundary gates → **v237 pack-and-mount-into-a-real-host**), pointed again at the **C22–C27 backlog + the deferred retire pass**.

**v238 dsh-anchored-standard** (2026-08-18): **T4 Plugin/Extension (agent-preset / Cordis row-composition flavour) with a T1 Skill/Methodology facet — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL · (b) MODERATE keys the tier ⚠️STRONG-reviewable · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG]; NO MINT (§C-mint alternative RECORDED + DECLINED on five grounds); counts 46/11 UNCHANGED; §C live standalones 49 unchanged; tracked surface ≈56 unchanged.** Operator-requested. ⚠️ **NOT source-cloned** (rendered repo page + raw README + git-tree API + 7 source files + 5 issues + FAREWELL/ACKNOWLEDGEMENTS/NOTICE/LICENSE/package.json/HANDOFF-2 + landscape research).

`xiaobright/dsh-anchored-standard` — repo tagline *"Two-phase DeepSeek Harness preset: Minimal-aligned bootstrap, then full Standard tools (Project2 98/99)."* A **DeepSeek Harness (DSH) agent PRESET** — not a plugin adding a feature, but a composition of Cordis rows copied into `~/.dsh/.agent-presets/` — that **constrains request #1 to the official Minimal preset's real two-tool schema (`bash` + `str_replace_editor`) and BLANKS every automatic context injection, then auto-promotes to a small resident catalog on the first durable `tool/call` or `assistant/message`.** MIT (`Copyright (c) 2026 xiaobright` + `Portions Copyright (c) 2026 DeepSeek`); **zero npm dependencies, no lifecycle scripts, no network calls, no telemetry**; Node ≥22.19.0; v0.1.0; 19 test files (`node --test`); CI ubuntu/Node 24 with `permissions: contents: read`; ~3,500★/106 forks/56 commits **page-stated §37.4** (→ NOT #52). Targets DSH **`0.1.0-rc.5`** at commit `47f9438`. **7 self-contained modes:** Anchored Standard (`preset/`) · Zero-Anchored · Whoami (「你是谁」 anchor turn) · Prefab (seeded trajectory) · Eternal Minimal (`dshx` bash gateway; catalog never grows) · Wire Think-Execute (`tool_choice: none` via a vendored sibling provider route) · Combo Anchored (think-split + depth gate + deliberation drip as 3 independent rows). Author **`xiaobright` = a BARE HANDLE** — 6 repos, 32 followers, 0 following, no bio/company/location/website; portfolio is measurement-first (`modeltest` = a frozen private eval harness *"Not a public benchmark"*; `modeltest-v5` = *"failed experiments archive (stalled)"*; `remote-mcp`; `vision-mcp-pool`); **NOT DeepSeek, NOT Anthropic** (§41; #19 19a).

**⭐ FINDING 1 — the project DIED the day before this ship, and its exit note is the most valuable artifact in it.** `FAREWELL.md` (2026-08-17, Chinese): 「很朴素：能力和财力都有限。API 涨价之后，一轮完整评测的成本已经超过了我的承受范围，而继续在没有验证能力的情况下堆功能，是对用户不负责任。」 (*"Simply: both capability and finances are limited. After the API price increase, the cost of one complete evaluation round has exceeded what I can bear, and continuing to pile on features without verification capability is irresponsible to users."*) `HANDOFF-2.md` prices it: an eval round went **~¥2 → ~¥12 (~$0.28 → ~$1.70)**. The absolute figure is trivial — which is the point: the work needed *many* rounds, so a ~6× multiplier killed it. **The generalisable lesson: for inference-time research the binding constraint is the cost of EVALUATION, not development.** Also 「项目现在有三千多个 star，但我清楚，这个数字并不等同于我个人的技术能力。」 and the real thesis, sharper than the README's: 「说得直白是替官方补位——把模型在评测条件下被训练出的好行为，在用户真实使用的环境里重新捞出来。」 (*"plainly: filling gaps for the official team — retrieving the good behavior the model was trained to show under evaluation conditions, back into the user's real-world environment"*), naming its own obsolescence condition (train across diverse harnesses; **cites Kimi K3's technical report** as proof the path works).

**⭐⭐ FINDING 2 — the evidence establishes the STYLE effect and does NOT establish the QUALITY effect; the two independent replications DISAGREE with each other.** ESTABLISHED: **#65** (@TipsyDrifter, 3×3 randomised block, n=3/preset) — trajectory anchoring **9/9 separated perfectly by preset**, *"real and very robust."* **#6** (@slicenferqin) — **~9 KB** of auto-injected skill catalog took the anchor from **~81% to 0/9**, which explains why third parties with local skills installed *"could never replicate."* **#11** (@Rtyyy233, 45-session controlled trial) — the tool schema is the decisive lever at the adapter-default 256000 maxTokens (README: 5/5 minimal anchored vs 11/11 standard-family standard-like; ⚠️ the issue's own condition table could not be cleanly reconciled to that 5/5-vs-11/11 framing without deeper reading — **flagged, not invented**; the shared conclusion "tool-schema identity is a sufficient variable at 256000" is what is cited). NOT ESTABLISHED: **#65** ability +3.3, **95% CI [−2.6, +9.3]**, ANOVA F(2,6)=1.05, **not significant**. DISPUTED: **#51** (@JimMilk, 11 rounds × 3 OSes) — Ability **85–90, 98/99 NOT reproduced**, trajectory showed **no correlation with scores**, *"the author's 98/99 trajectory is not reproducible on current weights"*; score losses traced to a **model-layer defect** (F3-05 session_id implicit authorization) *"unrelated to OS/preset/trajectory."* RETRACTED: **#60** (@MolecularFullerene, a **third party**) showed the headline scores had been **retroactively re-attributed** — those runs used a first-request `pwsh`+`read` surface promoting to the **full 25-tool** catalog; the exact Minimal pair arrived later (commit `a1e1c1d`). The author accepted it and the README now carries the caveat — **but the repo TAGLINE still advertises "Project2 98/99"**, the number nobody has reproduced.

**⭐ FINDING 3 — the mechanism is SOURCE-VERIFIED and well built.** `shared/context-gate.mjs` hooks two genuine unified injection paths — `system-prompt/assemble` **blanking the whole family** (`return { ...assembled, contexts: [] }`, deliberately *"without enumerating them"* so unknown third-party providers are suppressed by default) and `agent/pre-step` (`{ prepend: true }`) **filtering** to the claimed batch plus `allowKinds` (default `['skill-invocation']`, because *"a user-initiated skill gesture is not an automatic injection"*). Promotion reads durable events (`PROMOTE_EVENTS = { 'tool-call': ['tool/call'], 'assistant-message': ['assistant/message'], either: [both] }`) so resume is safe; `compaction/end` **re-demotes** (*"a 'second first request'"*); both filters **FAIL OPEN** (*"a gate bug must never eat the user's context"*). `shared/tool-bootstrap.mjs` **filters, not replaces** (`assembled.tools.filter(t => keep.has(t.name))`); resident set = `bootstrapTools + ['dev_tool_search','skill_search','skill_load'] + unlockedFor(session)`; `bootstrapMaxTokens` **explicitly stripped at promotion** (else the seed proposal carries it forward all session); **a missing bootstrap tool degrades to the full catalog with a one-time warning** while an invalid `promoteOn` **throws at mount** = **fail-soft at runtime, fail-fast at config time**. `preset/agent.cordis.yml` rows 1–2 confirmed `context-gate` then `tool-bootstrap`; the Standard sandboxed `tool-bash` row is `disabled: true` **on every platform** (same tool name into the same layer, registry rejects duplicates), as are `tool-subagent-codex` and `tool-subagent-claude-code`. `shared/toolchoice-adapter.mjs` **vendors a protocol-faithful subset of DeepSeek's own SSE/serialize/translate pipeline** (own `parseSseStream`, own `serializeThinkRequest`) because `tool_choice` is outside the harness `GenerateOptions` vocabulary and the official adapter builds its wire body in a private generator; registers a **sibling route** `deepseek-wire-think` (`toolChoice` defaults `'none'` only when `tools !== undefined`), resolves row-config → `llm-deepseek` settings → `DEEPSEEK_BASE_URL`/`DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, only URL literal `https://api.deepseek.com`, catches registration failure and degrades to the zero-tool condition, and the `logprobs` opt-in can only **log a per-request mean** (no StreamChunk surface exists) — the vendoring is disclosed in `NOTICE`. ⚠️ `eternal-minimal.mjs` / `wire-think.mjs` / `cot-drip.mjs` / `deliberation-gate.mjs` are **DOC-STATED, not source-verified** (WebFetch returned summaries; flagged, not papered over) — incl. the documented twist that gateway payloads must ride the **deny channel** (*"the only sanctioned pre-dispatch way to substitute a result"*) so genuine tool output arrives **flagged as an error**, with the payload wording compensating.

**SIX errors caught.** (1) ⚠️ **the GitHub API** — agents used `api.github.com` heavily; **§37.4 says this environment mocks it** → the **1,477-file** and **66-contributor** figures **DISCARDED**, replaced with the hand-verified 70-handle README block (several API figures *did* corroborate independently-verified page/registry facts — 4,419 ≈ "4.4k"; repo creation ~08-12 vs first npm publish 08-13 — so those are reported page-stated-and-corroborated, **never** as API-verified); (2) **my own package count** — I first recorded **8** packages from the README, the registry shows **13 `@linxin666` + `dsh-better-sidebar` = 14**; corrected in-session, and the discrepancy turned out to **BE a finding**; (3) **a near-miss mint** — the orchestration-platform row, avoided only by reading it verbatim; (4) **my own overstated risk** — I framed the danger as *"unattended cron + `ssh_exec`"*, but the scheduler **queues** (`mode:'queue'`) and is **fail-closed on permission**; the SSH risk is real, that framing was wrong; (5) **an agent's install-risk claim** — `prepare` runs for the publisher and on git installs, **not** for a registry consumer; the real transitive actor is **`cloudflared`'s `postinstall`**, verified in its own manifest; (6) **a tempting identity inference DECLINED** — the `Chimney` handle vs v236's `ccch1mneyyy`, left UNVERIFIED rather than asserted (§41 discipline applies to people, not only to criterion (a)). **`inflation_check` HELD.**

⚠️ **PILOT: read-and-borrow — do NOT install. NOT a hireui component.** Five sufficient reasons: a plugin suite for a rival lab's runtime at `0.1.0-rc.7` (shipped yesterday, breaking changes promised) · v0.2.0 on a ~6-day-old repo, 21 npm versions in 5 days · **`dsh-ssh` is a genuine hazard** · licence mixing blocks commercial use · the one-line install transitively fetches a tunnel binary. 🔴 **Never `dsh-ssh` against production; never the aggregate on a machine with real credentials; never point any of it at candidate data; DO NOT cite 98/99.** ⭐ **A1 → B5 → C11:** read `scripts/verify-docs.mjs` + the PR template + the Liangshen README against v238's issues (~30 min, zero install) → write a **vault doc-lint contract** into `CLAUDE.md` (required files · index↔content agreement · dead links · chapter-size caps · stale-row floors · count reconciliation) → **implement `verify-vault-docs`** that FAILS on each = **the C22–C27 retire pass, mechanised**, with five consecutive ships having handed over the parts. Also **B6** the AI-authorship disclosure field → hireui's PR template (borrow the field, **not** the auto-close severity) · **B7** the five-rule fail-closed scheduling contract for any hireui scheduled LLM job · **D14** *"an agent that can reach production must be gated at the tool, not the prompt"* into the hireui LLM ADR, citing **v212 as the reference implementation** and `dsh-ssh` as the counter-example (extends the RATIFIED candidate-LLM legibility ADR from *legibility* to *reach*) · **B8** mirror the `allowBuilds` + `minimumReleaseAge` + exact-pin hygiene · **E19** flag to the audit: the v237 axis at **N=3**, the v238 axis at **N=2-as-derivative** + the v236 `presets/liangshen/` evidence, and the new **SSH-fleet-reach** watch axis.

**Blunt summary.** Seventy people spent six days building a 13-package plugin suite for DeepSeek's web UI, and built better process machinery than most funded projects along the way — a **required AI-authorship field** in the PR template (naming Claude Code among four expected agent tools), a doc linter that **hashes translations so they cannot silently drift**, a CI job that mounts the plugin into a real host and renders it headless, a lifecycle allowlist, one-time pairing tokens. Then they shipped an SSH plugin that hands the model **`ssh_exec` and `ssh_cluster` with no approval gate** and keeps passwords in a **plaintext JSON file** — and said so plainly in the README, one ship after the corpus recorded **v212 tabularis** solving that exact secret class with the OS keychain. The pattern underneath is the lesson: **everything the build can check is checked; everything only a human can check has already drifted** — three plugin counts, a stale root version, a tagline advertising a feature that does not exist, and a benchmark number whose upstream retracted its attribution two days after this project copied it, still sitting in the npm registry today. **That last one is a mirror, not a gotcha. Take the doc linter and the disclosure field; leave the SSH plugin and the number.**

**⭐ PROVENANCE MEASURED WITHOUT THE MOCKED API — the clone carries authoritative git metadata.** First commit **2026-08-13 21:55:28 +0800** (`fkysly`, `init: awesome-dsh-plugin`) → latest 2026-08-18 19:38 = **~5 days old**; **1,662 commits**; **853 unique author emails**; commits/day 25/381/403/416/239/198. ⚠️ But maintainership is **bus-factor 1**: `fkysly` = **243 commits** and **86 of the ~93 commits touching `scripts/`+`.github/`**; `github-actions[bot]` = 113; the rest is a long tail (PerryLink 23, ahmed isam 17, John Tsui 15…), most with exactly one. `scripts/maint-rebase.sh` exists for that shape (a comment references **~150 open PRs**).

**⭐⭐ IT IS A REGISTRY, NOT A DOCUMENT.** `data/plugins/<owner>__<repo>.yml` = one 5-field record per plugin (`url`/`name`/`category`/`description.{en,zh}`, optional `tarball`); `scripts/generate-readme.mjs` compiles them into two 350KB+ READMEs between `<!-- BEGIN TOC/PLUGINS -->` markers; `scripts/build-site.mjs` (~41KB) emits the site **and** `docs/plugins.json` — commented at line 675 **「Public registry API: /plugins.json — deterministic; consumed by the find[er]」** — plus `readmes.json`, `count.json` (the README's own count badge), `feed.xml`, sitemap, per-locale JSON-LD, per-plugin detail pages. **Two independent runtime consumers, both fetch-verified:** **`dsh-market/dsh-market`** (MIT, page-stated 967★, **a SEPARATE org**) states 「Live from awesome-dsh-plugin.com/plugins.json … with a bundled snapshot as offline fallback」 and 「This repo is the market app, not the catalog」; **`awesome-dsh-plugin/dsh-find-plugin`** (MIT, page-stated 55★, the org's **only** other repo) registers a **`find_dsh_plugin` tool INTO the agent** ⚠️ *but* indexes the live GitHub `dsh-plugin` topic first and merely overlays the curated descriptions. ⭐ **Corpus link: v239's `community-plugins` panel earned a #68 sub-variant described as 「static, index-only, NO RUNTIME REGISTRY」 — v240 is that runtime registry.**

**⭐ COUNT RECONCILIATION IS EXACT, IN BOTH LANGUAGES** (hand-derived): 1390 `*.yml` = 1393 `^- [` lines − 3 TOC links = 20 category headings summing to **1390**, and `README.zh.md` likewise 1393 → 1390; **bilingual completeness 1390/1390** (`en` and `zh` both present in every record, zero misses). ⭐ **The v239 contrast: that subject stated 11 plugins, listed 12, shipped 14. This one cannot disagree with itself — one record, two renders = PREVENTION, strictly stronger than v239's blob-hash translation DETECTION.** Drift is **enforced**, not merely available: a whole-file 「Set check」 fails on `smuggled`/`missing` URLs and `process.exit(1)`.

**⭐⭐⭐ FINDING 1 — IT CHECKS ITS PROSE AGAINST ITS CODE, closing exactly the gap v239 was recorded as unable to close.** `generate-readme.mjs` ends with a check that `contributing.md`'s category enumeration equals `CAT_IDS`, exiting 1 on mismatch, commented 「It drifted once already — `usage` and `vision` were added to the taxonomy and the docs kept advertising the old twelve — so the list is checked here rather than trusted to stay in step by hand.」 **v239's own conclusion was that `verify-docs.mjs` 「checks structure, not content equivalence → prose numbers are exactly what it cannot catch」.** Two consecutive ships now supply the complete mechanism.

**⭐⭐⭐ FINDING 2 — THE INVENTORY RULE (the ship's best finding, hand-found).** `data/plugins/zmm863-commits__dsh-paperclip` is a **complete, well-formed, bilingual submission record with no `.yml` extension**. `scripts/lib/entries.mjs:69` = `if (!f.endsWith('.yml')) continue` — skipped **silently**. Verified consequences: **0** occurrences in `README.md`, **0** in `README.zh.md`, **0** in `screenshots.json`/`added-dates.json`/`stars.json` → therefore absent from the site, from `plugins.json`, and so from **dsh-market's storefront** and **`find_dsh_plugin`'s results**. Merged as **PR #1192 on 2026-08-17**. ⭐ And the filename-must-match-the-url validator at `entries.mjs:133` **sits downstream of the glob that excludes it**. → **THE GENERALISABLE RULE: a consistency check between two views of one source cannot see what is missing from the source; every generate-from-data pipeline needs a separate INVENTORY check enumerating the input directory by a DIFFERENT rule than the parser uses.** ⭐⭐ **That is the vault's C22–C27 class exactly** — an index↔content check between `CLAUDE.md` and `_state/03c` would never notice a chapter absent from the index, which is how `03c-projects-v61-v183.md` came to hold entries through **v240** under a `-v183` label.

**⭐⭐ FINDING 3 — A COHERENT DOCTRINE: AUTOMATE THE EVIDENCE, NEVER THE IRREVERSIBLE DECISION.** `scan-decay.mjs` (weekly; 4 signals `gone`/`archived`/`dormant` at **`DORMANT_MONTHS = 6`**/`unbundled`; one tracking issue updated in place) — 「**Flags — never removes** … removal stays a human decision because it is irreversible and a scan can be wrong … Anything inconclusive (API errors) is skipped, not flagged: **a decay report must only ever contain evidence, not doubt.**」 · `check-bleed.mjs` — detects one entry's description bleeding into another's, born from incident **#1348** (「a PR whose stated purpose was refreshing the dsh-notifier entry also appended [it] to `AKS1st/dsh-cyber-particle`, an unrelated plugin. **It happened twice**, and every existing check passed both times」), fingerprint = a shared run of **`RUN = 40`** chars, same-owner pairs skipped, **「reported, not enforced」**, threshold *empirically calibrated* (「At 40, a full pass over ~1170 entries surfaced five pairs, all genuine similarity」) · `build-site.mjs` — **`STARS_MIN_COVERAGE = 0.66`** publish floor from incident **#1673 dated 2026-08-18** (「`plugins.json` went out with `stars: null` for all 1,362 entries … nothing between it and the deploy asked whether that was plausible … a stale number degrades gracefully and a null does not」). ⭐⭐ **THE SHARPEST ONE-SHIP-APART CONTRAST OF THE RUN: v239's `pr-review.mjs` AUTO-CLOSED issue #532 — a substantive bug report — for template non-compliance; v240 refuses to auto-remove anything.** Every non-obvious constant here carries a comment naming the incident that motivated it and the measurement that calibrated it (`locales.mjs` even records an SEO finding 「measured at a third of the click-through their position should earn」).

**⭐⭐ FINDING 4 — A CONTESTED CLAIM CAUGHT PROPAGATING, AGAIN, ONE SHIP LATER.** The list's editorial policy requires a reviewer to check 「Does the code do what the entry claims — including any numbers or API names」. Its **verified entry for the v239 subject** reads 「… pet, **live token stats**, and a skin center」 — the phantom feature **v239 recorded as absent from every README and every published package**. **Re-verified independently by me against the live source:** `zhu1090093659/dsh-web-ui`'s current README (33,162 bytes, raw fetch) contains **ZERO** `token`/`Token`/`usage` hits; its single 令牌 occurrence is line 81, the **mobile-pairing** token. ⭐ **Structurally the same event as v239's and pointing the other way: v239 republished upstream's retracted benchmark into its npm description; v240 republishes v239's unsubstantiated feature into its registry API** — a claim moving downstream through a live dependency graph faster than anyone re-checks it. ⚠️ Fair caveats: banal not malicious (copied from the subject's own tagline, which the policy warns against), and I checked the aggregate's root README, not every sub-package. **⭐ Also: all three corpus DSH subjects were listed 2026-08-14 — day two of the list's life, BEFORE the corpus shipped any of them** (v236 08-17; v237/v239 08-18): v236 dsh-TUI 「Claude Code-style full-screen terminal UI…」 · v237 DSH-better-sidebar 「Full sidebar workbench … third-party plugins can register new tabs」 · v239 dsh-web-ui (above). **v238 `xiaobright/dsh-anchored-standard` is NOT listed** — though two same-named third-party presets are (`ruby1304__dsh-preset-anchored-standard`, `Jungod1121__dsh-anchored-standard`).

**⭐ FINDING 5 — SECURITY: the best CI-security artifact of the run, plus one honest limit.** **`pr-gate.yml`'s header** correctly diagnoses and avoids a known GitHub Actions privilege-escalation class: 「a token is in scope here, so **nothing from the pull request is ever executed**. The checkout stays on the base repo's default branch — trusted code, trusted lockfile — and the only thing taken from the PR is the content of `data/plugins/*.yml`, extracted into a scratch directory and **read as data**. Checking out `refs/pull/N/merge` and running `npm ci` there would hand the token to fork-supplied install scripts, which is the **`pull_request_target` footgun this workflow exists to avoid**.」 (Same file records a rate-limit incident dated 2026-08-18.) **All 6 workflows `permissions: contents: read`** except `decay-scan` (`issues: write`); no publish job, no secrets beyond `GITHUB_TOKEN`; **no lifecycle scripts**; 2 devDeps only (`js-yaml ^5.3.0`, `marked ^18.0.9` — both current; npm `latest` for js-yaml **is** 5.3.0 with `v4-legacy: 4.3.1`, registry-checked). Gate = **structure/metadata only**: `dsh.bundle` manifest present, **repo age ≥ 1 day**, **commits ≥ 10**, archived status, plus `awesome-lint` + locale parity. ⚠️ **THE HONEST LIMIT — and the project states it first:** the README's 「if a description claims '46 tools', someone counts them」 has **no mechanism**; `contributing.md` says so before anyone else can (「A green CI run is the **precondition**, not the decision … **It cannot tell whether a plugin does what its entry says**」). The adversarial verdict on "this is a verification pipeline" was **PARTLY**. `probe-tarballs.mjs` does **NOT** extract or scan tarballs — a ranged `GET bytes=0-0` only. **No listed artefact is scanned anywhere** (「Being on this list is not a security review」). ⚠️ **A lockfile finding no agent surfaced:** `package-lock.json` resolves **2 of 3 packages from `registry.npmmirror.com`** (`js-yaml`, `argparse`; only `marked` from npmjs.org) and **`npm ci` runs in 4 workflows** → integrity-hashed, so the exposure is **availability + install-traffic visibility, not integrity**. ⭐ Genuinely good privacy posture: self-hosted webfonts, and a privacy page that **names Cloudflare Web Analytics explicitly** (cookie-less, no fingerprinting, no ad networks/social widgets/tag managers, 「contains nothing about visitors」). ⭐ Provenance discipline on downloads: a `tarball:` must be an `https` `.tgz` on GitHub's own release hosting 「the list won't hand users a download link it can't vouch for」; screenshots must be GitHub-hosted, third-party image hosts 「rejected by the build for user-privacy reasons」 (675 of 1390 entries have screenshots). ⭐ And **real semver expertise** in `contributing.md`: a precise account of why a peer range like `>=0.0.1-rc.1 <0.2.0` **silently excludes** `0.1.0-rc.6` under node-semver, with the correct `||`-branch fix — **directly relevant to v236's 21 `@deepseek-ai/*` peers at `^0.1.0-rc.6` and v239's `rc.7`**.

It survives because `generate-readme.mjs` line 2 states 「Everything outside the marker blocks (badges, banner, …)」 is not regenerated — the language switcher is hand-written preamble. ⭐ **1,390 generated lines are perfect; the one hand-written navigation line is broken.** (2) **One CRLF record in 1,390** — `data/plugins/paicat1__dsh-screenshot.yml` (confirmed `od -c`: `v i s i o n \r \n`); no `.gitattributes`; js-yaml tolerates it so it renders correctly. a separate path un-protects the one who configured SOMETHING.**

**⭐ FINDING 7 — "STRONG ISOLATION" IS PASSTHROUGH, AND THE HONEST PART IS THE PART THE README HIDES.** README:33 claims *"Supports secure container runtimes like gVisor, Kata Containers, and Firecracker microVM."* Grepping the tree for `gvisor|runsc|kata|firecracker` across `.py .go .yaml .toml`, hits land **only** in the README, `server/configuration.md`, `config.py` (a `SecureRuntimeConfig` model + validation) and **tests** — **there is NO gVisor/Kata/Firecracker integration code.** What exists is a `secure_runtime` block (`type` ∈ `"" | gvisor | kata | firecracker`, `docker_runtime`, `k8s_runtime_class`) that becomes the pod's `runtimeClassName` (`config.py:808-813`). **Architecturally correct — but the claim belongs to Kubernetes: OpenSandbox does not isolate, it lets you TELL YOUR CLUSTER which isolator to use, and you install it.** ⭐ The real engineering is a **compatibility matrix enforced in validators** (`server/tests/test_validators.py:702-745`, `ensure_egress_runtime_compatible()`): **`test_rejects_gvisor_with_network_policy`** (the error message names "gVisor") vs **`test_allows_kata_with_network_policy`**; `firecracker` requires `k8s_runtime_class` and is **Kubernetes-only** (`configuration.md:273,280`). ⭐⭐ **Choosing their strongest isolation COSTS YOU their egress control — a genuine, non-obvious, security-relevant trade-off encoded in code and tests, which the README's single 🏰 bullet actively obscures.**

Images to 3 registries, cosign keyless-signed with provenance attestations, "pin by digest" advised. **19 lockfiles; ZERO npm lifecycle scripts across all 5 `package.json`** (no postinstall/preinstall/prepare/prepublish) — contrast v242, which needed a 5-allow/3-deny policy because it *had* scripts. **No mirror substitution in any lockfile.** ⚠️ **But 2 Dockerfiles rewrite upstreams:** `kubernetes/Dockerfile.image-committer:19,38` `sed -i 's/dl-cdn.alpinelinux.org/mirrors.aliyun.com/g'` and `:25` + `kubernetes/Dockerfile:36` `GOPROXY=https://goproxy.cn,direct` — **scope: 2 files, image-BUILD path only; dependency RESOLUTION stays canonical.** Not the v240-class lockfile-mirror defect, but a trust boundary in a security product. **Tests: 447 files / 6 languages** (236 Go · 137 Python · 47 Kotlin/Java/C# · 27 JS/TS; `server/tests/` = 66 files / 29,504 lines; test-to-source ≈**0.52**), real e2e (`real-e2e.yml`, Kind K8s e2e, `tests/{go,python,javascript}`). **24 CI workflows, 11 on `pull_request`.** ⭐⭐ **D28 — AN ABSENT CONFIG FILE IS NOT AN ABSENT CHECK:** grepping all 24 workflows for `codeql|trivy|gosec|bandit|semgrep|dependency-review|scorecard|snyk` returns **ZERO**, and there is **no `.github/dependabot.yml`** — **yet 18 `Copilot Autofix` commits and 5 `dependabot/` branches prove both run via GitHub SETTINGS, invisible in the tree.** A tree-only audit systematically **UNDER-reports** automated security posture; **the detector is the bot's commit trailers, not the workflow directory.** Completes the trio: **D26** what a body-grep counts · **D27** which refs it counts over · **D28** whether the config is in the tree at all.

**⭐ FINDING 10 — DOCS INTEGRITY: BETTER THAN CORPUS NORM, WITH ONE PRECISE GAP, AND ⭐ D29.** ⭐ **`cli/AGENTS.md` is CLEAN.** A critic flagged it *"67 days stale"*; I tested **every path it names** (`src/opensandbox_cli/{client,main,output,skill_registry}.py`, `commands/`, `skills/`, `tests/test_{cli_help,commands,skills}.py`, `../sdks/AGENTS.md`, `../specs/AGENTS.md`) — **all 11 EXIST ⇒ REFUTED.** ⭐⭐ **D29 — `mtime` IS NOT DRIFT; TEST THE CLAIMS, NOT THE DATE.** A file unchanged for 67 days because it is still correct is not stale; staleness is *content disagreeing with reality*. **This is the discipline that decides whether `verify-vault-docs` is a linter or a recency alarm.** Docs = static VitePress (`docs/.vitepress/config.mts`, *"no build-time code generation"*), **72 markdown files**, declared taxonomy, mandatory `title`+`description` frontmatter, and a hard gate in root `AGENTS.md`: *"`cd docs && pnpm docs:build` — must complete with zero errors."* ⭐ **A v240 inventory-rule instance, live:** of 71 non-README docs, **11 are unreferenced in `config.mts` — but 9 are `index.md` section landing pages VitePress routes by directory, so the genuinely unreachable content pages are TWO: `docs/examples/deep-agents.md` and `docs/components/egress-mitmproxy-sse-truncation.md`.** ⚠️ **Cite two, not eleven** — reporting 11 would be exactly the inflation this vault exists to catch; that `deep-agents.md` is an *agent-integration* page makes it the more interesting one. ⚠️ 3 files typo `Ltd..`.

**⭐⭐ RECORDED, NOT EXECUTED — FLAGGED TO AUDIT: the committed cross-harness agent-context bridge reaches N=3 and CROSSES the eligibility threshold.** **v213 geti** (committed cross-harness symlinks for a first-party skill suite, N=1) → **v243 ToolJet** (`CLAUDE.md` as a 9-byte symlink to canonical `AGENTS.md`, 3 of 13 dirs — N=2, recorded+flagged by v243, not promoted) → **v244 OpenSandbox** (`server/CLAUDE.md` symlink + an 85-byte root stub — **N=3**). ⭐ **Three independent, cross-author, cross-domain, non-port instances (Intel / ToolJet / Alibaba) ⇒ the corpus's eligible-at-N=3 discipline (v203) is SATISFIED and a promotion is live on the table.** ⚠️ **NOT self-executed — a promotion is an audit act (the v232 rule, upheld v235 and v243).** Three things the audit must weigh: (i) the three are **not the same mechanism** (geti = a skill *suite*; ToolJet = the *root* context file, the load-bearing half; OpenSandbox = a *subdirectory* file **plus a prose stub at root**) ⇒ the class likely needs stating **mechanism-agnostically** as *"a committed, drift-proof bridge from the harness-specific filename to a canonical `AGENTS.md`"* or it fractures at N=3; (ii) **both multi-instance cases are PARTIAL** (ToolJet 3/13, OpenSandbox 2/6 **with two incompatible mechanisms in one repo**) ⇒ the pattern's real-world form is *incomplete adoption* and the row should say so; (iii) the stub variant is drift-proof but **weaker for the harness** (a second read) ⇒ a promoted row should **rank** the mechanisms, not just enumerate them.

**⭐⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE — AN APACHE-2.0 REPO THAT EXECUTES A REVENUE-CAPPED ENGINE AND NEVER MENTIONS IT.** `needle/__init__.py:13-28` → `needle/agent/fetch.py:88-102` downloads `python/cactus_needle-2.0.2-py3-none-<tag>.whl` from the **HF MODEL repo** `Cactus-Compute/needle2`, unzips **`libneedle.dylib/.so/.dll`** out of it, and `ctypes.CDLL`s it into your process (`:38`). **Three licences are now live:** this repo **Apache-2.0** (⭐ changed **MIT → Apache-2.0** at `b188e110` on **2026-08-17, two days before HEAD**); the HF repo it fetches from declares **apache-2.0**; and **`cactus-compute/cactus`** — the C++ engine **SOURCE**, 5.9k★, updated 2026-08-17 — carries a **custom licence GitHub reports as "Other"**, free only under **< $2,000,000 total funding AND < $2,000,000 gross annual revenue**, **auto-terminating** with a commercial licence required within **30 days**. **🔴 And this repo says NOTHING:** `grep -rn -iE "cactus-compute/cactus|commercial licen|proprietar|funding|revenue|dual.?licen"` across all 44 files → **ZERO HITS** (SOURCE-VERIFIED). ⚠️ **NOT concealment** (the engine repo is public, linked from the org page, its licence plain text) and **NOT a legal conclusion**. **Sufficient claim: no document in either repo reconciles the declarations or states which governs the binary in your process.** ⭐⭐ **AGAINST v244 + v245 THIS COMPLETES A SET OF THREE: OpenSandbox OVER-asserted an identity its governance doc never named; Unsloth UNDER-asserted one its packaging enforced; Needle SPLITS one across two repos and the restrictive half is the half you execute — three consecutive ships where the licence in prose does not describe the artifact that runs, and in all three the ENFORCED/EXECUTED artifact is the honest one.**

**⭐⭐⭐ THE BEST IDEA IS ONE GREP — `grep -rni "silent" .` RETURNS THE CODEBASE'S DESIGN DOCTRINE IN FOUR LINES.** Three convert a silent wrong answer into a loud failure: `__init__.py:73-77` (the engine is a process-global singleton that **cannot unload weights**, so a base-model agent built after a tuned one **raises** — *"so this agent would **silently** answer with those weights; construct agents that want the base model before any tuned one, or run them in separate processes"*); `export.py:29-31` (`kv_window`/`kv_bits` are **baked into the `.cact` header** rather than exposed as runtime flags because *"a model quantized for one must be RUN at it — leaving either to a runtime flag **silently** [corrupts]"*); `export.py:547-554` (refuses an export that *"would **silently** ship plain W4 — numerics it was never post-trained for"*). Three more in the same spirit: `warnings.warn` at construction (`__init__.py:57-60`), the same note printed by every fine-tune run (`finetune.py:401`), and *"this is an engine bug — please report it with the prompt and schema"* (`__init__.py:92-96`). ⭐ **Every message states CAUSE, CONSEQUENCE and REMEDY** — that is what separates them from an exception. **⇒ THE RULE: every failure mode that would produce a confident wrong answer is converted into a loud one; where it cannot be made loud, the setting moves out of a runtime flag and into the artifact so it cannot be set wrong.** ⭐ **The grep is PORTABLE — run it on any codebase to find every place its author thought about silent corruption.** ⚠️ **The 4th hit is a COUNTER-EXAMPLE and it is what keeps the finding honest:** `doc/finetuning.md:19` *"longer examples are **silently truncated**"* — a silent data-loss path documented in prose with no warning emitted. **Three convert a silence into a noise; the fourth admits one and leaves it.**

**⭐⭐⭐ THE IRONY, AND THE SHARPEST FINDING: THE DOCTRINE IS NOT APPLIED TO THEIR OWN RELEASE GATE.** `.github/workflows/release.yaml` is a **daily automated release train** (cron 16:00+17:00 UTC with a DST guard selecting **09:00 Pacific**) that auto-bumps the patch version, builds, `twine check`s, publishes to PyPI and pushes a tag — **no human between a merge to `main` and a public release**. ✅ **Verified externally: PyPI shows 7 releases, 2.0.0 → 2.0.6, 2026-08-10 → 2026-08-17, one per day.** Much is genuinely good: top-level `permissions: contents: read` escalated only in the release job; **`id-token: write` + `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` = PyPI Trusted Publishing (OIDC)**, no long-lived token; and version discovery via **`git tag --list 'v*' --sort=-v:refname`** — ⭐ **a CORRECT version sort, i.e. exactly what the vault's own v245 ship got wrong with the lexical `git tag | tail`**. **🔴 BUT THE GATE IS `pytest -q -m "not slow"` ON A FRESH `ubuntu-latest`:** `tests/test_inference.py` (**5 tests**, the ONLY end-to-end engine tests) carries `pytestmark = requires_engine` (`:3`) and `conftest.py:20` **skips when no engine is cached** — a fresh runner has none; `test_build.py` (3) and `test_finetune.py` (2) are **`pytest.mark.slow` → DESELECTED**; and `test_weights.py:33-38` monkeypatches `_lib` with a **stub**. **⇒ EVERY test that exercises the shipped inference engine is skipped or deselected, and `pytest` REPORTS SKIPS AS SUCCESS. The daily automated publish is gated on a suite that CANNOT FAIL for an engine regression.** ⭐ **The most silent-failure-conscious codebase in the corpus ships behind a silent pass — the discipline is applied everywhere the USER could be hurt and nowhere the PROJECT could be.**

**⭐ WHERE THE MACHINERY ACTUALLY IS: NOT HERE.** `__init__.py:38-48` binds exactly **FOUR** C symbols (`needle_init`, `needle_complete`, `needle_reset`, `needle_load`). **The tool-retrieval head is in the binary** — Python's whole contribution is passing `tool_index_path` through `needle_init` (`:64, :89`), and **the "5" is not in this repository**; so is the **byte-level grammar**; so is inference-time **confidence** (the JAX side has `ConfidenceHead` at `architecture.py:463-488`, exported at `export.py:289`, but the score you read comes from the blob's JSON envelope). **The JAX code here is the TRAINING/EXPORT/REFERENCE side; the INFERENCE side is the blob** ⇒ **v242's D25 applied to a COMPONENT rather than a subject: the vault verified the tool-retrieval claim EXISTS IN DOCUMENTATION, not that it works** — there is **no benchmark data, no eval harness and no reproduction script** anywhere in the repo (the README's *"trades wins with FunctionGemma 270M, LFM2.5 230M and Apple FM"* is backed only by `assets/frontier.png`). **🔴 Do NOT cite its benchmark numbers.**

**🔴 THREE README CLAIMS THE CODE DOES NOT SUPPORT.** **(1) THE CONTEXT WINDOW.** README:13 says *"a 256-token sliding window with the tools pinned as KV sinks."* `architecture.py:597-611` derives the window from an **11.5 MiB BYTE BUDGET** (`KV_BUDGET_BYTES = 11*1024*1024 + 512*1024`, `KV_GROUP=32`, `KV_WINDOW_MIN=160`), clamped to `max_seq_len` (default **2048**) — **⚠️ The configuration that matters is a named PRESET, not the dataclass defaults** (`architecture.py:38-43`: `needle` = d_model 768 · 12 heads · 6 kv-heads · **27 layers**; `base` = 512 · 8 · 4 · **27 layers**; the dataclass defaults `d_model=512, num_layers=12` match **NEITHER**). **COMPUTED: `needle` preset → per_pos 25,056 → **480 tokens**; `base` → 16,704 → **704 tokens**.** Meanwhile the `256` all over the API is **`max_new_tokens`, the OUTPUT cap** (`__init__.py:109,125,147,165`). ⚠️ **The SHIPPED config is NOT VERIFIED** (`export.py:20-30` — `kv_window`/`kv_bits` ride inside the `.cact` header). **Surviving claim: the real bound is a byte budget, not a token count, and it is not 256.** **(2) THE QUANTIZATION.** README:5 *"compressed to **CQ2-bit**"* vs `export.py:5-7` *"Format is **W4A8**: … Cactus-Quants **INT4**; norms, Hadamard diagonals and gates stay FP16"*, and `cli.py:156` `--bits` ∈ {2,4} defaulting to 4 — two numbers describing **different artifacts** (the distributed model vs what `needle build` emits), and no document says so. **(3) THE PAPER.** README:23 cites **arXiv:2607.18363** for *"our Simple Attention Network findings"*; the paper is **real with a matching author list** but is titled **"A Controlled Study of Attention-Only Transformers"** (submitted 2026-07-20, scale range **6M–87M** which brackets 45M), and its reported result is that removing feed-forward layers **INCURS A PERFORMANCE COST**, substantially but not fully recovered by reallocating to attention depth, the residual gap concentrated on *"tasks requiring knowledge retrieval from weights rather than context."* ⚠️ **Precision:** the paper studies *attention-ONLY* stacks while Needle uses a **Hadamard MLP in place of** the FFN; whether the ablations cover that variant is **NOT VERIFIED**. **Defensible statement: the citation supports the architecture less enthusiastically than the README's framing implies.**

**🔴🔴 THE TRAINING PROVENANCE EXISTS ONLY IN A GITHUB TOPIC TAG.** The README explains the architecture down to the update rule (Walsh-Hadamard transform, Sinkhorn iteration, engram sites at two layers, sandwich-normed gated residuals) and says **NOTHING about what the base model was trained on**: `grep -rn -iE "distil|teacher|trained on|gemini|gemma"` across the tree returns **ZERO** hits for the base model — every "dataset" reference is about **your** fine-tuning JSONL — and the words *gemini* and *gemma* appear **NOWHERE in the repository**. **But the repo's GitHub topics are `cactus`, `gemini`, `gemma`, `llm`, `on-device-ai`** (PAGE-STATED), and third-party coverage describes Needle as *"a 26M-parameter model distilled from Gemini 3.1"* (secondary source, **NOT** a project claim). **⇒ The only thing in the entire project connecting Needle to Gemini is a TOPIC TAG — the one piece of metadata not in the git tree, not versioned, and invisible to anyone who clones.** ⚠️ Distillation is ordinary and may be fully licensed; **this is a due-diligence gap, NOT an accusation** — the checkable point is that **the training provenance of a model marketed for commercial on-device deployment cannot be established from its repository.** ⭐⭐ **EXACT INVERSION OF v244**, where the affiliation lived in **1,674 CI-enforced headers** while `GOVERNANCE.md` named it **zero** times ⇒ **both projects put a load-bearing identity fact in the one place their own tooling does not check.**

**⭐ WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD.** **`llms.txt` (202 lines) is the strongest agent-facing API contract the corpus has read** — *"This file is written for AI coding assistants. It is enough to write correct Needle code without reading the source. **Copy the patterns; do not invent API that is not listed here.**"* — with a **"Behaviour contract (important for correct code)"** section and a **"Common mistakes to avoid"** section, i.e. it documents the **failure modes an agent will hit**, not just the API surface (clean instance-strengthening of **Library-vocab #12 "LLM-routing artifacts", CONFIRMED N=5+**). ⚠️ **But nothing keeps it in sync** — README + `llms.txt` + `doc/apis.md` are **three hand-maintained restatements of one API with NO precedence statement and NO CI check** (the **v245 D32** situation *without* the D32 sentence; optional fields with no evidence are omitted, not guessed"*) is a **training-time property asserted in prose, NOT enforced in code** — test it, don't assume it. **⭐⭐ #83 HONEST-DEFICIENCY-DISCLOSURE, IN FOUR PLACES:** fine-tuning does not update the confidence head, so an agent built with `weights=` reports **`confidence` as `None`** (`__init__.py:57-60,122`) — disclosed in `llms.txt`, in `doc/apis.md`, in a **runtime `warnings.warn`**, and in **the fine-tune job's own stdout** ⇒ **a disclosure that the product's two headline features DO NOT COMPOSE** (tune it for your tools, *or* gate on calibrated confidence — not both), delivered at the moment of the mistake. **A 2nd #83:** `doc/finetuning.md:64` states the shipped `--epochs` default of **3** *"barely moves a rank 16 adapter"* and tells you to use **10–30**. **⭐ SECURITY: NO broken-auth triad** — playground defaults to **`127.0.0.1`** (`cli.py:174`, port 7860), **zero CORS handling**, and it calls `complete()` not `run()` so it **does not execute user Python** (`server.py:29-40`); **⭐⭐ THE CORPUS CONTRIBUTION — THE TOOL-CATALOGUE THREAD REACHES THE MODEL LAYER AND SPANS TWO LAYERS FOR THE FIRST TIME.** Every prior treatment was at the **harness** layer: **v167 audit** (the vault's own **~54K tool-catalogue floor**), **v238 dsh-anchored-standard** (blank the auto-injections; Anthropic ships it first-party as `defer_loading`, 77K→8.7K on request #1), **v245 Unsloth** (**measured** it — *"~28k tokens of which ~18k is System tools"* — and named `--tools` as the flag that restricts schemas). **Needle 2 is the FIRST subject in the corpus to move the problem into the WEIGHTS:** a learned retrieval head selects the **top-5 tools from a large declared catalogue per turn** and the grammar is then constrained to that subset, **so the catalogue never has to fit in the prompt at all** ⇒ **N=4, three harness-layer instances + one model-layer instance.** ⚠️ **With the §4 caveat: the head is in the binary and nothing in this repo measures whether it works.**

**MINT DECISION — NO MINT, on five independent grounds, three of them the vault's own written discipline.** The candidate would have been *"Sub-100M On-Device Tool-Calling Foundation Model Shipped as an Agent-Callable Library with Constrained Decoding."* **(1) The MODEL-TIER RULE binds and this is its 5th data point** — `_patterns/06:171` (v176 GLM-5) verbatim: *"**NO §C standalone minted** — a single goal-adjacent frontier model is not a recurring capability class; §C vocab is **tool/capability-shaped**"*; `_patterns/06:199` (v193 TimesFM) **DECLINED** a *"corpus-first time-series-forecasting FM"* mint on the same reasoning. **The Model/Inference-Substrate tier → descriptive N=5** (GLM-5 v176 · DeepSpec v186 · TimesFM v193 · PixelRAG v211 · **needle v246**; bookkeeping only). **(2) NOT world-first, in a crowded band** — FunctionGemma 270M, LFM2/LFM2.5, Apple FM on-device, Octopus v2, plus the Gorilla/ToolLLM/xLAM/Hammer line; the README names three of them as peers; grammar-constrained decoding is **standard practice** (llama.cpp GBNF, Outlines, XGrammar, Guidance, JSON mode). **What IS distinctive is SCALE — and scale is a number, not a class** (~5–6× below the smallest widely-cited peer) ⇒ a corpus-knowledge data-point, the **PixelRAG v211** discipline. **(3) domain-not-capability** (phones/wearables/smart-home/robots — the **meetily v196 / AIRI v210** discipline). **(4) §28 anti-inflation** — no cluster to join, no N=2 partner. **(5) The distinctive machinery is NOT IN THE SUBJECT** (see above) — minting would mean minting a class on prose describing unread code. **COLLISION CLEAN:** zero prior corpus mentions of cactus-compute / Needle / Henry Ndubuaku / Cactus Quants (hand-grep + agent, agreeing). **Pattern #57: NONE** — no dependency edge to any prior corpus subject.

NO MINT; counts 46/11 UNCHANGED; §C live standalones 51 unchanged; surface ≈58 unchanged.** **COLLISION CLEAN** (hand-grep: `ego-lite|citrolabs|ego.app|ego-browser` = **zero** prior hits in `CLAUDE.md`, `_state/`, `_patterns/`, `PATTERN_LIBRARY.md`). **Pattern #57: NONE.**

**⭐⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE — IT DECLARES THE BOUNDARY THE LAST THREE SHIPS HID, AND IT COSTS ONE SENTENCE.** The browser is closed; the repo is MIT; and the project says so **unprompted, in the two files a reader and an agent open first**: `README.md` (License) — *"The contents of this repository are released under the MIT License. **The ego lite browser is a separate, free download.**"* — and `AGENTS.md:3-5` — it drives the browser *"through `globalThis.ego` bindings (**provided by the closed-source ego lite app**)"*, and *"This repo contains the open-source harness and the agent skill package — **not** the browser itself."* ⭐⭐ **Against v244 → v245 → v246 this CLOSES A SET OF FOUR**: OpenSandbox **over-asserted** an identity its governance doc never named; Unsloth **under-asserted** one its packaging enforced; needle **SPLIT** one across two repos and never mentioned the restrictive half in 44 files; **ego lite splits one and declares it.** It is the counter-example the set needed. **⭐ CONSEQUENCE (v242 D25 applied to a component):** the README's differentiator — *"the strongest page Snapshot on the market … thanks to **kernel-level customization** … reliably handles deeply nested iframes"* — **is not in this repository.** `src/driver/observe.ts` is ~139 lines and calls `browserEgo().snapshot(options)`, a method of the binary; zero iframe traversal, zero AX-tree construction, zero "kernel-level" anything in the open code (`observe.test.mjs` contains zero references to snapshot or iframe). 🔴 **Do NOT cite this repo as evidence of snapshot or iframe innovation.**

**⭐⭐⭐ THE THESIS — THIS PROJECT WRITES EXCELLENT CHECKS AND DOES NOT CONNECT THEM.** Its own doctrine, `CONTRIBUTING.md` §12 "The Four Principles", **Goal-Driven Execution**: *"Translate the task into a verifiable goal; **write the check first**, then iterate until it passes."* Then: **`scripts/mutation-check.mjs`** = **real mutation testing**, hand-rolled ~370 lines on `acorn` (parses compiled JS, injects operator flips / return swaps / boundary shifts into *named focus functions*, runs that module's tests, reports kill rate), and its `MODULE_MAP` targets **exactly the predicates whose silent failure does damage** — `isAgentOwned`, `findMatchingTaskSpace` (is the agent about to seize the human's Space?), `boxModelCenter` (is the click landing on the element or the viewport corner?), `isStaleBackendNodeError`, `hasReturnStatement` — ⇒ **WIRED TO NOTHING** (verified: `grep -rn "mutation" .github/ lefthook.yml CONTRIBUTING.md AGENTS.md` = one unrelated DOM-mutation line). **`scripts/validate-agent-style.mjs`** = the rarer artifact, **a style linter whose target is the prose that instructs a language model** (lints `SKILL.md`, `README.md`, every `learnings/**/*.md` and every e2e case for fixed-coordinate `page.mouse.click(x,y)`, `page.waitForTimeout(>=1000)`, `page.locator("text=")`, `page.evaluate(String.raw + querySelectorAll)`; `agent-style-ok` escape) — **not** prose-vs-code (v240) but **prose-vs-DOCTRINE** ⇒ **WIRED TO NOTHING.** ⚠️ **I suspected it was theatre and was WRONG** — the e2e layer is Playwright-compatible, 122 occurrences of those patterns exist across the linted files, and there is exactly **one** suppression, with a stated reason (`cases/helper-surface.mjs:80`, a deliberate `text=` compatibility assertion) ⇒ real, targeted, hand-tuned, unwired. **By contrast `validate:site-skills` — the check on the DATA FORMAT — is wired in all FOUR places** (`ci.yml`, `quality-gates.yml`, the publish job, and the pre-commit hook). ⇒ **They wired the check on the data and left the checks on their own doctrine unwired.**

**⭐⭐ THE E2E PLACEMENT IS THE *RIGHT* ANSWER TO v246'S PROBLEM.** v246 needle shipped a daily automated PyPI publish behind `pytest -q -m "not slow"` where every engine-touching test skipped or was deselected and **pytest reports a skip as success** — a gate that could not fail for the thing being shipped. ego lite has the same structural problem (its real tests need a closed macOS browser that cannot run on `ubuntu-latest`) and solves it in the **opposite direction: it moves the test to where the dependency exists** — `lefthook.yml` runs **seven pre-commit gates** and the last is `e2e-test: npm run e2e`, the real-browser suite, on the developer's machine. CI then runs only what it can honestly run (prettier on changed files, `npm audit --audit-level=moderate`, `tsc --noEmit`, `npm test`, `validate:site-skills`) and **nothing in CI pretends to have exercised the browser.** ⭐ **THE PORTABLE RULE: put the test where the dependency is, and let the gate claim only what it ran.** ⚠️ **The honest caveat (mapping pass):** a pre-commit hook is opt-in (exists only if `npm install` ran `prepare` → `lefthook install`), bypassable with `--no-verify`, and **the e2e requirement is not disclosed in `CONTRIBUTING.md`** ⇒ a **silent contract**; nothing anywhere proves the browser suite ran before a merge.

**⭐⭐⭐ THE SHARPEST FINDING — A COMMITTED GATE THAT 66 OF 82 MERGES CONTRADICT.** `.github/workflows/main-pr-source.yml` is nine lines and one rule: *"Pull requests into main must come from the dev branch"* (fails any PR into `main` whose `github.head_ref != "dev"`). Added **2026-06-01** (`aefa07f`, *"Require developer branch for main PRs"*), and it **is** an ancestor of `main`. Measured against the history it governs: **82 PR merges into `main` since 2026-06-01 · 16 from `citrolabs/dev` · 66 from branches the gate is written to reject — including HEAD itself** (`#248 from citrolabs/section9-lab-patch-3`), plus `#249`, `#247`, `#164`, `#147`, `#141`, `#124`, `#114`, `#112`, `#106`, `#103`… And **four sources of truth about one process, no two agreeing**: the workflow says *from `dev` only*; `CONTRIBUTING.md:322` agrees (*"merge features into `dev` … then merge `dev` to `main`"*); **`CONTRIBUTING.md:283` contradicts both** (*"**Branch from latest `main`**"*); `lefthook.yml`'s `branch-up-to-date` hook gates on **`origin/dev`**; and the topology shows **`main` and `dev` have DIVERGED — `main` 32 ahead, `dev` 20 ahead, `main` at PR #248 vs `dev` at #128**. ⇒ **Follow `CONTRIBUTING.md:283` — branch from latest `main`, which is what a cloner gets — and the project's own pre-commit hook blocks your first commit (main is not a descendant of dev), then the CI gate rejects your PR (your head ref is not dev).** ⚠️ **What is NOT claimed:** whether the workflow is configured as a *required* status check — that lives in GitHub branch-protection settings, **not in the tree**. **This is v244's D28 run in REVERSE ⇒ NEW RULE D34: a committed CI rule is not an enforced one; presence of a gate says nothing about whether it is required.** No accusation — a measurement: *the rule this repository commits and the history this repository records disagree 66 times.* **⭐⭐ AND THE DETECTOR IS PORTABLE — this ship's method contribution alongside v246's `grep -rni "silent" .`: TAKE A GATE'S OWN PREDICATE AND TEST IT AGAINST THE HISTORY IT WAS SUPPOSED TO GOVERN.** *A gate you have never seen fail is not a gate you have seen pass.*

**⭐⭐ THE VERSION FACT EXISTS IN FIVE PLACES AND THE ONE MACHINE THAT WOULD RECONCILE THEM HAS NEVER RUN.** `SKILL.md` frontmatter `version: "1.2.6"` (`date: "2026-07-20"`) · `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` plugin `1.2.5` · `.codex-plugin/plugin.json` `1.2.5` · that same marketplace `metadata.version` `1.0.0` · `package.json` `0.1.0` (name **`ego-browser-v2`**) · newest tag `v1.3.1-beta.6`. `publish-ego-browser-skill.yml` **rewrites `SKILL.md`'s `metadata.version` from the git tag** at publish time, which would make one copy authoritative — 🔴 **but it has NEVER EXECUTED: it triggers on tags matching `[0-9]+.[0-9]+.[0-9]+` (NO leading `v`), and all 21 tags are `v`-prefixed (18 matching `v*.*.*`) or legacy two-component (`1.1`, `1.2`, plus a mutable `latest`) ⇒ ZERO tags match the trigger.** So the version normalisation, the **token-leak scanner**, the dry-run, the post-publish verification and the SHA256-pinned CLI download have all sat unexecuted since the workflow landed. ⚠️ **This CORRECTED MY OWN framing** (I had credited CI with keeping the version honest — my signature error shape: *inferring that a mechanism is operative from its existence*), and the corrected version is better because it **explains** the drift instead of noting it. ⭐ **And they have been here before:** `322b20b` *"chore: align Codex and Claude plugin versions"* aligned the two manifests **by hand**, and they have since drifted from `SKILL.md` again ⇒ **exactly v245's D32 case: hand-alignment does not hold, and there is no precedence sentence.** ⚠️ The documented install paths are unaffected (`npx skills add citrolabs/ego-lite` reads GitHub directly; the `.dmg` is a CDN download) — what never happened is the **registry** publish to ClawHub + SkillHub.

**⭐⭐⭐ THE DOC LEDGER AND A REFINEMENT OF THE VAULT'S OWN D22.** Five verified defects, **all in human-facing docs**: **(1)** `CONTRIBUTING.md:6` links `skills/ego-browser/SKILL.zh.md` — **deleted** at `1a7f293` *"Delete skills/ego-browser/SKILL.zh.md"*; **(2)** `CONTRIBUTING.md` attributes the Four Principles to `AGENTS.md` (*"see `AGENTS.md`"*) and **`AGENTS.md` contains none of them** (grep for all four names returns only `CONTRIBUTING.md`); **(3)** `CONTRIBUTING.md:46,198,274` + `package/ego-browser/README.md:66` teach refs as **`@eN`** — the exact format **`AGENTS.md:17` explicitly flags as wrong** (*"refs are numeric `backendNodeId`s (`@21`, **not `@e21`**)"*) ⇒ **the repo's own docs commit the mistake one of its docs warns against**; **(4)** `AGENTS.md:33` names `scripts/run-e2e.sh`, absent from the tree (in history at `f4ae5dc`/`6c443f8`/`44d19a7`; the file is now `run-real-browser-e2e.mjs`); **(5)** `AGENTS.md:41` describes `npm run e2e` as the *"task-space e2e suite (`src/taskspace-e2e.test.mjs`)"* while `package.json` maps `e2e` → `node scripts/run-real-browser-e2e.mjs`. **And `SKILL.md` — 209 lines, the file that ships to every agent — carries NONE of them** (uses `@N` correctly throughout; every path it references resolves). ⇒ ⭐⭐ **D22 SAID AGENT-FACING PROSE GOES STALE FIRST. HERE IT IS THE FRESHEST ARTIFACT IN THE REPOSITORY AND THE DEVELOPER-FACING PROSE HAS ROTTED IN FIVE PLACES — same repo, same authors, same 73 days: a controlled comparison. NEW RULE D35: prose goes stale in proportion to how little MACHINERY and how few READERS touch it — not by whether its audience is a human or a machine. The variable is CONSUMPTION, not audience.** (`SKILL.md` is read on every agent run, is what CI rewrites, is what publishes to two registries, and its errors surface immediately; `CONTRIBUTING.md` is read by almost nobody and checked by nothing.) ⚠️ **The vault application is exact and uncomfortable:** `CLAUDE.md` is read every session and is maintained; the `_state/03c-**v183**` filename label and the `_patterns/06`↔shim divergence are the two lowest-contact surfaces — and **the v246 E3 error (a stale shim premise fed to 14 agents) is the same mechanism.**

**⭐⭐ THE BEST AGENT-FACING CONTRACT IN THE CORPUS — AND ITS ONE SILENCE.** `skills/ego-browser/SKILL.md` beats v246's `llms.txt` on the merits because it governs **behaviour**, not just calls. Three things worth stealing: **(a) THE WRITE PROBE** — *"Before writing substantial content into a rich editor, perform a tiny **write probe**, then verify it … If the probe appears in the title bar, toolbar search, hidden input, or any wrong field, **stop using DOM/input helpers for that surface**"* ⇒ **v246's doctrine at the instruction layer**, converting *"I filled the form and the document is unchanged"* from a confident wrong answer into a detected one, and its second half is the part everyone omits: **on failure change TECHNIQUE, not parameters**; **(b) FAILURE AS THE CORRECT OUTCOME** — *"A 'user is controlling' error is a **hard stop on the whole task** — not an obstacle to route around … **Honoring it *is* the correct outcome here; pushing the goal forward anyway is the failure.** The only thing you may do is ask the user and wait"*; **(c) A TABULATED OWNERSHIP MODEL** — every Task Space is `agent | agentDelegatedToUser | user`, with a per-helper policy table for user-owned Spaces and *"Check `done` before telling the user the handoff is finished."* 🔴 **THE TENSION: a prose guardrail on an unguarded primitive** — the same table records that **`takeOverTaskSpace` has NO ownership check**, and the mitigation is a sentence (*"**Never** call `takeOverTaskSpace` on your own … it will seize the browser away from the user"*). Verified in code: `helpers.ts:347-353` selects the Space and calls `ego.takeOverTaskSpace()` with no ownership test; the JSDoc at `:130` admits it. ⇒ **the single most consequential action in the system — an agent taking the browser from the human using it — is prevented only by an instruction addressed to a language model: the EXACT INVERSE of v246's rule** (*where you cannot make a failure loud, move the setting into the artifact so it cannot be set wrong*). ⚠️ Fairly stated: an escape hatch is needed to resume after a handoff — but the guard could be a required argument, a handoff token, or a refusal when ownership is `user`, and it is none of those. 🔴 **AND THE SILENCE: NOT ONE WORD ABOUT A HOSTILE PAGE.** The product loop is *read an untrusted web page → an LLM decides → it writes JavaScript that runs against the user's authenticated sessions*, and `grep -niE "malicious|hostile|untrusted|prompt inject|do not follow|instructions on the page"` across `SKILL.md` + `AGENTS.md` + `CONTRIBUTING.md` returns **NOTHING**; there is **no `SECURITY.md`**. ⇒ **A 209-line skill reasons at length about one adversary — an impatient agent that might trample its user — and says nothing about the other: the page.** ⭐ And the means to close it are already in the repo: `validate-agent-style.mjs` proves they will lint agent-facing prose for patterns they consider harmful.

**⭐ IT IS A PLAYWRIGHT-SHAPED FACADE, AND `help()` IS GENERATED FROM THE CODE.** `helpers.ts:780-822` assembles the surface as **named facades** — `page`, `locator`, `browser`, `taskSpaces`, `site`, `fetch` — and `FACADE_HELP` documents a deliberately **Playwright-compatible** API (`page.locator()`, `getByRole/getByText/getByLabel/getByPlaceholder/getByTestId`, `waitForURL/waitForResponse/waitForLoadState`, `page.keyboard.*`, `page.mouse.click`, and on locators `filter/first/nth/check/selectOption/evaluateAll`), plus six `cases/playwright-*.mjs` modules. ⇒ instantly learnable; it explains the style linter's rules; and ⚠️ **it makes the README comparison table closer to apples-to-apples than the table implies** — Browser-Use, Vercel's agent-browser and ego lite are all Playwright-shaped, and the real difference is the browser underneath plus the ownership model. ⭐⭐ **AND `help()` IS THE REPOSITORY'S ONE DRIFT-PROOF DOCUMENT:** `src/help-runtime.ts` parses the **built bundle's** JSDoc with `acorn` **at runtime** to answer `help(name)` — as `AGENTS.md:23` puts it, *"JSDoc on exported helpers is therefore user-facing documentation."* The agent-facing reference is not a copy of the code, it **IS** the code ⇒ set against five hand-carried version strings and five rotted doc claims, **the one surface a machine generates is the one surface that cannot be wrong.** (⚠️ **NOT VERIFIED / E4:** a name-by-name inventory of `SKILL.md`'s helpers against the code — the surface is assembled indirectly through facades, and a grep cannot test it; recorded unverified rather than published.)

**⭐ SECURITY — THE BOUNDARY IS DRAWN WELL; THE RESIDUAL RISK IS THE PREMISE. NO BROKEN-AUTH TRIAD, STRUCTURALLY:** `ego-browser` opens **no port and no socket** — the transport is `globalThis.ego.sendCDPMessage`, a function the app injects (`browser-runtime.ts:27-35`; `installEgoSdk(globalThis)`). ⭐ **It notably declines the usual shortcut of exposing Chrome's `--remote-debugging-port`** — precisely the failure mode this corpus documented at **v231 CoreOfPotato** and **v232 gemini-web2api** (`0.0.0.0` + wildcard CORS + auth failing open while holding live authenticated sessions). ⚠️ Consequence for a reader: **the authorization model lives entirely in the closed app and cannot be audited** — the open layer cannot be faulted for lacking auth and cannot be credited with having it. 🔴 **The residual risk is the product's own premise:** inside a Space inheriting the user's logins, `js()` is `Runtime.evaluate` (arbitrary JS in the authenticated page), **`browserFetch()` issues requests from the page context and returns the body** (`http.ts:29-52`) ⇒ arbitrary authenticated reads, exfiltratable to any origin; `serverFetch()` fetches from Node with a spoofed `User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0` default; `uploadFile()` puts local files into a page; `driver/downloads.ts` pulls files down. **With the §SKILL silence, prompt injection from page content IS the whole threat model, and it is unaddressed.** Two precise smaller items: **`.env` is auto-loaded from TWO locations** (`env.ts:47-48` — repo root *and* `agentWorkspace()`, i.e. `EGO_BROWSER_AGENT_WORKSPACE` or the installed skill dir) so whatever `.env` sits beside the installed skill becomes environment for agent-authored JS (mitigating: only sets currently-undefined vars); and **validating a site-learning EXECUTES it** — `learning/validate-learning-format.ts:66` does `await import(pathToFileURL(toolPath).href + "?validate=" + Date.now())`, so `validate:site-skills` (CI + publish + pre-commit) imports every learning's JS with a cache-buster ⇒ ⭐ **correctly configured as `pull_request`, NOT `pull_request_target`, so fork PRs run WITHOUT secrets, and the publish job runs only on tags — the right choice, worth saying so.**

**⭐ SUPPLY CHAIN — MID-TABLE WITH TWO STANDOUT PRACTICES.** ⭐ **Exactly ONE runtime dependency: `acorn ^8.16.0`** (+9 devDeps) — no Playwright, no Puppeteer, because the CDP transport is the binary's; and `acorn` is **reused three ways** (`mutation-check.mjs`, `extract-help-docs.mjs`, `help-runtime.ts`) rather than duplicated, consistent with their **Simplicity First** principle. ⚠️ The trade is explicit: the dependency surface is small *because* the heavy code is closed. ⭐ **`npm audit --audit-level=moderate` runs in BOTH the pre-commit hook and CI.** ⭐ **The strongest single line in the release path — a token-leak scanner over the artifact about to be published:** `grep -R -E '(clh_|skh_|pt-)[A-Za-z0-9_-]{16,}' "$RELEASE_DIR"` → *"Release archive contains a token-like value."* → `exit 1`, scanning for **its own registries' token prefixes**, failing closed (⚠️ never run — see above). ⭐ **A mutable URL made immutable by a committed hash:** the SkillHub CLI is fetched from a Tencent Cloud bucket at `…/install/latest.tar.gz` and verified with `SKILLHUB_CLI_SHA256: af9e0763…` piped through `sha256sum --check -` ⇒ **the correct way to consume a `latest` URL, and it fails closed when upstream rotates — better than v246's "pinned-but-unverified over TLS" and far better than v234's plaintext `http://`.** ⚠️ Gaps: deps **caret-ranged, not pinned** (lockfile present); `npx -y clawhub@0.21.0` version-pinned but not hash-pinned; `prepare` installs git hooks into `.git/hooks` on a dev `npm install` (skipped when `CI=true`, documented in `lefthook.yml`'s header); and **the `.dmg` URL is an opaque fixed filename with no version in it** (`egolite-Y7MbxKIuhzFB.dmg`) ⇒ **you cannot pin, diff, or name what you installed.** Behind pi v228 (pinned + `save-exact` + `min-release-age` + `--ignore-scripts` + shrinkwrap).

extension, corroborated by HEAD being a merge commit): **Claude 91 lines across five model strings** — Opus 4.8 (1M context) ×36, Opus 5 (1M context) ×21, Opus 4.8 ×15, **Fable 5 ×11**, Opus 5 ×4, Opus 4.7 ×4 — plus Copilot App ×10. ⚠️ **BOTH the key form and the value form were counted** (v245's error was a key-form grep missing 104 value-form lines). **And NO policy asks for them** — / 165 commits · v246: 21 · **v247: 102**). ⭐ Branch names carry the provenance instead: of 70 refs, **15 are `codex/*`** plus one `agents/playwright-style-refactor-v2` — the v242 pattern (*built with
