**⭐ CLAIMS AUDIT.** 🔴 ***"up to 2.5× faster"*** vs Vercel's agent-browser on *"four complex tasks"* = **backed by exactly ONE PNG** (`docs/assets/ego-vs-agent-benchmark.png`); no data file, no task list, no harness, no reproduction script in 150 files; README says *"Check the comparison."* **with no link. DO NOT CITE.** ⚠️ **Sharper than v246's equivalent: ego lite HAS a 24-module / 31-case real-browser harness and did not use it for the one number in its README.** 🔴 *"substantially fewer tokens"*, *"higher task success rates"*, *"far fewer tool calls per task"* — unsupported by any artifact. ⚠️ ***"up to 5× faster"*** describes a feature the same table marks **"(coming soon)"**. 🔴 The mechanism claim (*"composing a multi-step task into a single output instead of a call-two-commands-look-at-the-result loop"*) — **`run.ts:108-131` performs no batching**: it wraps the agent's code in an `AsyncFunction` and each `await` is a CDP round-trip; *"the agent writes code"* is conflated with *"we batched operations."* ⚠️ **Experience accumulation:** the consume-side is real (`src/learning/`, 701 lines across 3 files: discover, validate, execute) but **nothing in this repository WRITES a learning** — the only `writeFile`/`mkdir` calls are fixtures in `learning/index.test.mjs`; the two shipped packs (`google/`, `x-com/`) are hand-curated ⇒ ⭐ **the README's "(coming soon)" label is therefore ACCURATE — honest labelling, not a false claim.** ⭐ **And the `learnings/` FORMAT is genuinely good:** a typed per-site capability manifest (`id`, `name`, `domains` with wildcards, `notes[]`, `nodeTools{}`/`browserTools{}` each with `description`/`path`/`callable`/typed `args` with `required` + per-arg descriptions/`returns`) = **an MCP-style tool schema for a website, stored as files**, validated by the one check they wired everywhere, which also **rejects temporary `@N` refs** so a learning cannot encode a throwaway snapshot ref. ⚠️ **Comparison table:** mostly defensible as a *category* claim; **"Reusable skills — Browser-Use: —"** is contestable because Browser Use ships its own MIT Claude Code skill (**this corpus's v198 video-use**) — fair under a narrow reading (*per-site machine-consumable capability packs*), misleading under the plain reading; **"Free — Atlas/Comet: —"** compares its free tier against competitors' subscription tiers.

**⚠️ PRIOR ART — NOT WORLD-FIRST (the mint's decisive ground).** Each component is occupied: *a daily-use browser whose agent reaches your real logins* → **Anthropic's Claude in Chrome**, **ChatGPT Atlas**, **Perplexity Comet** (the README's own table concedes Atlas/Comet inherit Chrome data); *isolated parallel workspaces in one browser* → **Arc Spaces** (the name is literally Arc's), **Firefox Multi-Account Containers**, **Chrome profiles**, and the entire **anti-detect** category, whose product *is* multi-profile isolation (**CloakBrowser v69**, **camofox v179**); *a browser drivable by an external agent* → **CDP/Playwright**, **Playwright MCP**, **Chrome DevTools MCP**, **browser-use v41**, **Vercel agent-browser**, Stagehand/Browserbase. ⚠️ **And a live competitive fact: Arc and Brave are shipping first-class agent APIs, Arc's with a declarative JSON permission system for what an agent may touch — a control ego lite does not have.** **What IS distinctive is narrower than the marketing: the per-Space ownership state machine** (`agent | agentDelegatedToUser | user` with `handOff`/`takeOver`/`claim`/`waitForAgentControl` as first-class operations, a tabulated policy, and a doctrine naming deference as success) — I did not find that primitive elsewhere, ⚠️ **but per the vault's own discipline an absence of evidence is NOT evidence of firstness** (the argument a v246 agent got wrong and had rejected).

**MINT — NO, on four independent grounds** (the collision agent and the critic reached NO MINT independently): **(1) form-factor-within-a-genre** — a browser is a product genre; ruled twice, **lobehub v222** (*fame is not a mint*; world-canonical ≠ world-first) and **hermes-webui v227**; **(2) a combination is not a capability class** — all three components occupied, §C vocabulary is tool/capability-shaped; **(3) the distinctive machinery is NOT IN THE SUBJECT** — the same ground on which v246 declined; **(4) §28** + the N=1 gate. ⭐ **RECORDED NOT EXECUTED — the losing alternative:** the strongest framing is not the browser but the pattern, **"Human+Agent Shared-State Co-Habitation with Per-Workspace Ownership Handoff"**, genuinely repeatable beyond browsers (an IDE, a terminal multiplexer, a shared design canvas) ⇒ **DEFERRED watch axis at N=1; a promotion is an audit act** (the v232 rule). ⭐ **Instance-strengthening, recorded not incremented:** **Library-vocab #12** (agent-facing/LLM-routing artifacts, CONFIRMED N=5+) via `SKILL.md`, and the **cross-harness packaging** family (four targets from one canonical skill). ⚠️ **NOT a palmier-pro v192 instance** — that row (N=5, promotion-flagged) requires a **first-party MCP server** and a **retrofit**; ego lite ships **a skill, not an MCP server** (verified: no MCP server anywhere in the tree) and was **built agent-first from the start**. **Both halves of the row's name fail ⇒ do NOT count v247 toward it.**

**⚠️ THE COMMERCIAL TIER — A SUSPICION TESTED AND DROPPED.** CitroLabs sells a subscription **`ego`** (the full personal agent) plus a **Business** tier; `ego (lite)` is the free community edition — and the repository mentions this **nowhere** (verified: no `enterprise|subscription|pricing|commercial|premium` hit across all 148 files outside unrelated test identifiers). Given the §1 framing I expected a second quiet omission; **it is not, and the fair finding is the opposite.** `lite.ego.app/enterprise` prices the free tier at *"$0 forever"* and the Business tier as *"priority support with response SLA, custom integrations and guided onboarding, volume and deployment terms"* = **services, not withheld features**; no capability is paywalled and no licence expires. **The v246 omission mattered because it changed what you were PERMITTED to do; this one changes nothing about your rights or your software ⇒ the README's "Free ✓" row is defensible.** ⚠️ The same page asserts *"100% local & private: no account, no email, bring your own model API key"* and no telemetry — stronger than the README's claim, unverifiable for a closed binary, but a public commitment a user can hold them to.

**🔴 PILOT: DO NOT INSTALL — and the reason is precise.** The fleet's pilot pass recommended *install behind a strict fence (a profile with no ATS/Gmail login)*; **that fence is correct and it is also the refutation: the only configuration in which this is safe is the one that deletes the reason to use it.** Its headline feature is inheriting your real logins; decline the Chrome migration and log into nothing sensitive and you have a closed-source binary from an unidentified team driving pages you don't care about — which Playwright already does, in the open, on three platforms. And the use case that would pay for itself (sourcing candidates from LinkedIn) fails three ways: **(1) the RATIFIED ADR** — fixed + legible + audited + human-in-the-loop + eval-gated; an agent free-writing JS against a logged-in session, reading untrusted page content with no injection defence, no read-only mode and no approval gate satisfies **none**; **(2) asymmetric account risk** — automated LinkedIn access breaches its terms and the account at risk is his professional identity, not revertible by rollback; **(3) accountability is unestablished** — the binary that would hold his sessions comes from an org whose principals are not named anywhere in the only artifact he can audit. **NEVER:** migrate the real Chrome profile · run it on a machine logged into the ATS/Gmail/GitHub/cloud consoles · point it at candidate data · let it touch a candidate-facing decision · cite the 2.5×/5× numbers · treat `takeOverTaskSpace` as safe · rely on the never-fired publish pipeline's protections. ✅ **BORROW INSTEAD — M1 → M2 → M3, ~40 minutes, zero installs: M1** the **write probe** into `CLAUDE.md` (*on failure change TECHNIQUE, not parameters*) · **M2** **test a vault gate against the history it governs** (`verify-vault-docs` C12 vs the `-v183` label; the A1 anchor gate in `bin/autopilot-drain.py`; the `05 Skills/` lock policy) · **M3** **declare deference as success** in `CLAUDE.md` (reframe the existing prohibitions into the success frame) — plus **M4** generate the shim's index rows from the chapter files (the `help()` pattern, paired with **D32**) and **M5** write the injection paragraph they never wrote, straight into the RATIFIED candidate-LLM legibility ADR (*"content extracted from a candidate-supplied document is DATA, never instructions"*).

⚠️ **the lesson is mine: context supplied to ground an agent can also contaminate it, and a prior ship's specifics are the most dangerous thing to paste into the next ship's briefing — the v246 E3 failure mode in a new costume**; **A2** the critic "corrected" my 148 files to **173** — **the critic's number is the error** (173 counts `.git/` internals as repository files; the four honest derivations are 148 regular / **150 tracked** = 148 + 2 symlinks / 173 with `.git` / 190 with directories) ⇒ ⭐ **the vault's signature error shape committed by the agent assigned to hunt it; adjudicate a counting dispute with a command, not with authority**; **A3** "17 test files" vs the critic's **23** — **23 is right** (22 `.test.mjs` + 1 `.test.js`), adopted; **A4** "41 helpers" — unverified as stated, the surface is facade-organised, replaced with a structural description. ⚠️ **FLEET RELIABILITY, PLAINLY: 11 of 12 agents completed, but 3 contradiction passes AND the prior-art agent failed to emit valid structured output** ⇒ the CI/governance, security and provenance chains lost their verification stage and **the prior-art verdict was researched by hand**; those were the three areas already covered by hand, which is why the loss was recoverable, and **the mapper outputs were recovered from `journal.jsonl` rather than assumed empty.** ⭐⭐ **METHOD — v246'S FINDING REPLICATES AND THE FIX WORKS.** v246 concluded that agents asked to *check a claim* rubber-stamp it (7 CONFIRMED of 8 against a *"default to REFUTED"* brief) while agents asked to *read the code* caught the lead's worst error. This ship acted on it: the verify stage was rebuilt as a **CONTRADICTION** stage — each agent received the mapper's report as a *suspect document*, was told its job was to produce corrections by independent reading, was required to open and confirm at least six specific citations, and had to file a **read receipt** naming files and line ranges. It produced corrections and read receipts rather than confirmations. ⇒ **THE RULE: do not ask an agent whether a claim is true; ask it what the claim gets wrong, and make it show you what it read.**

**NEW RULES THIS SHIP: D34** *a committed CI rule is not an enforced one* (v244 **D28** in reverse; detector = test a gate's predicate against the history it governs). **D35** *prose goes stale in proportion to how little machinery and how few readers touch it — not by audience* (refines **D22**; evidence = a within-repo controlled comparison, the shipped `SKILL.md` clean while five developer-doc claims rotted).

**Workflow:** 14 agents authored (5 map → 5 pipelined contradiction → 3 situate → 1 critic); **11/12 completed, 1 errored, 3 empty-result, ~1.53M subagent tokens, 393 tool uses, 817 s.** `Workflow` **stable across nine consecutive ships** (schema-compliance the weak link, as at v242's 3 schema failures). **Streak: v246 `GA:104` → `GA:105 · OG:13 [7 ov]`** (**28 consecutive GA**, v220→v247); **§35 CLEAR** (window {v245 GA, v246 GA, v247 GA} = 0 OG). ⚠️ **The ~v221 audit is now 35 ships overdue** (last v212; v213–v247 all shipped) and gains three items from this ship: the new watch axis, **D34**, and **D35**.

Docs `03 Projects/ego-lite - Beginner Analysis/` ((C) Deep Dive + (C) Verdict + (C) Pilot Methods Menu + wiki.html). Shipped on `wiki/v247-ego-lite` off the v246 tip (`4321bee`); **not auto-merged.**

## v249 — arc-task-gen (pathwaycom / Ludovic Arnould) — 2026-08-19 — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 [(a) FAIL §41 · (b) MODERATE keys the tier ⚠️STRONG-reviewable · (c) STRONG ⚠️tempered · (d) STRONG] — **NO MINT; counts 46/11 UNCHANGED; §C live standalones 51 unchanged; surface ≈58 unchanged**

**Subject.** `pathwaycom/arc-task-gen` — *"ARC-AGI-1 Task Generator: Distribution-Matched Tasks for Model Evaluation."* MIT, "Copyright (c) 2026 Pathway". A tool that prompts a frontier chat model (default `gpt-5.6`, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint) to **invent** ARC-AGI-1-style puzzles, one per API call, so a model can be scored on tasks it cannot have memorised. It accompanies **BDH-CQ** (arXiv:2608.09888, submitted 2026-08-10) — Pathway's 150M-parameter recurrent-latent-reasoning model — and its press launch. ✅ **SOURCE-CLONED TWICE, byte-identical** (`diff -r --exclude=.git` → 0). HEAD **`20b2203064b09f60f7925a191d75c11d72277f35`** (2026-08-11 11:52:10 +0200). **13 tracked files / 2,139 lines** (`generate_tasks.py` 905 · `generate_tasks_stratified.py` 508 · `label_eval_tasks.py` 238 · `describe_eval_tasks.py` 131 · `visualize_tasks.py` 108 · `instructions.md` 177 · `README.md` 58). **12 commits** on `HEAD` and on `--all` (identical); **TWO git roots** (`1a90ea7`, `841753d`, both 2026-08-04) ⇒ **D19 EXTENDED, count the roots**. Sole author **Ludovic Arnould** `<ludovic@pathway.com>` (9+2+1). Page-stated §37.4, **NOT API-verified**: 3.6k★ / 21 forks / **1 watcher** / 1 open issue / 0 PRs — a launch-attention signature (3.6k stars, one watcher).

**⭐⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE — THE CONTAMINATION IT EXISTS TO DEFEAT IS WORSE THAN IT SAYS, AND I MEASURED IT MYSELF.** The premise (`instructions.md:5-9`) is diffuse: the eval set *"appears in web-scraped training corpora."* The concrete channel is not mentioned anywhere in repo or paper. The tool's **only open issue — #1, `maurathat`, 2026-08-15, still OPEN, no maintainer reply** — claims 375/400 eval tasks sit in ARC-AGI-2's public **training** split, undetectable by hashing, attributing it to pair reordering + D₄ + colour permutation and warning that task-ID matching cannot be relied on. **I cloned `fchollet/ARC-AGI` and `arcprize/ARC-AGI-2` and tested six cumulative levels** (`leak.js`/`spot.js`, Node — ⚠️ **`python3` is SIGKILLed by this sandbox, exit 137, even for `print("hello")`; `node` and `perl` work**):

| Level | Rule | A1-eval found in ARC-AGI-2 `data/training/` |
|---|---|---|
| L0 | same filename / task id | **376 / 400** |
| L1 | byte hash | **0 / 400** |
| L2 | JSON-canonical hash | **0 / 400** |
| L3 | + demonstration pairs as an unordered set | **375 / 400** |
| L4 | + D₄ symmetry (8 transforms) | **375 / 400 — adds nothing** |
| L5 | + colour permutation | 371 (4 false negatives from my own tie-group cap ⇒ **L4's 375 is the sound figure**) |

**Controls:** A1-*training* → A2-training **386/400**; A1-eval → A2-**eval** **6/400**; **A2-eval → A2-training 0/120** (clean negative control). **Mechanism, exactly:** of the 376 shared ids, **375 carry an identical demonstration-pair multiset** (same grids, same colours, no rotation, no recolouring), **0 are byte-order identical**, **all 375 are reordered-only**, and **all 375 land on the SAME task id** (1 shared id, `ac0c5833`, genuinely differs). ⇒ **the issue is RIGHT about the number and WRONG about the reason** — it is pure pair reordering, D₄ and colour permutation contribute zero, and it is detectable with `ls`, so the issue's own ID-matching caveat is false for this pair. **Worked example `00576224`:** ARC-AGI-1 eval holds train pairs [A,B]; ARC-AGI-2 training holds [B,A]; **and the test pair is byte-identical in both files INCLUDING its output** — i.e. ARC-AGI-2's public training split ships the answer, and the same holds for all 375. ⚠️ **NOT concealment by ARC Prize:** `arcprize/ARC-AGI-2` `readme.md:31` does say the training set *"combines tasks from ARC-AGI-1 as well as new tasks"* — what it never says, there or in `changelog.md`, is that this includes **375 of the 400 ARC-AGI-1 *evaluation* tasks**, one line away from describing an eval split as for *"models that have never seen these tasks."* **Disclosed with the load-bearing half omitted** — the v246 shape (a load-bearing fact where the reader will not look).

**⭐⭐ AND THE PAPER'S OWN TRAINING MIXTURE REACHES THE SAME SET FROM A SECOND DIRECTION.** §4.2 verbatim: *"The dataset combines privately curated examples with publicly available data from the ARC-AGI-1 training set, RE-ARC, ConceptARC, ARC-Heavy, and **ARC-GEN100K**. We apply additional augmentations."* **No overlap analysis anywhere in the paper.** I checked the named sources: **RE-ARC** (Hodel, arXiv:2404.07353) = generators for ARC-AGI-1's **400 training tasks only** — clean. **ARC-GEN** (Google, Apache-2.0, arXiv:2511.00162) — I cloned it: `task_list.py` enumerates **900 distinct task ids = all 400 A1-training + 328 of the 400 A1-EVALUATION + 172 others**, and its README says ARC-GEN-100K covers *"all four-hundred tasks"* without saying **which** 400. ⚠️ **VERIFIED:** the generator suite named in the paper's training mixture publishes generators covering **328 of the 400 eval tasks the paper reports 29.5% on.** ⚠️ **NOT ESTABLISHED:** whether the ARC-GEN100K artifact Pathway ingested draws on that subset. **NOT an accusation and NOT a finding of contamination** — the sufficient claim is that the headline number sits on a set two of the paper's own named public sources demonstrably reach, and **no document performs the check**, which is exactly what issue #1 closes by asking.

**⭐⭐⭐ THE INVERSION — THE HONEST NUMBER EXISTS, IT IS HIGHER, AND IT IS IN AN APPENDIX.** I first framed this as *"the tool shipped; the honest number did not."* **That was MY error and I caught it by reading the paper.** Appendix A **Table 6** (verified twice, independently prompted): **Public ARC-AGI-1 400 / 118 / 29.5%** · **Calibrated generated 400 / 149 / 37.2%** · **Mechanic-stratified generated 1,131 / 337 / 29.8%**. The 400-task cohort is `generate_tasks.py --n 400`; the 1,131-task cohort is `generate_tasks_stratified.py --mechanics all` (§A.2: *"Every stratified task was authored by GPT-5.6 from a prompt naming the target mechanic."*), and **Table 7 breaks it across the tool's exact 16 mechanics with Wilson CIs, Flood fill 68.6% → Gravity and stacking 2.9%**. ⇒ **the model scores 7.7 points HIGHER on the set built to be uncontaminated** — the direction *inconsistent* with memorisation inflating the public figure, i.e. **the strongest evidence in the package for their own claim, and it is in Appendix A.1 while the contaminated number is in the abstract, the README, the chart and the press release.** ⚠️ **It proves nothing alone:** equally consistent with the generated set being **easier**, and **nothing in this tool measures difficulty** (it matches six surface statistics); the authors correctly decline the inference (§A.1: *"The generated cohorts serve different experimental purposes and are not directly comparable"*). ⚠️ **Direction note:** an ill-posed generated task is one the solver **loses**, so the disclosed ~5% unsolvable rate means 37.2% **understates** ability and **widens** the gap. ⭐ **The most interesting number is 29.8%** — the harder, evenly-stratified cohort landing 0.3 points from the public figure. ⭐⭐ **And the tool's real contribution, which its own README never states: the point of a distribution-matched private set is not to restate the aggregate, it is to BUY STATISTICAL POWER IN CELLS THE REAL BENCHMARK CANNOT FILL** — 400 public tasks cannot support a per-mechanic estimate, 1,131 evenly-allocated ones can, and the answer is a **24× spread**. The docstring's `--mechanics all --per-mechanic 94  # full powered design` is a power calculation.

**⭐⭐⭐ "INDEPENDENT REPRODUCTION" HOLDS FOR NONE OF THE THREE NAMED PEOPLE.** `README.md:54` heads a section **`## Independent Reproduction`**. `:56` credits **Łukasz Kaiser** — whom **Pathway's own blog lists among the company's "investors and advisors"** while quoting him endorsing the work; the README omits the affiliation. `:58` says the results were *"also **independently** reproduced by Remigiusz Kinas … and Richard Zhong"* — **both are authors 8 and 9 of the 9-author paper** (Engdahl, Kosowski, Chorowski, Stamirowska, Uznański, Jiang, Phadke, **Kinas**, **Zhong**). ⭐ **Git records the direction of travel:** commit `b1ff64c` rewrote *"also reproduced by Richard Zhong"* → *"also **independently** reproduced by Remigiusz Kinas … and Richard Zhong"* — **the word was ADDED in the same edit that added a co-author.** And **Pathway's own blog post never uses "independent"/"independently" about any reproduction and never mentions Kinas** ⇒ **the independence claim is STRONGER in the developer-facing repository than in the company's press release**, the opposite of the usual direction. ⚠️ **NOT claimed:** that the reproductions did not happen (Kaiser stated publicly he *"replicated their ARC-AGI-1 results myself"*), or that the result is wrong. The finding is narrow and verified: a section headed *Independent Reproduction* names one investor/advisor and two co-authors and calls two of them independent.

**⭐⭐ THE CHART ADMITS A CROSS-SET COMPARISON WITH A LEGEND GLYPH.** `assets/Pathway_ARC-AGI_result_chart.png`, read by cropping the regions: **legend — hollow circle = "Public Eval Set", filled = "Semi-Private Eval Set"**; **all three BDH-CQ markers (Low/Medium/High) are HOLLOW**; **GPT-5.6 Luna (Low) is FILLED at 34.2% @ $0.008**. **SECURITY — essentially NO attack surface in the artifact:** one Markdown file, one PNG, a stdlib-only script, one workflow; no server/port/CORS/credentials/dependencies/install path ⇒ **the v231/v232 broken-auth triad is STRUCTURALLY impossible.** Workflow read line-by-line: `permissions: contents: write` correctly scoped; `actions/checkout@v4` + `actions/setup-python@v5` **tag-pinned not SHA-pinned** (low, real); **triggers are `schedule` + `workflow_dispatch` ONLY — no `pull_request` trigger, so a fork PR never reaches a write-scoped token; the obvious injection path does not exist.** The script interpolates regex-captured `owner`/`repo` into an `api.github.com` URL with capture classes `([^/\s]+)`/`([^)\s]+)` — a crafted entry *could* inject path segments; **worst realistic outcome is an unintended GitHub API path queried with a repo-scoped token and a wrong star badge — the token is in a header, never the URL, and the host is fixed. **⭐⭐⭐ THE OPERATOR PAYOFF — THE SEGMENT-ALIGNMENT PROBLEM, DEFENDED AT FIVE LAYERS.** Send N regions to a model in one request; if the returned list is shifted by one, merges two, or drops an empty one, **every subsequent item is attributed to the wrong region and nothing crashes** (manga: a character speaks someone else's line; **hireui: one candidate's employer attached to another's degree**). Every backend defends it: **(1)** items carry a stable index (`indexed_texts`); **(2)** the contract is stated as machine-checkable rules — `mmt_core/prompt_studio.py:31–36` *"Preserve every page key exactly as provided / Preserve item count exactly / Preserve item order exactly / Do not merge, split, drop, or invent items / Do not add explanations, notes, markdown, or commentary outside the structured result"*; **(3)** the expected count is interpolated into the request — `gemini_translator.py:373` *the `"translations"` array must have exactly `{len(texts_to_translate)}` items*, `:276–277` *keep exactly the same page names / the same number of bubbles per page*; **(4)** the response is validated in every backend (`deepseek:238,516` · `gemini:396,640` · `local_llm:186` · `openai_compatible:344,384` · `batch_orchestrator:65` · `context_memory:91`) **and `openai_compatible_translator.py:355`/`:396` check the per-item INDEX, not merely the count** (*"response item index mismatch at position {expected_index}"* — a count check passes a swap); **(5)** the fallback preserves alignment over translation — `deepseek_translator.py:450` *"If response length mismatches, pad/truncate with originals."* ⭐ **Why layer 4 is load-bearing, in the code's own shape:** reconciliation is `zip(indexed_texts, translations)` (`deepseek:476` · `gemini:201` · `local_llm:195` · `context_memory:94`) and **Python's `zip` silently truncates to the shorter sequence** — the length check at `context_memory.py:91` sits three lines above the `zip` at `:94` for exactly that reason. ⭐⭐⭐ **Untranslated-but-correctly-placed beats translated-but-shifted** — the call most implementations get wrong, and **the most transferable thing in the repository: it discharges the eval-gating clause of the RATIFIED candidate-LLM legibility ADR, and the test it implies (mutate the model's response — drop one, duplicate one, reorder two — and assert the guard fires) needs NO ground-truth corpus**, which is what has been blocking that clause.

DeepSeek-OCR is a *document* OCR model, so pointed at a speech bubble it returns document structure: the filter's `STRUCTURED_TAG_MARKERS` are `("<table","</table>","<thead","<tbody","<tr","<td","<svg","<path","<math","<figure","<chart")`, it recursively unwraps JSON payloads (bounded at `depth > 3`), detects coordinate geometry by counting numeric-pair matches, and returns `OCRTextFilterResult(text, rejected, reason)` with **named reasons** — `empty_ocr_output` · `structured_json_non_text` · `structured_markup_non_text` · `coordinate_geometry_non_text` · `structured_hallucination_non_text`. ⭐⭐ **And it is scoped honestly:** `if provider_key != DEEPSEEK_PROVIDER_KEY: return OCRTextFilterResult(text=cleaned, rejected=False, reason="")` — **a no-op for every provider except the one whose failure mode it was written against.** ⭐⭐⭐ **This is the v246 `silent` doctrine independently re-derived:** the naive pipeline would typeset a plausible HTML table into a speech bubble and ship it; this converts a confident wrong answer into a **loud, named rejection carrying its cause.** ⚠️⚠️ **v246 `silent` DETECTOR: ZERO — fourth consecutive null, and I RAN it** (also zero for *âm thầm* / *im lặng* / *lặng lẽ*) — **and the most instructive of the four, because the doctrine is unmistakably present in the code and simply absent from that vocabulary.** v253: *the domain is artifacts that RUN* → refuted by v254. v254: *artifacts whose authors have DEBUGGED them* → refuted by v255. v255: *artifacts whose authors WROTE DOWN their reasoning about failure* → **and this author did exactly that, in five reason-strings and a commit-message obscenity, and the grep still returns zero.** ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FOURTH CORRECTION: the detector finds an ENGLISH WORD, not a discipline. Its four nulls measure vocabulary, and on a Vietnamese-authored codebase it is structurally blind.** ⭐ **Portable fix: grep the reason-strings, not the adjective** — `rejected` / `reason=` / `_non_text` / `mismatch` found this file instantly.

FALSE, and a fleet agent caught it pre-publication:** `.gitignore` was added by **`7a590cb` 2026-05-22 13:08** while the **18 `.pyc` came with the root commit `71951c5` 2026-04-26** (18 of its 45 files) ⇒ **twenty-six days apart.** In v256 the two genuinely did arrive together (`bdcb098` 2026-05-13 00:27:46 adds both `.gitignore` and `translator/test_translator.py`). ⭐⭐⭐ **The corrected finding is sharper: the author sat down on 22 May, wrote a `.gitignore` naming `__pycache__/`, and left eighteen already-tracked `.pyc` exactly where they were — no `git rm --cached`, in the five commits that followed. The rule was authored AFTER the violation and never applied to it.** ⇒ **what replicates across the two repos is the OUTCOME, not the mechanism** — and two unrelated routes to the same dead artifact is better evidence of a *disposition* than one repeated slip. **Sixteen of the eighteen are ordinary staleness** — the same 8 `src/` modules compiled **twice**, `cpython-312` and `cpython-313`, a fossil of the author changing Python versions and committing both times. **The other two have no source in the repository in any commit:** `manual_prompt_studio_v1.cpython-313.pyc` (79,818 B) and `_v2.cpython-313.pyc` (92,842 B). `strings -a` on both returns **`tkinter`** and **`ttk`** ⇒ ⭐ **both abandoned generations were Tkinter**; and `_v1` already contains `build_prompt`, `import_response`, `validate_response`, `refresh_review_queue`, `run_local_step`, `build_segment_glossary_local`, `build_segment_pronouns_local`, `assemble_volume`, `chapter_glossary_extract`, `chapter_relationship_extract` ⇒ ⭐⭐ **the entire pipeline vocabulary, including the deterministic local steps the README presents as the product's exclusive feature, was already in place in a prototype that was never published.** **The measurement that keeps it honest:** of the **117** `def` names in the tracked `manual_prompt_studio.py`, `_v1.pyc` shares **5** and `_v2.pyc` shares **51** ⇒ `_v2` is **not** that file compiled but an **earlier state of the lineage that became it**, and the file has since more than doubled **while still calling itself v2**, inside a repo whose README is titled v3. ⚠️ **Name-presence is weak evidence about behaviour and no behavioural claim is made.**

**⭐⭐⭐ ONE POLICY, THREE THRESHOLDS, AND THEY DISAGREE.** The intent is good — ask the model for a confidence score, route low-confidence output to a human. **Declaration 1:** `config/config.json`'s `dialogue_labeling` block declares `review_confidence_threshold: 0.72`, `auto_accept_confidence_threshold: 0.82` and **four** conditions `force_review_if_unknown_speaker` / `_unknown_listener` / `_multiple_possible_speakers` / `_no_matching_pronoun_rule`. 🔴 **That file is read ONLY by `src/config_loader.py:6` and `src/main.py:19` — generation 1.** Generation 3 reads a **different** file, `project_config.json`, via `workspace.py:22–27` ⇒ **the canonical policy file is orphaned from the documented application.** (⚠️ A fleet agent claimed the exact inverse; re-verified by grep, mine stands.) **Declaration 2:** `manual_workflow.py:117–118` and `manual_prompt_studio.py:528` hardcode **0.72 / 0.82** as literals and inject them **into the prompt** as `dialogue_labeling_config` ⇒ **the model is told the thresholds.** **Declaration 3:** `review_flags.py:101` and `:104`, plus `editor_actions.py:455`, test **`confidence < 0.8`** ⇒ **what the application actually enforces.** ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **The model is told 0.72/0.82; the app enforces 0.8; the file that declares the canonical pair is not read by the app at all. Three copies, three locations, and the enforced value matches NEITHER declared value.** And the four `force_review_if_*` rules appear in **ZERO** of the 47 `.py` files. ⚠️ **I first recorded this as "declared and not implemented" — WRONG:** `review_flags.py` is a **real 139-line service** emitting `ReviewFlag(severity, source, item_id, message, payload)` aggregated per segment and per volume. **The defect is triplication with disagreement, which is worse than absence, because each copy looks authoritative alone.** ⚠️ **The adversary's steelman, recorded:** in a render-and-paste architecture, telling the *model* the thresholds is legitimate design and code-gating would be a different product. **Accepted for declarations 1–2 and it does not rescue the position** — declaration 3 *does* gate in code at a different number, so the project is not abstaining from enforcement but enforcing an unpublished value; and the four conditions are **rules, not thresholds**, absent from the prompt as well as the code ⇒ **a design that delegates a decision to the human still has to tell somebody the rule, and these four are told to nobody.**

**⭐⭐⭐ THE GATE THAT CANNOT FIRE.** `ArtifactStore.upsert_jsonl` (`artifact_store.py:25`) writes `row.update({"item_id": item_id, "status": "success", "result": obj})` — **the status is a literal, assigned at write time**, recording *that a row was written*, not *that the content was right*. Two release paths read it: `release_builder.py:354,364` and `release_service.py:140,150`, both `if row.get("status") != "success": continue`. **And the ONLY code in the repository that can write `"failed"` is `src/pipeline.py:28` — generation 1**, returning `{"item_id": iid, "status": "failed", "error": str(e)}` when its API call raises. ⇒ **In generation 3 — the generation the README documents and `run.bat` launches — the sole writer of that field is a constant, so the gate can never exclude anything, and nothing about it looks broken.** (Also `"tentative"` ×3 for human-added entries, a genuinely good three-state design.) ⭐⭐ **THE RULE: a gate can outlive its signal source.** v250 aimed a gate at the wrong thing; v252 labelled unautomated rules *"Automated"*; v256 kept artifacts whose context had been deleted; **v257 is a correctly-written, twice-consumed gate reading a field whose only varying writer belongs to a generation that is no longer the product.**

**⭐⭐⭐ THE DURABILITY CLAIM AND ITS READER — the fleet's best find, which I had walked straight past.** The README's data-safety section is headed *"Cơ Chế Nạp Dữ Liệu & Khôi Phục **Siêu Bền Bỉ**"* (*super-durable loading and recovery*) and argues for the JSONL row format on exactly this ground: one JSON object per line *"makes reading and writing extremely independent, avoiding one line's error ruining the entire large data file."* The reader is `jsonio.read_jsonl`: **a list comprehension with a bare `json.loads` and no per-row `try`** ⇒ 🔴 **one malformed line raises `JSONDecodeError` and the caller loses EVERY row in the file** — precisely the failure the format was chosen to prevent, argued for by name one section above. **Blast radius is the whole app:** `artifact_store.upsert_jsonl`, `progress`, `review_flags` and `editor_index` all read through it, so one corrupt line takes out that artifact's history, its progress calculation and its review flags together. ⚠️ **Also the README's own example row is `{"item_id": "seg_001", "status": "done", …}`** while the code writes `"success"` and both gates test `!= "success"` ⇒ **the documented schema value would be silently skipped by the gate that reads it.**

**⭐⭐ WHAT IS GENUINELY GOOD, AND IT IS MORE THAN EXPECTED.** ⭐⭐⭐ **ONE ESCALATION PATH IS FULLY CLOSED, AND THE MODEL OPENS IT:** `prompts/03_build_segment_glossary.txt:11` instructs that if an important term appears in the segment but is not in the volume glossary, put it in **`missing_glossary_candidates`** *for human review*; `review_flags.py` reads exactly that field and raises a `warning` flag the UI surfaces. **Prompt, schema and gate all agree on one string, and the loop runs from the model's own uncertainty to a human's screen** — the single best thing in the repository and the pattern the three thresholds failed to achieve. ⭐⭐ **The prompts are strong** (read from the shipped screenshot's rendered prompt): a role line, `{{genre}}` injected, explicit **scope fences** (*do NOT translate the novel; do NOT merge relationship data here; do NOT overwrite existing canon*), a **precedence rule** (existing canon outranks chapter-level guesses), a **conflict protocol** (mark contradictions as conflict, group near-matches as aliases — never overwrite), **two-tier status semantics that tell the model how a DOWNSTREAM model will consume the field** (`confirmed` = force this exact term; `tentative` = reference, may adapt), and a strict output contract (JSON only, no markdown, no fences, no comments, `null` when unknown, `[]` for empty, confidence 0–1). ⭐⭐ **Every canon entry carries its own provenance** — from the Editor screenshot's raw-JSON panel: `source_items: ["c001","c002"]` per variant plus `appears_in: [1,2]` ⇒ **each entry records which chapters and volumes it came from**, i.e. **the v256 "artifact carries its own context" rule SATISFIED here by the same author who violated it four times next door.** ✅ `response_parser.py` (57 lines) strips ```` ```json ```` fences and, on failure, `_extract_outermost_object` walks the string with correct quote-and-escape handling — the right algorithm, not a regex guess. ✅ **Secrets posture CLEAN and I tried to refute it:** `config/config.json` stores **`"api_key_env": "DEEPSEEK_API_KEY"`** (the *name* of the variable), `.env.example` is a one-line `sk-...` placeholder, `.gitignore` covers `.env`, no key anywhere in tree or history. ✅ **Progress is derived purely from files on disk** (no cached state to drift), the Calibre push uses **list args, no `shell=True`, `check=False` and inspects `returncode`**, `ebooklib` is imported inside a `try/except` at call time with a Vietnamese install hint, `release_service` computes `missing_segments`/`missing_count` before publishing, and `series_canon` **appends and logs conflicts rather than overwriting** existing series entries.

**🔴 DEFECTS BEYOND THE HEADLINES.** The **3-level prompt override exists** (`workspace.py:34–44`: `prompts_root` walks `root/prompts`, `parent/prompts`, `parent.parent/prompts`, first that exists) **but resolves a DIRECTORY, not a FILE**, and `prompt_engine.load_prompt` has no `try/except` ⇒ **overriding ONE template per project appears to require copying all 13**, and nothing says so. **Silent degradation:** `prompt_engine.render` reads `00_json_output_policy.txt` and, if absent, sets `json_policy = ""` and renders anyway ⇒ **a missing output policy yields a prompt with no JSON contract, with no warning.** **`jsonio.write_json` is a plain `path.write_text`** — no temp-and-rename, **not crash-atomic**, against a README that promises safety *"even if you lose power or the machine hangs."* **The README MISATTRIBUTES the `.bak` mechanism** to `manual_studio/core/workspace.py`; it is at `jsonio.py:39–42` (`shutil.copy2` + `%Y%m%d_%H%M%S`), called from `series_canon.py:607` and `artifact_store.py:34,65,71,79`, with a **duplicate implementation** at `manual_prompt_studio.py:30–31`. **`manual_prompt_studio.py` (52KB) is reachable from nothing** — not the README, not `run.py`, not `run.bat`, not the `.spec`. **`src/main.py` exposes 17 verbs, `run.py` invokes 13** — the four unexposed (`extract-glossary`, `extract-relationships`, `merge-glossary`, `merge-relationships`) are plausibly the primitives that `glossary-prep`/`relationship-prep` compose, so **recorded as probably-sensible, not asserted as a defect.**

Two projects side by side, one tended and one not.** ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **THE FINDING: THE HABITS ARE THE CONSTANT; THE QUALITY IS THE VARIABLE.** Everything that replicates is **bookkeeping**; everything that diverges is **care applied to a particular surface**. **Discipline attaches to whatever the developer was thinking about; structure fails everywhere else** — a more useful model of AI-assisted solo development than either repository alone could support, and the reason a same-author control was worth a ship.

**⭐⭐ NO ALIGNMENT VALIDATION ANYWHERE (extent stated).** `grep -rn --include=*.py -E 'len\([^)]*\) *[!=<>]=+ *len\(|mismatch|expected .*items|same length'` across **all 47** `.py` files returns **nothing**; `response_parser.py`, read in full, validates exactly one property — **that the response parses to a JSON object.** ⚠️ **The FAIR reading, and it is genuinely fair:** the UI button is labelled **"Kiểm Tra Cú Pháp"** (*check syntax*) and the README promises *checking the response syntax* ⇒ **by v256's own rule — an unenforced check is a defect only when something claims it is enforced — this is a GAP, not a LIE.** But it is the gap that matters most for the operator, and it is the axis on which the **same author's other repository is materially better.**

**⭐ THE ACTIVE VOLUME CANON — the idea worth taking.** `series_canon.py:124` `build_active_volume_glossary` concatenates the volume's chapter+segment text into one `source_text`, then keeps each series entry when **`any(term in source_text for term in terms)`** (`:133–134`), where terms = the entry's `source` plus declared `aliases` (`glossary_entry_match_terms`, `:487`). ⭐ **Retrieval by PRESENCE rather than by similarity** — no vector store, no threshold, no index; for a bounded named-entity KB a genuinely good trade, and directly applicable to (i) hireui matching and (ii) **the vault's own ~54K tool-catalog context problem.** ⚠️ **Structural false negative:** an entity present only as a pronoun or under an undeclared alias does not match and is dropped from the prompt exactly when most needed; `build_active_volume_relationships` (`:324`) is stricter — a relationship survives only if **both** parties matched. Nothing counts or reports the drops, **which is also why the 80% figure cannot be checked from outside.**

**METHOD.** Orchestrator-first: two clones + `diff -rq` both ways; `git rev-list`/`--max-parents=0`/`shortlog` (D39); `git check-ignore --no-index`; `git log --all --diff-filter=A` for every never-existed claim; `strings -a` on the orphan bytecode; **both shipped screenshots read as images** (which settled the architecture, the review column and the provenance schema); then a **16-agent `Workflow`** (5 map → 5 contradiction → 3 situate → 3 check → critic → adversary; 14 done, 2 errored, ~2.05M tokens, 483 tool uses, 14m26s). **ERROR LEDGER — 4 MINE:** 🔴 **(1) the `.gitignore` timing** — asserted by analogy with v256 without checking; **false**, 26 days apart; **a fleet agent caught it and the anti-critic then repeated my wrong version back as "Established GT confirms…"** ⇒ ⭐⭐ **a ground-truth block handed to a fleet is an AMPLIFIER: one unchecked assertion propagated into sixteen agents and returned wearing the authority of confirmation. **⭐⭐⭐ CODE MOVES FORWARD IN TIME, NEVER BACKWARD.** The per-item alignment guard is the corpus's own borrowed pattern from v256, so its travel is measurable. **INVENTED in v256** at commit `67af566`, **2026-05-15 23:38** (subject: `New`), introducing `"OpenAI-compatible response item index mismatch at position {expected_index}."` **CARRIED into v258:** `vocra_core/translator/openai_compatible.py:173` checks `len(items) != len(originals)` and `:181` raises **`"Translator item index mismatch at position {expected_index}."`** — same guard, near-identical message, in a repo created **2026-05-26**, eleven days later; plus two further independent paths (`run_translator.py:77`, `vocra_translator/core/translation_service.py:135`) and count checks in the video pipeline itself (`frame_extractor.py:209`, `segmenter.py:375`). **NEVER REACHED v257:** `grep -rn --include=*.py -E 'index mismatch|len\(...\) != len\(...\)'` across **all 47** of v257's `.py` files returns **nothing (exit 1)** — and v257 was committed to **five times on 2026-05-22 and once on 2026-05-27 17:13**, every one after 2026-05-15. ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **he touched the novel tool six times after inventing the guard, including on the last recorded day of all three repositories, and never backported it.** ⚠️ **THE STEELMAN, and it partly holds:** v257 is render-and-paste — a *human* carries the prompt to a chat model and pastes the reply back — so there is no in-process request object to compare against, and its button honestly says *check syntax*; **a literal port is genuinely harder there.** ⚠️ A fleet agent argued the guard is therefore *"inapplicable, not forgotten."* **Answered:** v257 renders a numbered batch and imports a JSON reply, so **the COUNT of returned items is checkable against the count sent, and it is not checked** ⇒ **the barrier is not architecture alone; it is that nothing in a copy-forward workflow ever runs in reverse.** ⇒ **THE GENERALISATION: in a solo multi-project toolchain an improvement invented in project N reaches N+1 by copy-forward and never reaches N−1, because no shared library, package, dependency or CI carries it back. The oldest repository keeps the oldest mistakes permanently, EVEN WHILE BEING ACTIVELY EDITED.** Copy-forward is a one-way ratchet, and this is the whole argument for extracting a shared library: **it is the only mechanism that makes a fix travel backwards.**

**⭐⭐ THE CARRIED-OVER SUBSYSTEM GOT SMALLER AND GAINED AN ABSTRACTION — AND ITS BUG RODE ALONG UNCHANGED.** v256's OCR/inference layer: **5 ad-hoc files, 1,342 lines**, no shared base (`chrome_lens_client.py` 199 · `paddleocr_vl_client.py` 303 · `llama_cache.py` 138 · `llama_server.py` 459 · `ocr_providers.py` 243). v258's `vocra_core/final_ocr/`: **8 files, 971 lines**, with **`base.py` (19 lines)** defining a `FinalOCRProvider` **Protocol** (`provider_key`, `validate`, `recognize_image`, `close`, `metadata`) and **`provider_factory.py` (17 lines)** dispatching on a provider string and **`raise ValueError` on unknown**. ⇒ ⭐ **same subsystem, third project, 28% fewer lines and an actual interface** — direct evidence for the correlation above. 🔴 **And the defect came with it verbatim:** v256 `mmt_core/llama_server.py:221` and v258 `vocra_core/final_ocr/llama_server_manager.py:131` are the same two functions line-for-line — an `os.name == "nt"` branch calling `os.startfile`, and an `else` branch calling **`subprocess.Popen(["sh", str(bat_path)])`: the POSIX shell invoked on a Windows `.bat`** (both also `xdg-open` for the folder case). **⭐⭐⭐ LATE ADDITIONS FROM THE FLEET, ALL THREE VERIFIED BY ME — and the first is the ship's best positive.** **(1) AN INVALIDATION MECHANISM THAT ACTUALLY ENFORCES, completing a three-point arc the corpus has circled since v250.** `segmenter.py:_invalidate_downstream_outputs()` does not warn, it acts: it **deletes** the downstream cache files (`ocr_final`, `translation`) via `cache_path.unlink()`, then resets **four** status flags (`preprocessed_done`, `ocr_final_done`, `translation_done`, `export_done`) to `False` and persists them with `save_progress`. ⇒ **v256 wrote `DOWNSTREAM_STALE_STAGES` into its cached JSON, showed a GUI warning, and enforced NOTHING; v257 had NO staleness mechanism at all; v258 DELETES THE ARTIFACTS.** ⭐⭐⭐ **The repository with the most written-down reasoning is also the only one of the three that enforces its own invalidation — an independent confirmation of the ship's correlation, from a completely unrelated surface, and found by the fleet rather than by me.** **(2) 🔴 THE TIMEOUT IS ON THE WRONG CALL.** `burner.py` invokes ffmpeg two ways: `_run_capture` (`:582–583`), a **short probe**, is `subprocess.run(…, timeout=timeout)` with `timeout` a **required keyword-only parameter**; `_run_ffmpeg_stream` (`:534`), **the long-running video encode**, is a `Popen` followed by a bare **`process.wait()` with no timeout at all** ⇒ **the call that finishes in milliseconds is guarded by a mandatory timeout and the call that can run for hours has none**, so a stalled ffmpeg hangs the encode indefinitely. **Not ignorance of the parameter — the author made it compulsory in the helper directly below** ⇒ ⭐ **the same shape as everything else in this ship: the discipline exists and was applied to the surface that did not need it.** **(3) ⚠️ THE SSIM FILTER IS GREEDY-SEQUENTIAL, WHICH BOUNDS THE 90% CLAIM.** `ssim_filter.py:78` compares each frame **only** against `last_unique_image`, the reference advancing only on a miss (`:88–89`) — no rolling history. So a subtitle that disappears and **reappears** (A → B → A) yields three "unique" frames and the second A is OCRed again. ⭐ **It is the right algorithm for the common case** (a subtitle sits still, then changes) and it under-deduplicates on repeats ⇒ **the removal rate is a property of subtitle RUN LENGTH, not of the number of distinct subtitles, so "90%+" describes the input rather than the filter.** ⚠️ **Also recorded:** `draft_ocr.py:61–76` has deduplicated frames inherit their leader's OCR text via `frame_map` **with no check that the leader succeeded**, so an empty leader silently loses the subtitle for that whole run. ⚠️ **AND ONE FLEET CLAIM REJECTED, with the reason:** an agent reported `exporter.py:152` (`centis = int(round(millis / 10.0))`, clamped to 99) as a precision defect. **It is not — ASS timestamps are `H:MM:SS.cc`, so centiseconds are the format's own resolution**; the rounding is required and the clamp is a correctness guard. Recorded because it is exactly the class of "defect" that looks real until you read the specification.

## **v261 novel_studio (2026-08-21) — `mranex/novel_studio` — GOAL-ALIGNED INCLUDE 3/4 · NO MINT · counts 46/12 UNCHANGED**

**"Novel Translation Studio"** — an offline, single-user application for semi-automatically translating serial novels (Chinese → Vietnamese) under tight human control of glossary, character relationships, pronouns and dialogue attribution. Text is split into **skeleton → item → sub-item with stable IDs** and each unit translated with a prompt carrying exactly the context it needs. FastAPI backend (62 endpoints), React + React Flow frontend, a **Tkinter source-preparation sub-app**, OpenAI-compatible providers, file-based per-project storage. **The FIFTH `mranex` repository in five consecutive ships** (manga v256 → light novels v257 → subtitles v258 → anime library v260 → this), taking the same-author control to **N=5**.

⭐ **The corpus's FIRST same-author, same-domain SUCCESSOR.** v257 (`translate-LN-pipeline`, 2026-04-26) was a PyQt6 workbench for exactly this task whose defining design was that *the tool never called an API* — it rendered a prompt, the human pasted it into a chat LLM and pasted the answer back. v261 is that project rebuilt from scratch 34 days later in a different stack, with **both** an API path and a manual Prompt Studio path.

**⭐⭐⭐ HEADLINE 3 — THE STALL DETECTOR IS THE BEST TWENTY LINES IN THE REPOSITORY.** `internal/host/flow/dispatcher.go:112-140`, `trackRepeat`: *"记录连续相同指令的下达次数…用 **Agent+Task 相等性（不比 Reason，因为 Reason 是给人看的辅助文本）**…次数**恰好**到 repeatNotifyAt 时**在锁外**触发一次 onRepeat"*. **Four separate pieces of care in one small function:** **(1)** ⭐⭐⭐ **equality on `Agent+Task` only, deliberately excluding `Reason` "because Reason is human-facing helper text"** — a detector comparing the whole instruction would be silently defeated by prose that varies while the instruction does not, **and he identified that failure mode and wrote down why he excluded the field**; **(2) fires ONCE, exactly at the threshold** — one alert not a storm, asserted at `router_test.go:289-290` (*"应恰好在第 N 次触发一次"*); **(3) fires OUTSIDE THE LOCK** so a slow handler cannot block the dispatcher; **(4) `ResetRepeat()` on Resume/Start** so recovery does not inherit a stale count. **⭐ MINT — §C-2 row C57, N=1: "From-Scratch Non-Chromium Headless Browser ENGINE Built as AI-Agent / Scraping Infrastructure."** Corpus-first for the surface, and the gap was structural: every prior browser subject wraps, patches or drives an existing engine — CloakBrowser v69 (patched Chromium), camofox v179 (Camoufox/Firefox), browser-use v41 / Skyvern v24 (automation over existing browsers), crawl4ai v29 / firecrawl v214 (crawler library/API), page-agent v199 (in-page JS), ego lite v247 (a real browser), serve-sim v183 (simulator analogue), CoreOfPotato v231 / gemini-web2api v232 (DOM/HTTP harvesting). **None owns its own cascade, layout and paint.** ⚠️ **DECISIVELY NOT WORLD-FIRST** — `lightpanda-io/browser` (**AGPL-3.0**, Zig, V8, html5ever, 22 CDP domains, native MCP) precedes; servo/Verso/Ladybird precede as engine efforts. Capability-not-form-factor (the engine sets the ~30 MB envelope that makes one browser per agent task viable) on the v244/v215 reasoning; separated from the declines at v222 (fame ≠ mint), v236 (form factor), v211 (technique), v210/v196 (domain). **NO-MINT alternative recorded** (that Obscura is merely the 2nd entrant in Lightpanda's named class) and **declined** because outside-corpus prior art does not create a corpus N=2 — the camofox v179 rule exactly (*"Camoufox not a corpus subject; mentions ≠ recursion"*). Full row + scope note at `_patterns/06` C57.

**⭐ HOLD — C34 anti-detect/stealth browser stays at N=2** (v69 + v179). C34 requires *"a browser whose PRIMARY reason to exist is fingerprint evasion (vs a general browser-automation tool that treats stealth as one feature)."* Obscura's stealth is an **opt-in cargo feature** — `crates/obscura-cli/Cargo.toml:17` is `default = []` — absent from the default release archive, and one row of seven in its own comparison table ⇒ it is precisely what C34 defines itself against. ⭐ **Third consecutive ship where reading a §C row's own definition prevented a false N** (v262 C37, v263 C38, v267 C34).

**⭐⭐⭐⭐ HEADLINE — the repository implements a competitor's protocol namespace and never names the competitor.** `README.md:403` publishes `| **LP** | getMarkdown (DOM-to-Markdown conversion) |` — `LP` expanded **nowhere** in the README, `docs/`, `AGENTS.md`, or any code comment. `crates/obscura-cdp/src/domains/lp.rs:13` implements `"getMarkdown" =>`; `crates/obscura-js/src/markdown.rs:1` calls it *"the LP.getMarkdown CDP method."* **`LP` is Lightpanda**, per Lightpanda's own blog dated **2026-03-11**: *"`LP.getMarkdown` is the first command in a new custom CDP domain called **LP**, which is home for **Lightpanda-specific** capabilities that go beyond what standard CDP offers"* — and Lightpanda documents the identical CLI surface, *"from the CLI with `--dump markdown`."* Obscura ships both: `lp.rs` was present in `8749725 "Initial Release"` on **2026-04-13** (one month after the namespace was published), and `--dump markdown` arrived `d8b7c5f` 2026-05-13 (PR #78, an outside contributor). **A grep for `lightpanda` across every `.rs`/`.md`/`.toml`/`.yml` returns ZERO.** The resemblance is broad: same positioning ("headless browser for AI agents"), both from-scratch and explicitly not Chromium forks, both on **V8**, both on **html5ever/Servo** (`Cargo.toml:30-34`: html5ever 0.39, markup5ever, selectors, servo_arc, cssparser), both CDP-drop-in, both with native MCP in the binary, both with markdown extraction, comparable speed claims (9–11× vs *"~12x"*). ⚠️ **NO code derivation alleged or evidenced** — Zig→Rust, `lp.rs` is ~20 lines calling Obscura's own `HTML_TO_MARKDOWN_JS`, only 1 of Lightpanda's 4 LP commands is implemented, and **implementing a protocol method name is compatibility work with no licence issue.** **The finding is legibility**, and it is load-bearing because the two differ on **AGPL-3.0 vs Apache-2.0** — the single most decision-relevant fact for anyone choosing between them, and why this is the first subject in the class that is actually pilotable for hireui. Priority note: a prior-art lens dated Lightpanda's public announcement to ~mid-2025 (⚠️ agent-sourced, not independently verified; the 2026-03-11 LP date, which I verified, alone settles the namespace question).

**⭐⭐⭐ THE SHIP'S RULE — the discipline stops where the artifact stops being code.** v264: a discipline stops at the edge of the team that holds it · v265: where the safe choice would COST something · v266: it was already at the door in an unopened diff · **v267: everything a compiler reads is gated to the best standard in 267 subjects; everything only a human reads is gated by nothing, and `ci.yml:86` says so out loud.**

*The code side, and it is exceptional.* `ci.yml:6-8` opens with a **written threat model** (*"Pull requests execute contributor-controlled build scripts, proc macros, tests, and binaries. They must never receive a write token or repository secrets."*) and then honours it: `permissions: contents: read` (`ci.yml:9-10`, `release.yml:8-9`), write confined to one job (`release.yml:203-207`) that *"never checks out or executes repository code"*; `persist-credentials: false` on all four checkouts; **all 12 distinct GitHub Actions pinned to full 40-char SHAs, zero unpinned across three workflows**; ⭐ the **trusted-base pattern** (`ci.yml:54-55` reads `pr_policy.py` **and `deny.toml`** from the base revision ⇒ **a malicious PR cannot weaken the check judging it**; repeated at `:249-250`, and `:251-252` runs the base build from a separate trusted worktree *"so a PR-supplied `.cargo/config.toml` … cannot alter the compiler"*); ⭐ **cache poisoning closed** (`:143-145` `save-if: false` — *"A contributor therefore cannot poison a cache later consumed by a release"*); ⭐ **they pre-empted evasion of their own gate** (`:92-94` disables rename detection *"Otherwise moving runtime code to a documentation-looking path could incorrectly skip the runtime checks"*) — the corpus's first subject to anticipate a path-classifier bypass; **4 build configs / 3 test configs actually run on PR** (`:147-187`); a real **SSRF gate revalidating every redirect hop** (`ops.rs:2234/2331/2572/2820`, comment at `:2469`; private network denied by default, `--allow-private-network` to opt in, CI narrowing the opt-in to one test at `:160-167`); and the external obstacle course **SHA-pinned** (`:211-217`, `h4ckf0r0day/obscura-benchmark@6ebac829`) run **base-vs-candidate interleaved** (`:239-294`).

*The reader side.* **`ci.yml:86` routes `*.md|README*|docs/*` to neither `runtime` nor `audit`** ⇒ a docs-only PR runs the policy script and nothing else. Defensible engineering — and it is where every inflated claim lives: **four mutually-inconsistent speed figures** (`README.md:35` **85 ms** vs `:361-363` **51/84/78 ms** vs `AGENTS.md:98` ***"~12x faster"***; memory is consistent at ~6×), the headline value matching none of its own three benchmark rows; **`README.md:34` `| Anti-detect | **Built-in** | None |`** for a feature needing a compile-time flag **and** `--stealth` (`crates/obscura-cli/Cargo.toml:17` `default = []`), with **no in-tree test against any real detection service** (scoped search for creepjs/fingerprintjs/bot.sannysoft/browserleaks/incolumitas/datadome matches one prose file); and the unexpanded `LP`. ⚠️ **Fair reading:** `AGENTS.md:98` says *"on framework pages"*, a workload none of the three rows measures, and `README.md:365` points to a **real** external suite (existence confirmed by CI's SHA pin). ⭐ **The consequence is structural and refines v262's rule:** the claims **verifiable from inside the repo are conservative** — the README advertises ~10 CDP domains while the code implements **189 methods across 16**, *underselling* capability — and the claims **verifiable only from outside it** are the inflated ones. **The discriminator is not code-vs-prose but verifiable-from-inside vs verifiable-only-from-outside.** The detail beneath every headline is honest (`README.md:167-172`'s archive matrix truthfully lists the plain archive "Stealth transport: **No**"): **all three inflated claims sit in the top-of-README comparison table.**

**⭐⭐⭐ The number the rule names is computed, displayed, and never enforced.** `AGENTS.md:51-52` and `:69` both state the obstacle course *"must stay **33/33**."* `scripts/ci/compare_obstacle.py` is otherwise rigorous — `:15` `EXPECTED_STAGE_COUNT = 33` enforced for both sides (`:65-72`), stage-name set equality (`:73-76`), duplicate detection (`:33-34`), and `:36-43` explicitly rejects `bool` for `median_ms` because `isinstance(True, int)` is `True` in Python — then `:91-92` computes `base_passed`/`candidate_passed`, `:97` renders `| Correct stages | n/33 | n/33 |` into the step summary, and `:112-113` makes **`if regressions:` the only failure condition** (`regressions` at `:78` = passed-on-base-and-failing-now). ⇒ **the gate is purely differential — a candidate at 0/33 passes if base was 0/33; the absolute standard stated twice as mandatory is the one thing never checked.** Same shape one layer up in the same job: `ci.yml:269-279` wraps both runs in `set +e`, captures `base_status`/`pr_status`, and **`printf`s them without ever testing them** — only `json.tool` can fail the step. The v256 / v264 / v265 class, unusually pure because the gate is otherwise excellent.

**⭐⭐⭐ v265's RULE AT INDEPENDENT CROSS-ORGANISATION N=2 — and a stronger instance.** `crates/obscura-mcp/src/http.rs:132-146` **names the attack its own default permits** — *"When an allowlist is configured, a browser `Origin` must match one of its entries …; **this stops a malicious local web page from driving the loopback MCP port**"* — inside the same comment block that explains why the default stays open: *"Unset/empty → permissive (unchanged `*`) **so hosted dashboards keep working (issue #175)**."* `origin_allowed` returns `true` for `None`; `cors_header` (`:161-167`) emits `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`. **v265: a discipline travels freely wherever it is FREE and stops wherever the safe choice would COST something.** Different author, different language, different domain, two ships later — **and stronger than v265's own instance, because here the cost and the attack are written in the same comment.** Mitigations, stated fairly: the native binary binds loopback (Dockerfile `:52-54` documents `0.0.0.0` as container-only), and `Origin`-less native clients are the normal path. Compounding: **37 MCP tools with ZERO approval gate, no read-only mode, no URL allowlist** — a scoped grep over `crates/obscura-mcp/` for approve|confirm|consent|read_only|dry_run|allowlist returns only the CORS origin list and the word "confirm" inside a tool *description* (`lib.rs:575`) — including `browser_evaluate` (arbitrary JS), `browser_get_cookies`, `browser_storage_state`, `browser_pdf`. **⭐ A fence made of a sentence.** `AGENTS.md:134-135`: *"**Git-ignored** internal handover notes are private working material: do not edit them, link them from public documentation, stage them, or **commit them**. **Do not commit generated screenshots or reports.**"* **`.gitignore` is 18 bytes: `target/` and `.DS_Store`.** Nothing ignores any handover note (`.git/info/exclude` is the stock template). ### ⭐⭐⭐ THE LICENCE — MIT as far as the publication mechanism could see

| Declaration | Value |
|---|---|
| `LICENSE` (root) · `hithink-finance-cli/LICENSE` · `package.json` · README's final line | **MIT** |
| **`python/pyproject.toml:11`** | **`license = { text = "Proprietary" }`** |

**Chronology, verified commit by commit:** **2026-06-15** `b837e7b` (first code commit) — `pyproject.toml` says **Proprietary**, and **no `LICENSE` file exists anywhere** · **2026-07-10** `45d49cd` — `hithink-finance-cli/LICENSE` (MIT) arrives for the npm subpackage; root `pyproject.toml` moves to `python/` **carrying Proprietary** · **2026-07-13** `05903e9` ("发布 hithink finance CLI 0.1.1") — root `LICENSE` (MIT) arrives, **28 days after the first commit, in an npm-publication commit**.

**Why:** `hithink-finance-cli/docs/maintainers/npm-publishing.md:1` — *"Obtain team approval for an open-source license and add `hithink-finance-cli/LICENSE`; **publishing is blocked until this exists**."* ⭐ **The MIT grant arrived BECAUSE publishing required it, and was applied at the two paths npm cares about. `pyproject.toml` was outside npm's field of view, so nothing prompted it.**

⭐ **And the gate is TEN LINES:** `scripts/check-license.mjs` calls `access('../LICENSE')`. It **never reads the file** — so it cannot see a licence contradiction, a wrong SPDX id, or a `package.json` mismatch. Its error message says *"an **approved** LICENSE is required"* — the doc's sentence had two clauses (*obtain team approval* **and** *add LICENSE*) and **the script implements only the mechanical one, while the message claims the other.** It runs in `prepublishOnly`, the highest-stakes moment.

Any licence scanner (pip-licenses/FOSSA/Snyk) reports Proprietary for those 5,051 lines. **v245's "Apache metadata over an AGPL wheel" INVERTED, and stronger than v269's licence-by-omission — this is an affirmative contrary declaration.**

### ⭐⭐ SUPPLY CHAIN — all 206 dependencies resolve to a Chinese mirror

`npm-shrinkwrap.json` (which, unlike `package-lock.json`, **is always included in the published tarball and is authoritative for consumers**): **206** `resolved` entries · **206 → `registry.npmmirror.com`** · **0 → `registry.npmjs.org`** · **206 carry a `sha512` integrity hash**.

**What it is NOT:** a code-substitution risk — integrity is verified post-download; a hostile mirror cannot serve different bytes. **What it IS:** every consumer inherits a lockfile directing all 206 fetches to a third-party PRC host — a **privacy/observability** exposure (the mirror sees installer IP + full dependency graph) and an **availability** coupling to a host the publisher doesn't control. **Cause visible in the repo:** README recommends 「国内用户可使用 npmmirror 镜像加速」 with `--registry=https://registry.npmmirror.com`; the maintainer installed with it configured and the lockfile recorded it. **Why nothing caught it:** CI runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts`, which *uses* the lockfile as written and passes; `npm pack --dry-run` passes; `tests/release/package-contents.test.ts` checks **contents, not hosts**; `check-license.mjs` checks a filename. **Nothing in this repository looks at where its dependencies come from.** ⭐ **The v260 §42 workspace leak at its purest** — an artifact of *where the work was done*, published to everyone. ⚠️ **My fleet asserted the opposite** ("all network calls use HTTPS" — true but irrelevant) and never inspected `resolved` hosts.

**Otherwise strong:** all 5 direct deps + 206 locked packages **exact-pinned** (no `^`/`~`) · API keys in the **OS keychain** (`@napi-rs/keyring`) + `redact.ts` + `tests/security/secret-leak.test.ts` + `auth login --api-key-stdin` (key never in argv) · `update-check.mjs` (23 lines) hits **only** `registry.npmjs.org`, 15 s timeout, cache at **mode `0o600`**, **atomic temp+rename with PID**, and a swallowed catch **with a written rationale**; it records a version, it does **not** install · 3 dedicated security test files (`injection`, `path-traversal`, `secret-leak`) · release uses `npm publish --provenance`, Trusted Publisher, protected environment, tag↔version equality, idempotent republish guard, *"Never use a long-lived npm token"* · `npm ci --ignore-scripts` **everywhere** in CI. **Weak:** **9 `uses:` clauses, 0 SHA-pinned** · **2 of 4 workflows have no `permissions:` block** (`cli-ci`, `python-ci`; the canary correctly sets `contents: read`).

🔴 **THE POSTINSTALL: `npm install -g` writes 85 skill files into your global agent skills directory (`skills add … --global --copy --all --full-depth`), no prompt, no documented opt-out — and the word "postinstall" appears in ZERO markdown files.** ⭐ In the same 27 lines it **sets `DISABLE_TELEMETRY: '1'`** on that dependency and stays **non-fatal** on failure: **it protects your privacy from a third party while writing to your home directory without telling you.**

### ⭐⭐ TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS OF ONE ON-DISK FORMAT

The TS CLI (`src/infrastructure/duckdb/*`, `migrations/001-initial.sql`) and Python `marketdb` (`sql/schema.sql`, `views.sql`) **both** init/sync/query/migrate a DuckDB store, with **identical table and view names** and **incompatible definitions**.

`raw_kline_daily` — TS: OHLCV **NOT NULL**, **`amount`**, **`batch_id`**, **`prev_close`**, 10 cols. Python: nullable, **`turnover`**, **`source_batch_id`**, plus **`currency`/`interval`/`adjusted`**, 12 cols.
`raw_adjustment_events` (the table feeding the adjustment calc) — TS: **`rights_ratio`**, **`rights_price`**, `batch_id`, NOT NULL DEFAULT 0. Python: **`allotment_ratio`**, **`allotment_price`**, `source_batch_id`, nullable, plus `ticker`/`currency`.
Also `stg_symbol` vs **`stg_symbols`**; `_meta.updated_at` only in Python. **Six diverging column names.** All four view names identical (`v_symbol`, `v_daily`, `v_daily_qfq`, `v_daily_hfq`) and `v_daily` selects **different columns** in each.

⭐ **Root cause visible: 配股 renders into English as either "rights issue" or "allotment"** — two implementations built from one Chinese spec, each choosing independently. **No test in either suite reads both schemas.** **Collision is SILENT** because both use `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` and `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW`: the first tool's tables are accepted, the second's views replace the first's, the DDL succeeds and reports nothing.

⚠️ **The mitigating fact, which must LEAD the risk framing: the DEFAULT PATHS DIFFER** — TS uses `<platform dataDir>/market.duckdb` (`platform-paths.ts:164`), Python `./data/market.duckdb` (`config.py:48`). **The common case never collides.** You must point them at one path — which `.env.example` and every README `marketdb` example do use — and the README presents both as ways to manage "the local database" without saying they are different databases.

⭐ **And the elegant part:** the TS side has a real migration system — `_meta.schema_version` + `schema_checksum`, `SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSION`, and `migrations/manifest.json` pinning `001-initial.sql` by **sha256**. **It verifies its own schema cryptographically and cannot see the other implementation of the same schema in the same repository.** v264's rule (*a discipline stops at the edge of the team that holds it*) — **here the edge is the LANGUAGE.**

**The Python data layer is genuinely good.** `calculations/adjustment.py` (125 lines) is the best code here and the highest-stakes: the standard A-share ex-rights formula stated in a header comment with every variable defined **and the net effect spelled out**; **ex-dates mapped to the next real trading day** (`MIN(k.date) WHERE k.date >= e.ex_date`); `prev_close` via `LAG(close) OVER (...)`; **`EXP(SUM(LN(ratio)))`** for cumulative products (twice); log-domain guard `WHERE ratio > 0`; `NULLIF` divide-by-zero guard; correct 前复权 normalisation via `LAST_VALUE`; **`factor_version = '1.0'` stored per row**; idempotent full recompute with batch provenance. ⚠️ **A caveat I raised and then REFUTED myself:** I suspected it assumed unadjusted input without checking; `importers/parquet.py:41-77` scopes every operation to `WHERE adjusted = 'none'` **with a comment saying why**, and the tests seed `adjusted='none'`. Narrow residual: `adjustment.py` itself doesn't filter it, so **the guard lives at the writer, not the reader** — safe today because nothing writes a non-`'none'` row.

### ⭐⭐⭐ THE AGENT SURFACE — the most transferable material

**Two tiers, 11 skills, 327,920 bytes.** `skills/hithink-finance/` = **1** unified router (`SKILL.md` 14,495 B; 26 files / **154,555 B** total). `hithink-finance-cli/skills/` = **10** domain packages (85 files / **173,365 B**), generated from code, sha256-pinned. ⚠️ **CORRECTION: 10 CLI packages, not 11** (10 + the router = 11 skills total).

**Progressive-disclosure ladder, measured:** router only **14,495 B** → everything **154,555 B** = ⭐ **a 10.7× reduction**, and `test_root_skills_are_consolidated` asserts the words 「渐进」/「按需」 are present (weak enforcement — the vocabulary, not the behaviour — but more than prose).

**⭐⭐⭐ THE NEGATIVE ROUTING CLAUSE — 10 of 10 descriptions, verified programmatically.** Every CLI skill description ends by naming where to go **instead**: financials 「价格行情转 …-market，指数财务**不在本 skill 范围**」 · fund/index/symbol/special-data each redirect to their siblings by name · valuation 「历史估值、ROE 和投资建议**不在本 skill 范围**」 · research 「**不用于**实时取数、荐股、择时、组合建议或投资结论」 · shared 「**不要用于**行情、财务、指数、特色数据或研究取数」 · data 「远端实时数据转对应业务 skill」. ⭐ **Ten descriptions forming a routing mesh where every node names its neighbours, in the one field the model always sees** — attacking the hardest problem in any multi-skill collection.

**Instructions telling the agent to distrust documentation:** `hithink-finance-cli/README.md:70` 「**Agent 不应只凭 README 猜参数。** 先读取 `capabilities`，再对目标 capability 读取 `schema`。」 ⭐ **= v269's rule at independent cross-organisation N=2** · `AGENTS.md:52` 「**离线测试不能证明线上认证或实时服务可用；只有实际授权请求才能称为线上验证。**」 ⭐ **and this one is MECHANISED** by `hithink-finance-cli-live-canary.yml` (weekly cron, 3 real authorized requests, asserts `ok` + `meta.request_id`) · `README.md:29` 「**不要在终端指引中把源码安装伪装成正式发布安装**」 · `python/toolkit/fuyao/README.md:144` 「**不要从旧文档推断当前签名**」 · templated across ~40 reference files: 「**不要猜字段名**」.

**Anti-fabrication, and WHERE it is placed:** the general rule appears 4× in README, but the effective placements are narrower — `docs/api/README.md:62` on error **`3002` 数据尚未准备**: 「**不得补零或使用模拟数据**」 · `docs/mcp/capability-map.md:58` on a revoked key: 「**不要改用模拟数据**」 · `examples/.../02:20` 「**`null` 保持缺失，不补零**…不要编造估值、行业均值和评分」. ⭐ **The instruction is attached to the specific error condition that would tempt fabrication** — and for financial data 「`null` 保持缺失，不补零」 is load-bearing: a zero is a real value, a null is absence.

### THE EXAMPLES — a disclosure that stops at the file boundary

16 numbered dashboards; **16/16 complete** (README + HTML + JPG); **all fully static** (0 network calls, 0 credential leaks). Two claims, measured separately **inside the `example.html`**: investment-advice disclaimer **16/16** ✅ · **simulated-data disclosure 8/16** (examples 09–16 only).

⚠️ **A CORRECTION I CAUGHT PRE-PUBLICATION:** my first grep used only 「非投资建议」 and reported 8/16 for the *advice* disclaimer too. Examples 01–08 use a **different wording** — 「仅供信息展示，不构成投资建议」. **Grepping one phrasing for a semantic property produces false negatives on half the corpus.**

**The chronology is sharper than "forward only":** commit `77d9469` (2026-07-17) **added 07–16 AND simultaneously modified 01–06's `example.html`**. So in one commit, one author, one day: the simulated-data label went into 09–16 (8 new files), **not** into 07–08 (2 new files in the same commit), **not** into 01–06 (6 files whose HTML was open and being edited). ⭐ **The improvement failed to travel SIDEWAYS within a single change** — v259's copy-forward problem compressed into one commit.

**And the consequence is load-bearing:** `README.md:471` offers, for the example it bills as the 默认示例, `- [直接打开静态 HTML](examples/inspirations/01-stock-overview/example.html)` — **a link that bypasses the README carrying the label.** `01`'s HTML is 70,049 B titled 「同花顺行情工作台」 with no in-file synthesis notice, and the data **is** synthetic: **616 of its 1,880 decimal values (32.8%) carry a repeating-sevenths fingerprint** (`192.72142857142853`) while Chinese exchanges quote to two decimals. ⭐ **The honesty label is welded into the DOCUMENTATION and absent from the ARTIFACT — the exact inverse of v270**, where the freshness claim was welded into the artifact nine times and the age was absent. **In fairness: 16/16 example READMEs carry both labels, so the repo's own 「冒充」 rule is discharged for any reader arriving via the README. A boundary defect, not dishonesty.**

**CLI `src` 10,141 LOC / `tests` 2,879 (45 files, ratio 0.28); `python` 5,051 / tests 3,156 (23 files, ratio 0.62); 253 test functions** (116 vitest `^\s*(it|test)\(` + 137 pytest `^def test_`). ⭐ **`vitest` include `tests/**/*.test.ts` covers all 7 subdirectories** (unit/integration/contract/e2e/performance/release/security) — **no orphaned test directory**, unlike v264 where a whole language's tests never ran; `npm run verify` = `format:check && lint && typecheck && build && test:built` on **10 matrix combos**; **0 skipped TS tests**, 1 in Python (the necessary export skip).

### DOCUMENTATION — excellent, and Chinese-only

Method: `tr -d '\000-\177'` per file counting residual non-ASCII bytes, cross-validated with `grep -cP '[\x{4e00}-\x{9fff}]'`. **164 tracked `.md` · 161 contain Chinese · 3 pure ASCII** — `hithink-finance-cli/AGENTS.md` (11 lines), `SECURITY.md` (**3 lines**), `docs/maintainers/npm-publishing.md` (7 lines) = **21 lines of English total, all stubs.** No `en/`, no `README.en.md`, no switcher. ⚠️ **FLEET ERROR: it claimed "all 164 files contain both Chinese and English, zero English-only."** I read all three English files verbatim. ⭐ **Honest impact: an LLM reads Chinese fluently, so the AGENT is unaffected — it is the HUMAN who cannot audit what the agent is being told.** A 327,920-byte Chinese-only skill surface installed globally by an undisclosed postinstall is a real barrier for an operator whose discipline is *verify the claim yourself*. **The CLI is bilingual at runtime; its documentation is not.**

### THE SHIP'S RULE

> **Every gate here is correct about what it checks and silent about the adjacent thing you would assume it checks. Each gate's scope is inherited from WHERE IT LIVES, not from WHAT IT CLAIMS.**

`sync_skill_contracts.py` guards 17 mirror pairs and not `references/cli*`/`python-sdk*` (the parts describing what this repo changes every release) · the doc-governance suite guards nine properties and its trigger excludes README/CHANGELOG/AGENTS.md/`examples/**` · `check-license.mjs` guards a filename and not `pyproject.toml` · `migrations/manifest.json` guards one SQL file by sha256 and not the other implementation of the same schema · `eslint` guards style and not 12 layering violations · `npm ci` guards reproducibility and not 206 mirror URLs · the export test guards the denylist polarity and **skips wherever it ships** · ⭐ **and `generated-contracts.test.ts` is the one that got it right, by delegating its list to a hashed manifest.**

**Ladder:** v267 the discipline stops where the artifact stops being code · v268 a gate exists where a reader can refuse · v269 no gate can see an entry that was never added · v270 no gate can fire on a claim true when written · **v271 a gate's scope is inherited from its location, not its subject.**

⭐ **What makes this subject different from the previous four: I could not find a single declared-but-absent discipline.** Everything declared is implemented; every countable claim is accurate. **The gaps are all SCOPE gaps** — a `paths:` filter, a directory boundary, a language boundary, a registry field — **the kind you get from building carefully in one place and shipping to another.**
