### ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE — the validated artifact is frozen; the unvalidated one grew a third

Two generators in `scripts/`, both wired into the same `prebuild` line. `generate-style-skill.mjs` (169 lines) renders `data/style-library.json` → the skill's `references/style-library.md`: **`grep -c throw` = 9**, validating unique ids/categories/styles/scenes, **every `template.anchor` existing as `<a name=…>` in `docs/templates.md`** (a cross-document reference check), **every template and category `cover` resolving to a file on disk**, no duplicate covers — plus **`assertNoPattern()`, which THROWS if the generated text contains the Chinese AI-slop construction 不是…而是**. `generate-site-data.mjs` (189 lines) parses 930 KB of gallery prose → `data/cases.json`: **`grep -c throw` = 0**, with three silent fallbacks.

**And the measurement that settles it.** At the last published tag `…-v1.0.4` (**2026-05-08**) vs HEAD (2026-08-23), by `git show <tag>:<path> | md5`: `SKILL.md` **byte-identical** · `references/style-library.md` **byte-identical** · skill `package.json` **byte-identical** · `data/style-library.json` **byte-identical** · `data/cases.json` **`totalCases` 398 → 529**.

⭐⭐⭐ **In the 108 days since the skill was last published, the catalogue gained 131 cases (+33%) and the agent skill did not change by a single byte.** The 22 templates are frozen (35 `"anchor"` occurrences at both refs). **The gate is pointed at the thing that does not change; the silent fallbacks are pointed at the thing that grew by a third.** Agent consequence: `SKILL.md` says *"Prefer the reference over memory when template names, categories, covers, or style tags matter"* — and the reference's newest referenced example is **case 378** (34 `exampleCases` refs, max 378, 0 dangling) while the catalogue runs to **532**. **154 cases the skill has never heard of.**

**The three fallbacks, and what each produced.** `extractPrompt` → `''` on a regex miss: **0 empty prompts at HEAD**, the markdown convention held. `extractSource` → `{label:'Community', url:''}`: **0 cases labelled `'Community'` — the fallback never fired**, and all **25** empty-`sourceUrl` cases are explainable (15 Xiaohongshu account ids with no linkable per-post URL, 9 the author's own cases credited to his WeChat article, **1 — case 3 — the literal string 未提供**), plus case 270 whose URL was swallowed by malformed markdown (`\[OpenNana]\(]\(<https://x.com/Toshi_nyaruo_AI/…>)`). **529 of 529 cases carry a `来源：` line** (164 in part-1 + 365 in part-2) ⇒ ⭐ **the disclaimer's promise to "make every effort to preserve original sources" is substantially KEPT — a genuine strength that corrects the direction the analysis was heading in.** `inferCategory`/`inferTags` → keyword heuristics: **this one fired, 15 times.**

**The inventory rule, live (v240), run by hand in both directions:** images with no case entry **3** (`case12.jpg`, `case169.jpg`, `case170.jpg`) · case entries with no image **0** (⚠️ my first pass said 13; **my own `caseN.jpg` regex was too narrow** — they are `.png` and all 529 resolve) · anchors vs `cases.json` **exactly equal both ways** · `gallery.md` index refs with no anchor **0** · **anchors ABSENT from the `gallery.md` category index: 15** (cases 42, 48, 50, 66, 69, 82, 90, 133, 159, 172, 243, 280, 301, 318, 332). `parseCategoryMap()` reads its map from `gallery.md`, so **those 15 get `undefined` and fall through to keyword inference — a category the author never chose.** ⚠️ **Mitigating fact that must lead:** the `"Other Use Cases"` bucket is **28 cases, all 28 author-indexed as `cat-other`** — **zero** of the 15 landed in the junk bucket.

⚠️ **AND A CORRECTION TO MY OWN FRAMING.** I set out to prove the heuristic misclassifies using identical titles, and it does (cases 82 and 90, titled 信息图可视化设计, went to *UI & Interfaces* while 66 and 69 with the same title went to *Charts & Infographics*). But grouping all 529 by title shows the real story: **that one title is shared by 27 cases across 7 distinct categories, and 23 of the 27 are author-indexed.** The categories disagree because **the titles are degenerate, not because the heuristic is bad: 529 cases carry only 392 distinct titles; 161 cases (30.4%) share a title; the worst are 信息图可视化设计 ×27 (7 categories), 主题海报版式设计 ×21 (5), 界面交互设计图 ×14 (4).** Titles come from the author's own `### 例 N：…` headings and serve *both* as the card title a visitor reads **and** as classification input — **a generic label is doubly load-bearing and carries no information in either role.** Prompts, by contrast, are 509 distinct of 529.

**The style vocabulary: 10 declared, 19 emitted.** `inferTags()` declares `styleOrder` with 10 values; `cases.json` emits 19. The 9 extras (Architecture, Characters, Charts, Documents, History, `"Other Use Cases"`, Photography, Products, Scenes) all come from one expression — the style fallback borrows `caseItem.category.split(' & ')[0]`. ⭐ **Two fallbacks in one function, one right and one wrong:** the *scene* fallback is the constant `'Creative'` and emits exactly the declared 10; the *style* fallback reaches into a different taxonomy and invents nine facets from it. Consequences shipped: `data/style-library.json` now carries all 19 (the 9 artifacts **ratified into the curated schema**, with empty `keywords`, so they can never be matched since `styleOrder` is hardcoded), and `src/main.jsx` renders `siteData.styles` as filter chips ⇒ **the live site shows `Character` and `Characters` as two separate filters, and a visual style literally named `"Other Use Cases"`.**

**The anti-slop gate — correct, narrow, aimed at the one clean file.** I ran the repository's own regex over all 77 text files **with a validated positive control**: `references/style-library.md` (**the only file it guards**) **0** · `data/cases.json` **8** · `gallery-part-1.md` **3** · `gallery-part-2.md` **2** · `templates.md` **1** ⇒ **14 matches in unguarded files, 0 in the guarded one.** ⚠️ **Be fair about the aim:** the reference is rendered from English scaffolding plus the hand-authored `zh`/`en` fields of the JSON, so the gate *is* correctly aimed at the only prose that can reach the artifact it guards. What it cannot see is the 930 KB of gallery prose and the 1.3 MB `cases.json` — where the product lives. **Pattern #88 88c at the BUILD layer rather than the review layer.**

### The licence, stated plainly

`README.md` contains, **in the same file and the same language, sixteen lines apart**: **:512** *"This project only organizes publicly accessible community prompts and example images… It does not claim ownership of any third-party original content."* · **:520** *"This repository does not guarantee that third-party content can be used commercially. Please obtain authorization from the original rights holder before commercial use."* · **:528** *"This project is open source under the MIT License. You can use, modify, distribute, and build on it freely…"*

⚠️ **THIS CORRECTS MY OWN FIRST READING.** I had it as an i18n finding — a claim in English qualified only in a Chinese-only file. **It is not.** `README.md:504-520` carries the full disclaimer in fluent English, clause for clause, in all three READMEs; `docs/disclaimer.md` is a **Chinese duplicate** of a section already present in every README, which the "Full disclaimer" link points at. (Two copies of one licence-critical fact, two languages, no declaration of which wins — **D32 unapplied**, in the lowest-stakes place it could happen; not yet drifted.) ⇒ **the contradiction is fully legible to every reader, in one document.** MIT covers the code — 10,666 lines, cleanly. It does not and cannot cover 543 images the same file says belong to someone else.

**On the images:** line 512 says the project *organizes* "community prompts **and example images**"; line 516 calls them "generated images" whose "inspiration and data sources" are public communities ⇒ **AI-generated images collected from public posts, not generated by this project.** Six sampled jpgs are plain JFIF with **no C2PA, no OpenAI marker, no copyright field, no watermark** — which proves nothing either way, only that any provenance metadata is gone.

**Attribution, measured:** the disclaimer names two principal sources. **OpenNana is cited per-case 5 times** (`gallery-part-2.md` lines 2189, 3155, 3414, 3657, 4563 — one being the malformed one). **YouMind is cited per-case ZERO times** (extent: all 12 tracked `.md` + both data JSONs; it appears only in the four document-level disclaimers). The other ~524 cases credit the **original poster** — ~230 distinct X/Twitter handles (@MrLarus 30, @liyue_ai 21, @BubbleBrain 11) plus ~15 Xiaohongshu ids. ⭐ **That is better practice than crediting the aggregator** — and nothing explains that the disclaimer answers *where the author looked* while the per-case sources answer *who made it*.

**Monetisation is disclosed and asymmetric:** each of the three READMEs carries **6 `aff=` + 3 `utm_`**, identical; the website carries **1**; **the agent skill directory carries 0** (grep over `agents/` for apimart/hiapi/packyapi/doloffer/pptoken/ciyuan/canghe.ai). ⭐ **The agent-facing artifact carries no monetisation at all.** **17 of 159 commits (10.7%) concern sponsor placement**, including the two immediately before the last case-add (*"move APIMart sponsor to first position"*, *"Move PackyCode sponsor to second position"*). One link carries **`utm_campaign=awesome-gpt-image-2`** — the v40 UTM-instrumented-funnel mechanism, campaign named after the repository. **And the image backend is Ciyuan** (`generate-image.js` → `${CIYUAN_BASE_URL}/v1/images/generations`), **itself one of the seven listed sponsors** — the sponsorship is load-bearing on the product.

### ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE SHIP'S RULE

**A gate holds when something else already requires it. The checks you must remember to run are the checks you do not have.**

`prebuild` runs the schema validators because Vercel needs a build. A whole migration exists because Supabase's advisor emailed a warning list. The lockfile is clean because npm's default registry is npmjs.org. Publishing needed a `LICENSE`, so there is one. And 27 tests that name, individually, every way a payment system can be defrauded sit behind `npm test`, which nothing types; 10,666 lines of JS have no linter; and the 529 cases that *are* the product have no schema, so there was nothing for a validator to attach to, so they got three regexes with fallbacks that cannot fail.

⇒ **v267:** the discipline stops where the artifact stops being code · **v268:** a gate exists where a reader can refuse · **v269:** no gate can see an entry that was never added · **v270:** no gate can fire on a claim that was true when it was written · **v271:** a gate's scope is inherited from its location, not its subject · **v272: a gate holds when something else already requires it.**

**And the measurement that proves it, in one line: the artifact with five fail-closed invariants has been byte-identical for 108 days; the artifact with three silent fallbacks grew by 131 cases in the same window.**

### Method

**Fleet:** 13 dimensions, **12 returned, 1 died** (`tests-and-gates`, StructuredOutput retry cap) — **hand-covered in full**, including the enforcement census with stated extent over all 656 tracked files, the 27 test names, the dynamic `api-imports.test.js` and the `prebuild`→Vercel gate. **46 agents · 5.39M subagent tokens · 1,172 tool uses · 13.7 min.**

**Fleet errors — 4, of which 2 substantive.** 🔴 **(1) FABRICATED:** a dimension reported at HIGH significance that *"`python/pyproject.toml` declares `Proprietary` while the root LICENSE says MIT."* **There is no Python in this repository** — `ls-files | grep -c '\.py$|pyproject|requirements|setup\.py'` = **0** over all 656 files, and the string `Proprietary` appears in **zero** tracked non-image files. **It imported v271's HiThink finding wholesale**, and a second agent then corroborated it claiming *"GROUND-TRUTH-VERIFIED: I read the actual files."* Had it stood it would have been a headline. 🔴 **(2)** line numbers reported as case ids (*"cases 2189, 3155, 3414, 3657, 4563"* — max id is 532; those are `gallery-part-2.md` line numbers); the underlying fact was right once corrected. ⚠️ **(3)** `git log --all --oneline | wc -l = 50` against a truth of **160**, refuted by running it myself. ⚠️ **(4)** a CRITICAL rated on a wrong consequence (*"README.md:74 links to a Chinese-only disclaimer, trapping English readers"* — the file **is** Chinese-only, but the same README carries the full disclaimer in English 430 lines further down; the agent never checked). ⭐ **Three of four got the fact right and the interpretation wrong — v271's D51 pattern at a fifth data point. Only the Python one was invention.**

**My own corrections, all pre-publication:** (1) the disclaimer is **not** Chinese-only — `README.md:504-520` carries it in English, which killed my strongest i18n framing and produced a better one; (2) `install.mjs`'s `rmSync` is **correctly scoped** to its own subdirectory; (3) my perl anti-slop counter reported **0 everywhere** and was silently broken by byte-vs-codepoint semantics — caught by a positive control, re-run in node with the repository's own regex; (4) my "13 missing images" was a too-narrow `caseN.jpg` regex — they are `.png` and all 529 resolve; (5) my identical-titles-misclassified framing was **subsumed by a better finding** (the titles are degenerate: 392 distinct for 529 cases; 23 of the 27 sharing the worst title are author-indexed).

⚠️ **NEW METHOD RULE PROPOSED — a companion to §43.2.** The v257 hazard is that *a ground-truth block handed to a fleet is an amplifier*. This ship found the adjacent one: **a fleet agent can import the PREVIOUS SHIP's findings into the current one, unprompted.** My ground-truth block never mentioned Python; the prompt merely cited v271 and v269 as *method* precedent. That was enough. ⇒ **When a fleet prompt cites a prior ship for method, name the prior subject explicitly and state that none of its facts transfer** — and on the orchestrator's side, **every cross-ship-shaped finding must be re-derived from a command in this clone before it enters a document.**

⚠️ **D39 refined at a fourth data point.** `git log --all --oneline | wc -l` = **160** in my own run, matching `rev-list --all --count`; `git log --oneline` = 159 = `rev-list --count HEAD`. **The v267 50-cap did not reproduce**, and the 50 the agent reported was an artifact of the *agent's* output handling, not of git ⇒ **v270's narrowing holds, and the transferable lesson is narrower and sharper: a subagent's reported command output can be silently truncated in ways the subagent does not detect.** §43.1 again.

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **THE SHIP'S RULE: A CLAIM IS SAFE WHEN A GATE COVERS IT, OR WHEN A HABIT COVERS IT. THIS ONE HAD NEITHER.** The GitHub repository **description** — verified today on **two independent GitHub surfaces** (the repo page and the owner's `?tab=repositories` listing) — still reads *"Core: the Depth Tree method, which splits a task N layers deep and gives every leaf the full time budget of the whole task, **so effort multiplies with depth**."* That claim was **retracted inside the repository on day one, in three places**: `CHANGELOG.md:59` *"Reframed the Depth Tree as decomposition and integration **rather than an arithmetic effort multiplier**"* · `references/method.md:3` *"**Do not treat depth as an arithmetic promise about effort or tokens**"* · `:5` *"**The original v1 method claimed** that each binary split multiplied effort."* **A grep across all 28 tracked files finds the arithmetic promise in ZERO of them.** ⭐ Read literally, `method.md:3` instructs the reader not to believe the repository's own sidebar. **Why it survives is the finding:** a description is not a file (no CI can reach it) and it is not in the tree (the author's own editing pass never touches it). ⭐⭐⭐ **AND THE HABIT IS MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED:** `CONTRIBUTING.md:23` forbids em and en dashes, nothing lints it, and there are **ZERO of either across all 28 tracked files** (positive control: 9 hyphen matches — the grep fires). **4,150 lines, an unenforced rule, perfect compliance.** ⇒ **the prose rules hold because ONE careful person writes all the prose; the code rules are gated because SEVEN strangers touch the code; the description is the only surface with neither.** ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **THE LADDER: v267 the discipline stops where the artifact stops being code · v268 a gate exists where a reader can refuse · v269 no gate can see an entry never added · v270 no gate can fire on a claim true when written · v271 a gate's scope is inherited from where it lives · v272 a gate holds when something else already requires it · v273 a check is only as permanent as the place you put it · v274 NEITHER A GATE NOR A HABIT REACHES A CLAIM STORED OUTSIDE THE REPOSITORY.**

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ **THE §42 SAME-AUTHOR CONTROL — and it is the strongest structural result of the ship.** This is the author of **corpus v81** (`Leonxlnx/taste-skill`, 2026-05-20), a **193-ship gap**. I **cloned taste-skill and measured it** rather than trusting the v81 entry: **153 commits main / 271 all-refs / 1 root / 64 files / 2026-02-19 → 2026-08-22 (six months, last commit two days before this ship) / 265 of 271 commits by the same email / `.github/` contains EXACTLY `FUNDING.yml` + `copilot-instructions.md` / ZERO workflows / ZERO `package.json` / ZERO test files** (its four `scripts/*.mjs` are README-asset build helpers) / **79,622 stars page-stated — against the 18,264 the v81 entry recorded, a 4.36× rise.** Versus unlazy: **4 test suites, 64 assertions, 9 CI jobs (3 OS × Node 16/20/24) on push AND pull_request, both actions SHA-pinned.** ⇒ ⭐ **THE ENGINEERING DISCIPLINE IS NOT A PROPERTY OF THE DEVELOPER. IT IS A PROPERTY OF WHAT THE ARTIFACT CLAIMS.** taste-skill claims **taste** — judged by a human looking at a UI, so nothing is checkable and nothing is checked. unlazy claims **verification** — and a tool arguing *"prove outcomes against a ledger instead of relying on a confident done report"* cannot ship untested without its own thesis indicting it. **§42 split — DISPOSITIONS (replicate):** the `npx skills add` multi-harness install path · the anti-**slop** → anti-**laziness** framing · README-as-product-page polish · overwhelming solo authorship · accepting outside PRs. **ATTENTION (varies):** tests, CI, a threat model, a research protocol, a shared strict parser — every checkable thing. **Sample size N=2: a mechanism, not a law** (§42.4).

**WHAT I ATTACKED AND WHAT HELD** (I ran the checker rather than reading it; exit codes read **unpiped** — my first pass read `head`'s status, **D41**). ⭐⭐⭐ **THE CONSENT BOUNDARY IS GENUINELY FAIL-CLOSED — the best implementation since v244's exact-`YES` gate, and unlike that one it sits on the execution path of the product's primary function.** `--status` on a gate whose CHECK writes a sentinel → **sentinel NOT created**; normal mode on an unapproved oracle → prints the **fully resolved** oracle (CHECK, EXPECT, CWD, SHELL, full PATH) then `NOT RUN: inspect this oracle, then re-run with --approve`, **sentinel NOT created**; `--approve` → writes a sha256-named approval record, executes, `PASS`, **sentinel created**. **The approval binding is exactly as documented, field by field:** `gate-check.mjs:312` `oracle()` returns `{schema, check, expect, cwd, shell, timeoutMs, maxOutputBytes, regexTimeoutMs, platform, path}`; `:328` `signature()` = `sha256(JSON.stringify(oracle))`; `:340` `approvalPath()` = `sha256(absLedger + NUL + gateId + NUL + signature)` ⇒ SECURITY.md:16's claim TRUE. ⭐⭐ **`:337-344` refuses an `UNLAZY_APPROVAL_DIR` INSIDE the repository root — a hostile repo cannot ship its own pre-approvals** — and that hole was closed by an **outside contributor** (`6e23038`, marce). Success conjunction holds: exit 0 + wrong EXPECT → **FAIL**; right EXPECT + exit 3 → **FAIL**; empty `EXPECT:` → **refused, exit 2**. Bare `EXPECT: .*` → **FAIL** (expectations are literal substrings; the opt-in regex form is `/pattern/flags`, `gates.mjs:51`, with a 1000-char cap and a 250 ms worker-isolated timeout).

🔴 **WHERE IT DOES NOT HOLD.** **(1) A gate can lie, trivially** — a gate titled *"every payment migration path is verified against production data"* with `CHECK: node -e "console.log('migration verification passed')"` was certified `PASS`, flipped to `[x]`, and given an EVIDENCE line reading `exit=0; shell=/bin/sh; cwd=…; output=migration verification passed`. **Documented, not hidden** — `references/gates.md:93` states it with unusual candour: *"`G1: invoices reconcile` plus `CHECK: node -e "console.log('ok')"` is syntactically valid and **semantically useless**."* ⇒ ⭐ **unlazy makes incompleteness VISIBLE; it cannot make completeness TRUE.** **(2) 🔴 The stale-green window** — with an approved gate at `[x]`, mutating its `CHECK` by ONE SPACE leaves `--status` → **`ALL MET`, exit 0** and normal mode → **`ALL MET`, exit 0**; only `--reverify` catches it (**UNMET, exit 1**), and when the mutated oracle is unapproved `--reverify` reports UNMET but **does not rewrite the ledger**, so the next `--status` says `ALL MET` again. `--status` is the command `SECURITY.md:11` and `SKILL.md:14-17` tell you to run **FIRST on an inherited ledger**. ⚠️ **NARROWED in the project's favour: declared** at `gates.md:57` (*"does not revalidate old evidence"*) and `orchestration.md:35` (*"**`--status` alone is not re-verification**"*) ⇒ a documented hazard with a documented mitigation. ⭐ The structural tension is real: **you cannot verify evidence without re-executing, and you cannot re-execute what you are refusing to run.** Cheap fix = one field: **bind the EVIDENCE line to a hash of the oracle that produced it**, using the hash `:328` already computes. **(3) 🔴 `EXPECT: /.*/` PASSES** — the regex form accepts a catch-all ⇒ **exactly what open PR #17 offers to lint.** **(4) 🔴 The Stop hook reimplements a platform guard instead of reading it** — `grep "stop_hook_active" scripts/*.mjs tests/*.mjs` = **ZERO OCCURRENCES IN THE ENTIRE REPO**; the hook reads only `payload.cwd` (`:29`) and `payload.session_id` (`:30`) and hardcodes `MAX_BLOCKS = 6` (`:11`) against Anthropic's documented **8-block** cap, whose guide says a hook *"needs to check whether it already triggered a continuation … Parse the `stop_hook_active` field … and exit early if it's `true`."* ⇒ ⭐⭐⭐ **A TOOL WHOSE THESIS IS "CHECK AGAINST AN AUTHORITATIVE EXTERNAL ORACLE" SUBSTITUTED ITS OWN BOOKKEEPING FOR THE PLATFORM'S AUTHORITATIVE SIGNAL** — a precise instance of the error the product exists to prevent. *(In fairness: stricter, 6<8, and demonstrably terminating — I traced the release path.)* ⭐⭐ **AND THE MISSED CONNECTION IS WORTH MORE THAN THE DEFECT:** `stop-hook.mjs:130` tells the model *"Use `ABANDON: <id> <non-blank reason>` only when a gate is **genuinely impossible**"* while Claude Code documents a Stop-hook field **`impossible: true`** meaning exactly that ⇒ **unlazy invented `ABANDON:` for a concept the platform models natively, and the two never meet.** *(Observation only — §43.3: a wiki documents its subject, it does not repair it.)* **(5) Half the product has NO enforcement** — the five declared leaf states `WAITING`/`READY`/`IN-FLIGHT`/`VERIFIED`/`ABANDONED` appear **0× in `scripts/`, 0× in `tests/`, 31× in `references/`+`templates/`** ⇒ **unlazy is TWO PRODUCTS in one repo and only one is enforced**: the gate half is 1,570 lines with 1,290 lines of tests and a boundary I could not break; the orchestration half (five-state machine, rolling-dispatch driver loop, four-tier verification hierarchy) is instructions to a model. **Not hypocrisy — the boundary of the technique, and the docs say so** (`orchestration.md:75` *"**Leaf self-check** … **remains self-certification**"*; `:91` *"Do not call a leaf `VERIFIED` merely because every runnable gate passed"*). CHANGELOG:57's ambition — *"Moved completion enforcement from prose into gate files, runnable checks, evidence"* — **was achieved for the half where completion is a fact about a file, and could not be for the half where completion is a judgement about work.** **(6) 🔴 The link self-check covers 6 of 8 links** — `tests/self-check.mjs:95` `matchAll(/\]\((references\/[^)]+|templates\/[^)]+|scripts\/[^)]+)\)/g)` under a check **named** *"every reference doc the skill links to exists"*; the two invisible links are **both `SECURITY.md`** (`SKILL.md:26`, `:84`) — the threat model, the one doc the skill says to read before executing untrusted code. Both resolve today ⇒ **coverage, not breakage** (the v268 distinction). ⭐⭐⭐ **v269's rule at N=2 in an independent codebase, one ship later: a hand-written prefix list cannot see a link class nobody listed.** **(7) 🔴 The Windows timeout path leaks descendants** — `gate-check.mjs:440-441` `if (process.platform === "win32") child.kill("SIGKILL"); else process.kill(-child.pid, "SIGKILL")` with `detached: process.platform !== "win32"` at `:470`: Unix kills the **group**, Windows only the **immediate process**, and the comment at `:445` names the failure mode (*"A descendant that escaped the shell can otherwise keep inherited pipes open forever"*). ⭐⭐⭐ **CI runs Windows in 3 of 9 jobs and every suite passes — because no test covers timeout-orphaning.** Open **PR #20** fixes it. **(8) The activation metadata names the wrong harness** — `SKILL.md:3`'s `description`, the field an agent reads to decide whether to fire, says *"Use when **Codex** faces a long or multi-part task"*, while `Claude` appears 46× , the only deep integration is the Claude Code Stop hook, and the only agent-metadata file is **`agents/openai.yaml`** (no `agents/claude.yaml`). **No test reads that field.**

PocketBase's own aggregate: Cost $13.91 → $11.02 (**−21%**), Wall-clock 2,044s → 1,762s (**−14%**) ⇒ **1.27× and 1.16×**. The best single figure disclosed anywhere is one task at $2.19 → $0.84 = **2.6×**. **Nothing in 575 lines reaches 4× or 3×.** ⭐⭐⭐ **THE COMMIT CHAIN:** `94a5d80` (2026-07-24, Shrish) added the headline **and** a footnote — *"The 'up to 4× cheaper / 3× faster' figures are the biggest single-task wins from a separate real-repo sweep (**PocketBase, ollama, Excalidraw**)."* · `630cd1d` (2026-08-11, **author `Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>`**, Co-Authored-By Claude Sonnet 5, carrying a `Claude-Session:` URL) changed it to **2×/2.5×** and **deleted that footnote**, message: *"…so the headline **overstated what the adjacent table showed**. Rewords to 2x/2.5x, backed by this table alone."* · `35ac2ae` (2026-08-12, Shrish, **one line, no rationale**) reverted **only the headline**. ⇒ **At HEAD the strong claim stands and its attribution does not, and neither commit produced that state** (`README.md:29` verified — no "biggest single-task wins" sentence). ⭐⭐ **And the sweep was never published:** scanning **all 402 commits**, a `### Excalidraw` or `### ollama` heading has **NEVER existed (0/402)**; the string "Excalidraw" appears in **exactly 2 commits** — the one that added the footnote and the one that deleted it. **THE LADDER: v270 no gate fires on a claim true when written · v271 a gate's scope is inherited from where it lives · v272 a gate holds when something else already requires it · v273 a check is only as permanent as the place you put it · v274 neither a gate nor a habit reaches a claim stored outside the repository · v275 A CHECK THAT REACHES THE CLAIM, IS CORRECT, AND IS APPLIED CAN STILL BE REVERTED BY SOMEONE WITH THE STANDING TO DO IT.**

**⚠️ BUT THE RESEARCH ITSELF IS HONEST, AND THAT MUST BE SAID.** **No benchmark artifacts exist** — `git ls-files | grep -iE "bench|swe|eval|result"` is **EMPTY**; `git grep -il "swe-bench"` returns **README.md only**. Yet the detail sections are markedly more disciplined than the hero: the SWE-bench write-up states **"50 instances"** in its own body, names the model (Claude Sonnet 5) and grader (**official `swebench` 4.1.0**, native x86_64), declares its own subsetting (*"over the instances **both arms resolved**"*), **names the self-measurement problem out loud** (*"The sweep above is our harness measuring our mechanism. So we ran the industry-standard one too"*), uses a cache-aware cost model (reads ≈0.1×), and **reports a null result against itself** — in the 162-run sweep correctness is **93% vs 93% (equal)**. ⇒ **The composite HERO TABLE is the defect, not the research:** it takes the efficiency rows (+46%/+42%/+60%) from the experiment where **correctness was flat**, and the correctness row (54%→66%) from the experiment whose efficiency numbers were **roughly half as good** (+25%/+23%/+32%). The footnote says which is which; the table does not.

**⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE TELEMETRY CONTRACT — an exceptional mechanism, an ungated document.** `TELEMETRY.md:8-13`: *"This document is the complete, authoritative contract: **if an event or property is not listed here, graft does not send it** … enforces this list as a hard allowlist … **The code and this file are kept in lockstep**, and because the repo is open source you can verify that yourself."* **The mechanism is the best-tested privacy surface in the corpus**: `test/telemetry-contract.test.ts` (171 lines) feeds a realistic payload `/Users/someone/secret/repo/src/auth.ts` and asserts **`'path' in ev.properties === false`** *and* **`JSON.stringify(ev).includes('secret') === false`**; drops raw numbers under legal keys (every count bucketed so it cannot fingerprint a repo); rejects prototype keys as both event and property names; `langsValue` drops `'../../etc/passwd'` and `'src/secret project/auth.ts'`; `errorCode` maps to a fixed enum and **never returns the message**. **⭐ I RAN IT: 55 tests, 55 PASS, 0 fail, 115ms** (telemetry contract + notice + gate + claude-settings-merge + shim-template + savings). It honours **`DO_NOT_TRACK`** and never notices in CI (*"CI gets no notice — there is no one there to read a disclosure"*). Telemetry is **opt-out, on by default** — established by an executed test named *"never chosen means on — the documented default."* 🔴 **BUT NOTHING READS `TELEMETRY.md`**: a full-extent grep across every `.ts`/`.mjs`/`.cjs`/`.yml` in the tree returns **7 hits — 5 comments, 1 user-facing string, 1 URL. Zero reads.** The test pins the event set against **a list typed a third time inside the test file** (`assert.deepEqual(Object.keys(EVENTS).sort(), [six literals])`), and `src/telemetry/contract.ts:3-5` states the rule as an instruction to a **human**: *"one that is not in `TELEMETRY.md` **must not be added** here."* ⇒ **Three copies — the published document, the code, and the test — and the gate compares copy 2 to copy 3; the authoritative copy is unchecked.** All three agree today (six events, verified). ⭐⭐ **The sharpest part: this codebase demonstrably knows how to assert on markdown** — `test/hosts-init.test.ts:31` asserts `GEMINI.md` includes `'graft ask'`; `covers.test.ts`, `graph-posix-paths.test.ts` and `context.test.ts` all read generated `.md`. **The capability is aimed at every markdown file graft WRITES and at none of the markdown files graft PUBLISHES ABOUT ITSELF.** That is **v250's rule** — *a gate's aim, not its quality, decides what rots* — reached independently.

**⭐⭐⭐ THE `pull_request_target` WORKFLOW — stated AND obeyed (D34 tested).** `blast-pages.yml` publishes a per-PR viewer to GitHub Pages under **`pull_request_target`** with **`contents: write` + `pull-requests: write`**. Its header (`:6-13`) names the hazard: *"That choice carries the standard hazard: this workflow runs with the BASE repo's permissions while the PR's code is attacker-controlled on a fork. So it checks out the base ref for the tooling, builds the CLI from the BASE commit, and **only ever reads the PR's files as data — never runs a script from the PR (no `npm ci` on the PR's package.json, no postinstall)**."* **I tested the predicate against the file:** `:64-67` checkout `path: base`, **no `ref:`**, `persist-credentials: false` ✅ · `:73-75` **the only `npm` invocation in the file**, `working-directory: base` ✅ · `:84-90` `ref: refs/pull/N/merge`, `path: pr`, credential-less, `allow-unsafe-pr-checkout: true` ✅ · `:103-104` the graph build runs in `pr` with a binary built in `base` ✅. **The invariant holds absolutely.** ⭐ `:79-83` carries the best sentence in the file — the override flag *"refuses a fork's PR ref … unless the workflow opts in — **the review that opt-in asks for is the header of this file**."* **A direct cross-author N=2 of v273's finding, one ship later, in an unrelated codebase.** **ZERO `paths:` filters across all six workflows** — unlike v271, the gate's *scope* is right; CI simply has nothing to say about the README because no test reads it.

🔴 **WHERE IT DOES NOT HOLD.** **(1) The rename `context-graph-engine` → `Graft` is unfinished in 7 places / 5 files:** `package.json:17,19,21` (repository/homepage/bugs) · `README.md:563` (**the literal `git clone` command under `## Development`**) · `src/telemetry/notice.ts:22` (`TELEMETRY_DOC_URL` — **the privacy-policy link shown to users**) · `.claude/helpers/graft-hooks.cjs:7` and `graft-statusline.cjs:7`, both carrying `BAKED = "/Users/shrishdwivedi/Documents/Context graphs/context-graph-engine/dist/claude"` — **the author's own laptop path, committed to a public repo**. ⭐ That last is better than it looks: `src/claude/shim-template.ts` shows the `.cjs` helpers are **generated by `graft init`** with the local package path baked in, resolving through four candidates so a stranger's machine falls through harmlessly. `.gitignore` reasons about exactly this line — ignoring `.claude/settings.json` as *"regenerated per machine … never shared"* while stating *"the hook helpers/skills alongside them stay tracked."* **The rule was written and correct in intent; its population was typed by hand and one member was misclassified.** **(2) Twelve stale `.context/` doc-comments across seven source files**, describing an output directory the product abandoned (it writes `graft/`) — and **two are contradictory**: `src/context/check.ts:2` *"is the **committed** `.context/` graph still in sync…"* and `src/engine.ts:70` *"whether the **committed** `.context/` markdown graph is in sync"* — while the product's central design is that the graph is **never committed** (`.gitignore`, the README, and a remote branch literally named `docs/graft-cache-not-committed`). ⭐ **The pivot reached the README, the `.gitignore`, the `.ignore`, the SKILL and the CLI; it did not reach the doc-comments inside the files that implement it** — which is the prose an agent reads when it opens the source, i.e. precisely what Graft exists to replace. *(That its own generated graph would inherit the error is a mechanism I state and did NOT measure — building needs an API key and native bindings I could not compile.)* **(3) Raw source → your LLM with no secret-scanning:** `src/context/build.ts:181` `await opts.summarizer.summarize(code, { path: rel })`; in *your* repo `dist/cli.js` is your build output, now pre-approved to run unprompted with arbitrary arguments. **(5) Global writes for two hosts:** project-local for Claude Code (**a real improvement on v273**, which wrote the global `~/.claude/settings.json`), but Codex/Antigravity write `~/.codex/hooks.json` (**a hook firing in every repo**), `~/.codex/config.toml`, `~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json`, `~/.gemini/skills/graft/SKILL.md`. ✅ Escape hatches exist and are documented: `--dry-run` (`cli.ts:838`), `--no-global` (`:840`), `--agents` (`:832`). **(6) Release bookkeeping drifts both ways:** 6 tags vs 9 CHANGELOG versions — **`v0.7.1` and `v0.12.1` have no CHANGELOG entry**; ✅ **SOURCE VERIFIED** — two clones, `diff -rq` clean **both** directions, HEAD `32df94d38a0c39b4c94206966e44f7273e151fca`. **`git rev-list --count`: 1,811 commits / 2,700 all-refs · TWO roots (`aff34717` + `efc0cd39`, both 2025-01-02) · 312 merges · 54 tags · 5,867 files · 2025-01-02 → 2026-08-24 (latest commit: yesterday).** Lines: **YAML 4,266 files / 115,049** · Python 641 / 82,689 · Markdown 250 / 38,140 · TSX 104 / 27,515 · Go 111 / 25,931. **47 author emails on HEAD** (48 across all refs — the extra is `cursoragent@cursor.com`); `zhuque@tencent.com` = 872 (48%); **1,003 Tencent vs 808 outside (45%), and 312 merges ⇒ outside contribution is genuinely merged**. **`noreply@anthropic.com` 0.** Tests: **228 Go test functions (33 files) + 121 Python test functions (17 files) = 349.**

**⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE SHIP'S RULE: THE RELIABILITY OF A NUMBER IS PREDICTED BY ITS AUDIENCE, NOT BY THE TEAM'S COMPETENCE — the same people apply two standards in one repository, and the variable is who is reading.** Three numbers, one repo: **(1)** `Research/deepseek-harness-security-assessment/` — **14,560 runs**, **TWO independent evaluators reported side by side *including where they disagree*** (`J_R` deterministic 5.6%/2.0% vs `J_L` semantic 5.3%/7.3%), a written sanitization policy (*"one row per completed run without prompts, generated model text, tool arguments, internal paths, credentials"*), a **re-runnable** aggregation script, and slices published that make its own defences look worse (**Skills channel 16.0%**, Hidden-Unicode 25.5%) — *written for peers who will re-run it*. **(2)** `CHANGELOG` v4.5.0: *"**130 components, 1888 rules**"* — `git ls-tree -r --name-only v4.5.0 -- data/fingerprints | wc -l` → **130**; `-- data/vuln` → **1888**. **Both exact.** **(3)** `CHANGELOG` v4.5.2 (three weeks later): *"**2000+ CVE rules**"* — at that tag `data/vuln` = **1,916**, `data/vuln_en` = 1,914, **distinct CVEs = 1,662**. **No honest population reaches 2000+**; the only one that does is the **bilingual double-count** (3,830) — **D23 exactly**. At HEAD (7 days on) `data/vuln` = 2,014, so the claim became true *by being outrun*; on distinct CVEs (1,767) it is still false. **⭐⭐⭐ AND THE `+` IS THE TELL:** measured at the very commit that wrote it (`58ba98a8`, 2026-03-20), `CLAUDE.md` says `data/eval` **"13+"** (was 13 ✅ exact), `data/vuln` **"589+"** (was 640 ✅ true), and `data/fingerprints` **"60+"** — **the tree held 51. False the day it was typed.** Three counts, one document, one day; a reader cannot tell them apart. ⇒ **a floor is the form a number takes when nobody derived it.** And the claims needing a *judgment about population* are the wrong ones: *"3 official skills"* (**4** dirs at that tag) · *"10 skills total"* (**4** dirs; the 10 are agent-scan **detection types**).

**⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE HEADLINE — CI RUNS 1 OF 349 TESTS (0.29%), AND THE GATE IS AIMED AT THE DATA.** Exactly **three** workflows; two fire only on a version tag. The third, `yaml-lint.yml`, is `push`+`pull_request` **`paths: ['data/**', 'cmd/yamlcheck/**']`**, and `:32` runs **`go test ./cmd/yamlcheck`** — **the only test invocation anywhere in the repository** (full-extent grep over `*.yml`/`*.sh`/`*.json`/`*.toml`/Makefile; positive control `go build` = 3 hits) — and that package holds **exactly one test function**, `TestFindCaseInsensitivePathCollisions`. `pytest` is declared in three `pyproject.toml` files and invoked by **no** workflow. The never-run packages include **`common/fingerprints`** (the matching engine), **`pkg/vulstruct`** (the CVE version-range DSL) and **`internal/mcp`** — *the code that decides whether a real CVE is reported*. **The mistake is not laziness: they wrote 349 tests. The one job that runs a test runner was built to serve the DATA pipeline and inherited its scope.** Editing `common/runner/runner.go`, `README.md`, `CHANGELOG.md` or `docker-compose.yml` triggers **zero CI**.

**⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE TRUST MODEL THAT WAS BORN INCOMPLETE.** `SECURITY.md` is one of the better security documents in the corpus — a real threat model (`:70-73`: *"LLM API responses … are treated as untrusted content — **the scan engine processes them, not the host OS**"*), per-mode deployment boundaries (`:64-66`), and an explicit out-of-scope list; the code obeys it (`cmd/cli/cmd/webserver.go:65` defaults `127.0.0.1:8088`), and **`README.md:149` discloses the gap prominently under the install command**: *"It currently lacks an authentication mechanism and should not be deployed on public networks."* 🔴 **But `docker-compose.yml:48-51` gives the agent container — the one running the Python scanners on untrusted input — `cap_add: SYS_ADMIN` + `security_opt: seccomp:unconfined`, and SECURITY.md mentions them ZERO times** (full-extent grep `SYS_ADMIN|seccomp|unconfined|capabilit` = 0; positive control "docker" = 2). **Subject.** `MeteorNOX/DeepSeek-Balance-Whale-Widget`, npm **`dsh-whale-widget` v0.2.10**, MIT — 「DSH Web 界面右下角的 DeepSeek 余额小鲸鱼挂件」. A **DeepSeek Harness bundle plugin** that parks a cartoon whale in the corner of the harness's web GUI showing **account balance**, **today's spend**, and **what the turn that just ended cost**. Host plugin `lib/index.js` (2,023 lines, ESM, **zero dependencies**) registers **8 routes** on the harness's own web server, injects a browser widget via `tapIndex`, and listens to `session/event` to meter per-turn cost from the model's real usage counts. Two spend modes: **小鲸鱼记账** (default — poll the balance, add every decrease; no usage API, no token counting) and **实时·令牌** (the platform usage endpoint converted to money by a built-in peak/valley price table). Author **pseudonymous**, NOT Anthropic. **Phase 0.9: (a) FAIL · (b) STRONG ⚠️MODERATE-reviewable · (c) STRONG · (d) STRONG.**

✅ **SOURCE VERIFIED** — two clones, `diff -rq` clean **both** directions, HEAD `4448c61db7d180c4c307aa3fa734db7c8507658d`. **15 tracked files · `rev-list --count HEAD` 30 · `--all` 49 · 1 root (`306e660`) · 9 merges · 9 tags · 2026-08-20 → 2026-08-25 (5 days) · 4 author emails** (20 owner / 6 方便面 / 2 under-the-ocean / 2 soursweetlemon; PR #26 from `xiaolinnnnnnn`; PR numbers to **#46**, 13 distinct issue refs). ⚠️ **No network** (npm contents, GitHub's rendered release list, world-first priority all UNVERIFIED); `python3` SIGKILLed (D41); **neither product installed or run.**

**⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE SHIP'S RULE: every failure in this repository sits on a boundary it does not own — and every success sits inside one it does.** Inside its walls: a never-throw route contract, retry-with-stale-fallback, in-flight de-duplication, per-session cost bucketing that anticipates **subagent parallelism**, an explicit memory-leak disposer, an 8 KB body cap, **no XSS path in 2,000 hand-written framework-free lines**, and price rules **versioned by date**. ## v278 x64dbg-mcp-server (2026-08-25) — `duty1g/x64dbg-mcp-server`

*"MCP-powered agentic reverse engineering for x64dbg."* A **native x64dbg plugin** — a `.dp64`/`.dp32` DLL loaded into the debugger's own address space — running an HTTP server that exposes **80 MCP tools** so a coding agent can drive a live Windows debugging session: breakpoints, single-stepping, process memory read **and patch**, disassembly, call stacks, module dumping, OEP detection on packed binaries. Written in **Zig**, **zero dependencies**, cross-compiling to x86 and x86-64 from any host, resolving every x64dbg SDK symbol at runtime via `GetProcAddress`. MIT. Author **`duty1g`** (`dzc0d3r@hotmail.com`) — a **pseudonymous** individual with a disclosed Red-Team/RE presence (`duty1g.online`, `@duty_1g`), **NOT Anthropic** (§41; #19 19a).

The shared state is the ring buffer at `mcp_server.zig:87-90` (`pending_events`/`pending_event_lens`/`pending_head`/`pending_count`): **producer = x64dbg's own debugger thread** via `main.zig:349,375,423,428,433,438` → `notifyEvent` → `pendingPush` (`:194-195`); **consumers = every HTTP client thread** via `pendingDrain`/`pendingDrainToBuffer`. A raced `pending_count -= 1` **underflows a `usize`** — and the README's own build command is `ReleaseSafe` (`:229`), where that is **checked and panics, inside x64dbg**, killing the analyst's session. ⚠️ The queue also **silently drops the oldest event** at 16 (`:120-123`) while `SKILL.md:23` says *"Always read these"*.

No linter, no formatter, no CI, no release workflow, no provenance.** ⇒ **6,396 lines of Zig, inside a debugger's address space, parsing network input, granting remote callers arbitrary memory write — and the only thing that verifies any of it is `zig build` succeeding.** *More extreme than v276, which at least had 349 tests and wired one.*

**✅ WHAT IS GENUINELY CORRECT.** Token generation is **sound crypto** — `config.zig:139` declares `SystemFunction036`, the real `advapi32` export name for **RtlGenRandom**, the Windows CSPRNG; `generateToken` (`:141-149`) takes 16 bytes → 32 hex = **128 bits** ⚠️ (*I grepped for `RtlGenRandom`, got zero hits, and nearly recorded the commit message as unsupported — the commit message was accurate and I was not*). Auth now **fails closed** (`:460`). **No JSON injection** — `json.zig:76-77` escapes `"` and `\` **first**, so a hostile binary cannot break out of a string. **No buffer overflow** — `wsRecv` (`:440-455`) is structurally bounded into a fixed `[65536]u8` with `@min` clamping (oversized requests are silently *truncated*, a correctness not a safety issue). Hygiene: **zero `catch unreachable`, zero `catch {}`, zero bare `unreachable`, one `@panic`**, 52 × `catch return` (a coherent *never take down the host* discipline); `defer parsed.deinit()` at `:523` and `:614` ⇒ **no leak** (a fleet claim refuted). **MCP-conformant `readOnlyHint`/`openWorldHint` on all 80 tools** (`:715`). **`bridge.zig:1-2` credits the x64dbg SDK header by URL.** ⭐ **`isMcpToolName`** is a guard built against a *real observed LLM failure mode* — the model passing tool names to `ExecuteDebuggerCommand` — with `SKILL.md`'s "Common Mistakes" table doing the same job in prose: **the same failure addressed in prose AND in code.**

**⚠️ AND THE INSTRUCTION THAT UNDERCUTS THE ANNOTATIONS.** `mcp_server.zig:715` ships the per-tool mutation hints; **`:692`, twenty-three lines earlier in the same function, tells the model 「Never wait for user confirmation — monitor actively」** (and rule 4: *"NEVER go idle or ask the user…"*). Read charitably these are **liveness** rules about not idling while polling — almost certainly the intent — but they are unqualified CRITICAL RULES delivered to a model holding **44 mutating tools**. ⭐ **He classified all 80 tools correctly (enumerated) and then wrote one summary sentence that reads across the whole surface. The same pattern again.**

**⭐⭐⭐⭐ THE HAZARD NOBODY DOCUMENTS.** Even with perfect escaping, **the content of an analysed binary flows into the analyst's agent context** — `GetStrings` on a malware sample faithfully delivers whatever that sample's author wrote, including text shaped like instructions. The disclaimer (`README.md:272-278`) covers legal misuse and network exposure; neither it nor `SKILL.md` mentions that **the artifact under analysis is hostile input to the agent doing the analysis.** For an agentic RE tool that is *the* hazard, and it is unaddressed. ⚠️ Separately, `json.zig:72-90` escapes only five characters, so **29 of 32 control bytes and invalid UTF-8 pass through raw** ⇒ malformed JSON from hostile binary content — **not an injection**, a denied tool call.

**🟡 PRECISE, NOT INFLATED.** `std.mem.eql` is **not constant-time** (`:460`) but runs only after a length check, on a 128-bit token over HTTP with network jitter ⇒ **low**. **`Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *`** on every response (`:845`) and `OPTIONS` returns 204 **before** the auth block (`:447-451`) — that is *correct* CORS (a preflight cannot carry `Authorization`); the real consequence is that **any web page can fingerprint the server** without a token ⇒ **modest**. `DumpMemory`/`DumpModule` do **not** constrain `filePath` (`tools.zig:2832-2847`, interpolated into `savedata "{s}", …`, so a `"` breaks the quoting) — **but this is NO privilege escalation**, since the same authenticated caller already holds `ExecuteDebuggerCommand`. `isMcpToolName` guards **28 of 80** — introduced fresh at `eb63792`, all 28 names real ⇒ a deliberate judgment sample, **not drift**. ⚠️ `SKILL.md` has **no YAML frontmatter** — Anthropic's Agent Skill *filename* without Anthropic's Agent Skill *format*; a loader would not register it. ⚠️ **Licence, facts only:** x64dbg is GPLv3, this is MIT, it re-declares SDK constants/structs in Zig and resolves every symbol at **runtime** via `GetProcAddress` rather than linking; no `NOTICE`, no compatibility statement — **stated as facts, no legal conclusion**. ⚠️ `bridge.zig:327` is the single `@panic`, on a missing bridge symbol — **v277's rule appearing here once: a failure on a boundary he does not own** (x64dbg's export table), which he cannot test because it depends on the user's x64dbg build.
